README known-limitations text and actual parser tree can differ; no universal 'any SID' capability claim. ci.yml still has continue-on-error:true on test step; latest commit reports 3040 passed/3 failed/86 skipped on corpus-less clone. Green CI cannot be treated as proof of a clean test suite. SID corpus/third-party binaries in tree retain separate rights.

decisions.title: sid-analyzer — SID structure, MIDI and project exporter
decisions.reason: Accepted at the reviewed scope. Experimental Rust SID structure/tracing/MIDI/Pertylizer exporter with generic mos6502 execution. It has no playback UI or complete mixed SID-to-WAV renderer; exports are approximations. RSID export refused by default without unreliable override; incomplete CIA/interrupt hosting. Secondary-SID capture available but most exports primary-chip-only; MUS/STR emulation unsupported. MIDI loses sub-frame timing; digi WAV is separate PCM, not full mixed SID rendering. No local build/fixtures run; pinned toolchain/dependency availability not independently checked.

decisions.title: Commodore Commander — Theia development IDE
decisions.reason: Accepted at the reviewed scope. Theia/Electron desktop development IDE with Kick Assembler language support, VICE DAP debugging and graphics/SIDScore tools. Generic machine profiles are not proof of equal feature support on every model. No build or package smoke test performed. README says macOS bundle ad-hoc signed by default; release notarisation remains manual. IDE includes third-party tooling/ROM-derived symbol material; project licence is not a blanket rights statement.

decisions.title: MW2MID — Martin Walker Game Boy/Game Gear music converter
decisions.reason: Accepted at the reviewed scope. Reverse-engineered music-sequence extractor/converter for Martin Walker Game Boy/Game Gear drivers. C64 ancestry is upstream speculation; GBS/SGC and other-console/computer formats are TODO. No Makefile/build instructions; compilation not established. Pitch bend/portamento incomplete and Speedball 2 desynchronisation known. GBS/SGC, SNES/Mega Drive and computer-driver support are TODO, not supported targets. Exact owner spelling is turboboy215, correcting handoff typo.

decisions.title: Reginald and the She Vampires — native CPC remake and sequel
decisions.reason: Native C remake/reboot and sequel of the named 1987 game. The substantial game modules implement movement, monsters, menus, sarcophagi, levels, victory and defeat. This is a reimplementation, not an established decompilation or byte-exact reconstruction. Released upstream as version 1.1.1; native CPC remake/reboot and sequel, not independently built or played. README requires two different Arnaud6128/CPCTelera branches: intro uses development 1.5/SDCC 3.6, main uses CPCTelera-next/SDCC 4.5. No compile, gameplay or real-machine validation here. GPL-2.0-or-later in game source; top-level GPL-2.0 license detected. Original game identity and any inherited assets retain separate provenance; redistribution clearance was not established.

decisions.title: Space Hockey — BASIC-to-Z80 CPC rewrite
decisions.reason: Native assembly rewrite of David Hay’s Amstrad Action issue 42 Locomotive BASIC type-in. The BASIC source is retained and the new assembly contains the gameplay loop, player collision and ball logic; this is neither an emulator wrapper nor an inferred binary decompilation. Upstream calls the Z80 rewrite fully playable and compiled with RASM; no local build or gameplay verification. RASM build command is documented. Existing BIN/CDT/DSK files are evidence of supplied artifacts, not independent build or runtime verification. WINAPE assembler needs adjustments. Source headers specify GPL-2.0-or-later, while top-level LICENSE is GNU Library GPL v2. Preserve this mismatch instead of reporting a single unqualified license. Original BASIC type-in is credited separately.

decisions.title: Red Planet — native CPC464 action-adventure
decisions.reason: Original/homebrew CPC game built on Mojon Twins MK1/la Churrera. Custom configuration, gameplay, maps, scripts and assets are present. This does not establish a reconstruction of another legacy binary or original authorship of the inherited engine. Released native CPC464 action-adventure source with English and Spanish artifacts; not independently built or played. Windows batch pipeline expects z88dk zcc, cpcrslib and bundled conversion tools. Supplied binaries and upstream release status were not compiled or played here. README says software is GPL v2, but cover artwork by Masterklown is explicitly excluded and requires separate permission. Do not treat the cover as GPL.

decisions.title: Sorcerers — native 64K CPC464 game
decisions.reason: Native homebrew potion/adventure game built with CPCtelera. Substantial main.c implements game states, rendering, input and end-game logic. The bundled Android APK is not evidence of an independently sourced Android reimplementation. Released one/two-player 64K CPC464 game source; native CPC build and gameplay not independently tested. Requires CPCtelera v1.5 development branch. Android APK is also present but is not a separately accepted port; only native CPC source is accepted. No build/runtime tests performed. Top-level license and README describe GPL v3/GPL, but main.c header says LGPL v3-or-later; retain the inconsistency. Castle artwork is adapted from Freepik with attribution terms.

decisions.title: Galaga CPC — native Z80 arcade remake
decisions.reason: Native Z80 reimplementation of Galaga, using a CPC-specific overscan architecture. Actual enemies, bullets, stages, collisions, audio, high scores and capture/rescue behavior are implemented. No original arcade CPU execution or disassembly-derived port is established. Substantial native CPC clone with tractor-beam, stages and alternate-player logic; build and arcade parity unverified. Build.bat hard-codes G:\Amstrad\rasm_w64.exe and uses WSL/iDSK and Python. Cassette highscores are not persisted. No independent build, playback, gameplay-parity or real-hardware test. No top-level license detected. Galaga-related artwork/name/data provenance and redistribution rights remain unverified.

decisions.title: Habitat — partial CPC6128 colony simulation
decisions.reason: Planetbase-inspired native homebrew colony simulation with its own Z80 economy, jobs, routing, construction, sound, saves and world generation. Inspiration does not establish a Planetbase source port or reconstruction. Partial native colony simulation: upstream reports it runs, but economy, balance, rendering and asset completeness remain unresolved. Keep partial status. RASM/iDSK/headless cpcemu paths are author-local defaults; assets are generated in related CPCArt. Upstream test claims are not independent verification. Complete balanced gameplay and finished assets are not established. No top-level license detected. Separate generated art repository and Planetbase inspiration need provenance care; no asset clearance established.

decisions.title: GearSF7000 — SG-1000 / SC-3000 emulator and debugger
decisions.reason: Generic whole-machine SG-1000/SC-3000 emulator and debugger, not a game-specific emulation wrapper. CPU, memory, VDP, audio, keyboard and SF-7000 disk/timing modules are implemented. SP-400 printer support is explicitly planned, not implemented. Substantial desktop Sega machine/peripheral emulator; Windows package is described upstream as ready to run, with fidelity unverified here. C++20/SDL3 desktop build and GTK3 Linux/BSD dependency. No local compile or compatibility tests. SP-400 support is explicitly planned. Fidelity, supplied packages and cross-platform behavior remain upstream claims. README/top-level license state AGPL v3; core source retains GPL v3-or-later headers, and imported components have their own notices. Do not flatten this into a license for ROMs or media.

decisions.title: CP/M 2.2 / P2DOS — SC-3000 disk-system adaptation
decisions.reason: Adaptation/preservation of historical CP/M-compatible P2DOS with SC-3000-specific BIOS, boot loader and disk I/O. BIOS jump table, keyboard, console, FDC reads, warm boot and CCP loading are source-backed. This is not original authorship of the entire OS. SC-3000 BIOS, P2DOS/CCP sources and disk image preserved; bootability and overall compatibility unverified. Requires SC-3000 with suitable disk expansion/SF-7000 rather than stock bare hardware. Brief README does not establish overall compatibility; no OS boot or build was performed. No repository-wide license found. P2DOS source includes explicit noncommercial-use restrictions and author permission for commercial use; do not characterize it as unrestricted public domain.

decisions.title: SF-7000 IPL — annotated SC-3000 expansion firmware
decisions.reason: Firmware preservation/reconstruction for the SC-3000 SF-7000 disk expansion: annotated Z80 entry points implement boot, disk commands, keyboard/video, utility and self-test behavior. README does not establish an official Sega source release or the exact reverse-engineering method. Annotated IPL firmware reconstruction and WLA-DX recipe present; official-source provenance, byte match and boot remain unverified. No byte-identical ROM reconstruction or boot test performed. SF-7000 is retained as hardware-expansion detail under SC-3000 rather than a new standalone platform. No project-wide license detected; bundled WLA-DX licensing does not establish rights to Sega firmware/ROM/font contents.

decisions.title: ZVM Sega — partial Z-machine interpreter for SD-1000-expanded SC-3000
decisions.reason: Reusable Infocom Z-machine v3 interpreter, with opcode/operand decoding, text/dictionary/object/stack modules and story banks. This is a language virtual machine, not emulation of an original physical game CPU and not a game-specific CPU-emulation execution path. Partial game-agnostic Z-machine v3 runtime requiring SD-1000-style 16 KiB unmirrored RAM; stock Sega memory layouts are unsupported. Does not run correctly on stock SG-1000/SC-3000 or standard Master System RAM layouts. README-equivalent hardware document contains both updated local patched-emulator claims and older unverified statements; no verified supported runtime here. Memory output stream is unimplemented, window handling is minimal, save/restore are stubs. Keep partial status and label SC-3000 with SD-1000 caveat. No top-level project license detected. SGlib has its own license; bundled Mini-Zork story and generated bank source do not establish permission for arbitrary redistribution.

decisions.title: gfx2sg — SG-1000 graphics converter for SGlib
decisions.reason: Modern host-side graphics conversion tool producing background/sprite data for SGlib/TMS9918. Actual palette/tile conversion and adapted ZX7 compression are implemented. It is neither native SG-1000 executable code nor an emulator or legacy game reconstruction. Implemented Python/Pillow TMS9918 tile/palette converter with documented omissions and preview issue; not executed here. No independent conversion test. README warns of preview transparency issue and lacks resizing, color reduction, dithering and duplicate-tile tilemap support. Modern Python is needed by current syntax/cache usage. Top-level LICENSE is BSD-2-Clause; source comments say the rest is BSD-3-Clause and preserve Einar Saukas’s three-condition ZX7 notice. Record mixed/inconsistent notices instead of flattening.

decisions.title: Wonder Boy — Emulicious-generated Master System disassembly
decisions.reason: Source-level preservation of the 1986 Master System game through explicitly Emulicious-generated disassembly. Approximately 344 KB of assembly, bank maps and extracted DAT chunks are present. Mechanical/anonymous labels must not be presented as a fully understood hand-annotated reconstruction, modern remake or generative-AI output. Mostly mechanical disassembly with ROM data and WLA-DX build recipe; semantic annotation, execution and byte identity unverified. Mostly mechanical/anonymous labels; semantic annotation and byte-identical output were not verified. Shell script begins with Windows-style @echo off and assumes an author-local Emulicious jar path; no build executed. Repository supplies GPL-3.0 text, but original Wonder Boy ROM/data rights are separate and not established by that file. output.sms and extracted data are included.

decisions.title: Qasteroids — native Atari STFM asteroid-game port
decisions.reason: Native port/adaptation of a Lovable-based asteroid-action game, with portable fixed-point C game logic and ST-specific planar video, 68000 acceleration, IKBD input and YM2149 sound. It is not a reconstruction of original Atari arcade ROM logic or a game-specific emulation wrapper. Substantial native 68000 port with upstream artifact/test claims; sustained gameplay validation is still required. Target is 1 MB Atari 1040 STFM/TOS low resolution. Upstream benchmark and test results are not independently reproduced; README says sustained real-machine/emulator play testing is still needed. No build or execution performed. No top-level license detected. Includes historical reference source zip and a file named 104_se.img despite README saying ROMs are not bundled; that file was not opened or identified, so redistribution assumptions remain unresolved.

decisions.title: Duke Nukem Episode 1 — FreeNukum Atari ST port
decisions.reason: Approved new repository-root addition with substantive primary implementation evidence. Native Atari port of the FreeNukum C reimplementation with its own planar renderer, YM2149 sound backend and expanded Duke Nukem Episode 1 game logic. Hatari is a test host, not an embedded guest-CPU execution path. Upstream calls Episode 1 feature complete and reports clean builds and playable ST output; optional features remain absent and 1 MB mode is experimental.

decisions.title: RoadBlasters — Atari STE enhancement patches
decisions.reason: Approved new repository-root addition with substantive primary implementation evidence. Address-specific native 68000 overlays replace road/background rendering and patch the VBL vector to use STE Blitter hardware. This is partial reverse engineering and enhancement of an existing executable, not a complete disassembly or standalone remake. Early STE patch prototype for the original ST executable; upstream confirms the Linux Makefile, but there is no standalone runnable disk image.

decisions.title: Player Manager — Amiga save editor and analytics toolkit
decisions.reason: Approved new repository-root addition with substantive primary implementation evidence. Modern Python research/editor tooling for the original Amiga Player Manager save-disk format. The custom file-table parser, byte workbench, tactic editor and analytics are concrete tools; this does not reconstruct or run the football game engine. Released v2.6.1 cross-platform save editor; upstream reports working GUI/CLI, with heuristic and English-name features still beta.

decisions.title: Bloodwych ZX Spectrum — level editor and renderer research
decisions.reason: Approved new repository-root addition with substantive primary implementation evidence. Modern browser level editor and ZX-specific reverse-engineering/reconstruction tooling. Byte-preserving sessions and semantic edits target Level TZX/TAP; source-driven renderer work reconstructs a subsystem but does not execute a full Bloodwych game. Upstream-documented level-editor milestone with a source-driven partial first-person renderer; not a playable game engine or complete game editor.

decisions.title: The Settlers — GameMaker/Freeserf recreation
decisions.reason: Approved new repository-root addition with substantive primary implementation evidence. A direct GML port of Freeserf simulation with a GameMaker renderer, original Amiga assets, lockstep networking and its own UI/quality-of-life changes. Native game-state routines replace the legacy engine; no Amiga CPU interpreter was found in the inspected execution path. Upstream-reported playable GameMaker recreation with native GML simulation and networking; strategic fighting AI and intro are unported.

decisions.title: Netwalk — Amstrad CPC native puzzle game
decisions.reason: Approved new repository-root addition with substantive primary implementation evidence. A new native Z80 implementation of the Netwalk puzzle, with growing-tree maze generation, animated tile rotation, connectivity/completion logic, menus and timer. It is homebrew game code rather than a recovered commercial Netwalk binary. Upstream publishes a playable CPC puzzle game; loading screen, high scores, sound effects and original music remain unfinished.

decisions.title: Color Flood — Amstrad CPC territory puzzle game
decisions.reason: Approved new repository-root addition with substantive primary implementation evidence. Original native CPC homebrew implementing a two-to-four-player flood-fill territory game, inspired by 7 Colors and related games. The actual C board model and turn/podium flow establish a substantive game; no commercial executable disassembly is claimed. Released CPC homebrew puzzle game with build maintenance through 2024; initialization/fairness TODOs remain.

decisions.title: Defender of the Crown — CPC enhancement source preservation
decisions.reason: Approved new repository-root addition with substantive primary implementation evidence. One original-game/enhancement source lineage: DoTC.asm credits B. Rive (1988) and Megachur optimization/improvement (2012), with preserved older ASM and newer DoTC modules. It is not presented as a new complete remake or two independent games. Preserved original/2012 enhancement sources with incomplete routines and absent external includes; repository-only reproducibility is unestablished.

decisions.title: Downland — native C reconstruction and console ports
decisions.reason: Approved new repository-root addition with substantive primary implementation evidence. Native C/C++ game logic derived from Downland_RE, with a separate game_8bit implementation and platform layers. player.c implements physics, hazards, pickups, doors and game flow rather than interpreting original 6809 instructions. The research repository is a predecessor, not a second C port. Alpha native reconstruction with upstream-playable ports; close rather than exact fidelity, original ROM required, and SG-1000 physical banking unverified.

decisions.title: Fairlight I / II — Godot recreation
decisions.reason: Approved new repository-root addition with substantive primary implementation evidence. An independent from-scratch Godot 4.5 recreation with native GDScript movement, gravity, combat, inventory and room transitions. Both Fairlight games are organized into three chapters; this is separate from the baseline ZX disassemblies and is not an original-binary rebuild. Upstream-reported playable three-chapter recreation of both games; compiled-platform claims and fresh builds are unverified independently.

decisions.title: Boulder Dash for PlayStation
decisions.reason: Native PlayStation rules remake with ten original caves; upstream verification claims remain unconfirmed. C++ rules explicitly derive from documented 1984 behavior and C64 disassembly; actual cave.cpp implements cave generation, scan logic and game rules. Ten newly authored caves rather than copyrighted 1984 cave data; sound synthesized at boot. No build, emulation, hardware or playability testing here. README says host planner completes nine caves, not every cave. No independent proof of accuracy or byte identity. README and latest commit describe real emulated gameplay/render verification; planner completes nine of ten caves. Runtime/playability flags are bounded upstream claims, not complete-game parity or our execution. A build recipe is not an independently demonstrated successful build.

decisions.title: Gauntlet Construction Kit
decisions.reason: Native C64 editor plus Python level generator; original game required. 6502 editor gedit.asm runs on C64; Python generator produces 128-level D64 and cassette images. Level formats derived from disassembly; generated data separate from original game data. Requires user-owned Gauntlet or Deeper Dungeons; no original game included according to README. Generated level statistics and upstream playability checks do not establish independent playability. No explicit software license file in root tree. README says native editor runs on C64 and Python writes 128-level disk images. This is upstream runtime evidence; no independent compile/conversion/hardware check. Editor builds with CBM prg Studio; batched tape workflows remain explicitly hardware-untested.

decisions.title: re64 collaborative C64 reverse-engineering framework
decisions.reason: Active collaborative C64 reverse-engineering framework; source and experiment records available. TypeScript work-queue 6502 disassembler, PRG/D64 loading and structured claims model; MCP/HTTP/WebSocket interfaces share project knowledge. Source implements control-flow warnings, target discovery and memory-layer handling; experiments document agents analyzing programs. Active development; not a game reconstruction itself. README says user header is not authenticated; deploy security not assessed. Game/ROM/reference artifacts have distinct provenance; project MIT label does not license third-party games. README and 11 documented agent-analysis experiment runs establish upstream use of the server/UI/API. npm scripts and Node >=22.5 requirement are reviewed, but compilation/tests were not run. Model/lifter tests are not whole-machine accuracy or game completion.

decisions.title: SMON C64 readaptation
decisions.reason: C64 readaptation of the known SMON monitor lineage; copied documentation and build-script caveats retained. 6502 monitor/direct assembler adapted back to C64, with C64 KERNAL and CIA definitions in source. Adds memory size/test, BASIC DATA output, load/save and help features per README. README retains outdated Ben Eater/serial installation text and conflicting removed/added command descriptions. Use actual C64 source/config evidence over copied setup text. build.py failure path missing sys import. No explicit license file found; historical magazine/source rights not resolved. Author explicitly confirms compiling on Windows 10 and running generated floppy image in VICE. Positive flags are attributed upstream. build.py omits importing sys before sys.exit on failure; inherited Ben Eater serial/ROM setup instructions do not describe this C64 target.

decisions.title: PET Project development and debugging tools
decisions.reason: Agent-oriented PET development/debugging tools; external VICE and cc65 required. Python petlib CLI/MCP tooling for Commodore PET sessions, BASIC tokenization, 6502 assembly, debugging and disk packaging. Actual build.py wraps cc65 assembly/link and PET program packaging; native PET demo sources included. Tool suite depends on VICE, not a new emulator or standalone recreation of its demo games. Debian/Ubuntu VICE ROM setup remains external; README explains it. README reports real VICE integration testing and packaged native PET demos; runnable means upstream CLI/tool use. Python >=3.11, VICE >=3.5 and cc65 are explicit dependencies. No installer/build/VICE session or demo gameplay was executed here.

decisions.title: dwimsy media-preservation toolkit
decisions.reason: Partial media-preservation toolkit; native PC-8001/PC-8801 tape path implemented, broad roadmap unimplemented. Pure-Python tape pulse/FSK/audio core, PC-88 T88 container/protocol implementation, convert/inspect/split/join and WAV/T88 filters. Actual dispatcher and PC-88 block/state parsing inspected. Broad disk/ROM/multimachine support is largely roadmap, not current capability. Amiga/C64/SC-3000 search matches largely come from broad roadmap/dependency discussion, not evidence of implemented support. Added NEC PC-8001 and NEC PC-8801 as genuinely distinct source machines: README explicitly documents both current streaming filters. Other machine claims remain roadmap. ChatGPT attribution in README belongs to the linked fat8_d88_tool dependency, not proof of dwimsy authorship. README documents an actual Dig Dug PC-8801 capture conversion and current PC-8001/PC-8801 streaming filters. This supports upstream runtime only. Run from checkout withPython 3.9+; no packaging manifest/installed command yet. Most other machine/disk/ROM support remains roadmap.

decisions.title: MGI: Multi Game Interpreter
decisions.reason: Partial multi-engine adventure interpreter and authoring toolkit; no title claimed completable. TypeScript implementations of SCUMM, AGI, SCI, AGOS and several Revolution engine families, plus authoring/export tooling. Actual SCUMM v5 script engine dispatch/handlers and build configuration reviewed. Engine bytecode interpretation is implementation of the game engines, not CPU/game-machine emulation. Eight family labels must not be read as full game support; Lure does not execute bytecode, Sky only reaches a room, Broken Sword II does not walk. Ninth SLUDGE family has reader/disassembler only and no interpreter. Requires user-owned game data; DOS-first scope excludes several non-DOS variants despite broad search matches. No local test/build/gameplay validation. Source/config and upstream engine capability matrix inspected. Some SCUMM/AGI/SCI sequences execute, but no engine/title completion claim; Lure bytecode execution and SLUDGE interpreter absent, Sky reaches a room only, Sword II cannot walk. Runnable=true is bounded upstream demonstration, not broad playability. npm/Vite build not run.

README explicitly says the project source codes are currently PRIVATE. Tools may be interesting, but claims and binary archives do not meet the source-backed threshold. No project is added by this decision. No build or runtime verification was performed.

decisions.reason: Substantial citation-backed reference corpus and routing scripts, but not a distinct game/application reconstruction, emulator, source recovery or development implementation. This is distinct from the tracked BBC binary reconstruction and JavaScript path-tracing remake. substantial historical implementation; runtime unverified. README reports the author’s actual build time on an Acer laptop and says the program was tested using OpenGL 3.0. Compilable/runnable=true are upstream-only historical build/runtime claims. No local CMake/Qt build, gameplay or compatibility test was performed, and complete playability remains null. Rights: GPL-3.0-or-later (source header).

decisions.title: Oil's Well — Godot 4 remake
decisions.reason: Accepted at the reviewed scope. Native Godot remake of Oil’s Well. Pipe movement/retraction, collisions, enemies, oil collection, score, lives and level transitions are implemented in GDScript; neither a screenshot-only mockup nor a guest-instruction wrapper. gameplay source present; completion unverified. project.godot declares Godot 4.3, a main-menu scene and autoloaded game/music managers. Those settings and populated level scenes support the implementation scope, but no build, export, runtime or full-game test was performed. Every build flag stays null. Rights: No declared license found in inspected repository.

decisions.title: Knight of Wor — JavaFX remake of Wizard of Wor
decisions.reason: Accepted at the reviewed scope. Native Java/JavaFX remake of the C64 Wizard of Wor subject, with maze, player/enemy, bullet, score/lives and timed-update logic. It is distinct from the existing C64 assembly reconstruction. implemented game source; runtime unverified. README documents mvn clean install; pom.xml targets Java 8, an executable TitleScreen entry and 0.0.1-SNAPSHOT. Tests exist but were not run. Instructions and an executable-JAR configuration do not establish a successful build or modern JavaFX compatibility; all build flags remain null. Rights: GPL-3.0.

decisions.title: Blok Copy RX — native C64 Remix Edition source
decisions.reason: Accepted at the reviewed scope. Author-credited native homebrew source for the C64 Remix Edition, with VIC-II, joystick, title/game, score and puzzle-shuffling implementation. Source preservation does not by itself establish source restoration or binary-derived reverse engineering, so work_kinds is empty. It shares the Blok Copy design with the separate Atari edition. released source and binaries present. Source headers describe ACME assembly and Exomizer release packing; build.bat implements that recipe and PRG/binary assets are present. No successful clean assembly, execution or playability was independently established, and binary presence alone is insufficient; all build flags remain null. Rights: No declared license found.

decisions.title: Blok Copy — native Atari 8-bit Edition source
decisions.reason: Accepted at the reviewed scope. Hardware-specific Atari edition of the shared Blok Copy homebrew design. Native display lists, interrupts, player/missile graphics and puzzle rules distinguish it from the C64 implementation. No predecessor binary is shown as reverse-engineering input; work_kinds is empty rather than inventing a source-restoration or RE-derived-port method. released source and binaries present. Source headers and build.bat provide Xasm assembly followed by Exomizer Atari packing, and OBX/XEX outputs are present. These establish a substantive source/build tree, not a verified clean build or playable release; all build flags remain null. Rights: No declared license found.

decisions.title: Ultima V Remastered — C64 cartridge/disk adaptation and patches
decisions.reason: Accepted at the reviewed scope. Game-specific native C64 adaptation with loader/IO replacement, selective original music/IO disassembly, binary patches, savegame editor and build tooling. This is not a whole-game decompilation or rewrite. EasyFlash, 1581 and BackBit identify storage/device variants, not additional source platforms. author reports completed playthrough; independent runtime unverified. README says the author completed the EasyFlash version but did not test it thoroughly. Runnable/playable=true are upstream-only claims scoped to that variant, not independent verification of all media outputs. The Makefile assembles loaders, selectively disassembles original routines, patches disk data and packs media; compilable stays null pending a reproduced build with user-supplied disks. Rights: Apache-2.0 for new code.

decisions.title: 1NVADER — original C64 assembly game source
decisions.reason: Accepted at the reviewed scope. Original native homebrew game source written in 2019, with C64 screen, sprites, joystick and gameplay initialization. No historical executable is being disassembled or reimplemented; source_platforms/source_cpu/work_kinds are empty. released 2019, source available. README explicitly says the game was assembled with TurboMacroPro and first distributed on 17 May 2019. Compilable=true is an upstream-only historical assembly claim, not a verified current build. The checked Makefile instead uses TMPx, Exomizer and c1541 to create a D64. Runtime/playability and byte identity remain unknown. Rights: GPL-3.0.

decisions.title: Destiny Hunter — PET homebrew with C64 and Apple II ports
decisions.reason: Accepted at the reviewed scope. Standalone 2021 tribute homebrew with native game/map/enemy/control code and a stage editor. PET and C64 binaries are documented; Apple II branches and controls establish source support. This is one cross-platform original game, not a reconstruction of a predecessor commercial binary; source fields and work_kinds stay empty. released PET/C64 builds; additional target support partial. README documents PET/C64 release PRGs, a complete package and detailed gameplay/controls for a short self-contained game. Runnable/playable=true are upstream-only PET/C64 release claims. Apple II is source-supported only. Manual core.h target selection and machine-relative compiler paths remain; no clean compilation or game execution was performed, so compilable is null. Rights: Apache-2.0 (explicit file notice).

decisions.title: Wolf64 — native C64 Wolfenstein 3D fan port
decisions.reason: Accepted at the reviewed scope. Native C64 Wolfenstein 3D fan implementation with assembly raycaster, enemy chase/shoot/line-of-sight logic and native VIC/SID/input/loader modules. It is distinct from the existing Amiga CD32 port and does not execute the DOS program through a guest CPU interpreter. active native port; version 1.9 identified in credits. README/build.sh give an ACME/Python/c1541 recipe for KERNAL and Krill disk variants; credits identify version 1.9. A version label and recipe do not establish a successful build, frame-rate measurement or tested complete game. No source build or C64/emulator execution was performed, so all build flags remain null. Rights: No general code license found; noncommercial/fan notice and third-party caveats.

decisions.title: Crazee Rider — original BBC Micro source
decisions.reason: Author-released source adapted for BeebAsm; upstream build recipe available Kevin Edwards identifies this as his original 1987 racing game, detokenized from BBC BASIC inline assembly and adapted to BeebAsm. ROUT1.6502 implements input, game-state reset and vehicle control; MODULE.6502 contains BBC hardware IRQ and palette writes. Master.mak assembles separate game modules and emits the SSD image. The BBC and Electron roots are authentic machine-specific source versions, not duplicated mirrors. The BBC code includes raster palette changes absent from the Electron implementation. Author publishes converted original source for preservation; no explicit reuse license or LICENSE file was found. Public availability does not establish open-source permission. Documented build uses BeebAsm and a Windows make.bat wrapper. Supplied assembly, binary data and disk templates were inspected; no build, byte comparison, emulator or hardware execution was performed. Windows path/case assumptions should not be interpreted as a portable Unix build. This root covers BBC Micro only. The historical introduction mentions Master 128 and Electron, but that does not establish their source is included here.

decisions.title: Crazee Rider — original Acorn Electron source
decisions.reason: Author-released Electron version with documented BeebAsm build Distinct original Electron release adapted by Kevin Edwards, retaining 6502 gameplay and rendering source. MODULE.asm has Electron-specific joystick sampling and omits the BBC raster-palette IRQ path; game-state/control source differs from the BBC root. README documents fewer simultaneous opponents and manual palette selection. Master.mak and make.bat target CrazeeRiderElectron.ssd. Author publishes converted original source for preservation; no explicit reuse license or LICENSE file was found. Public availability does not establish open-source permission. Documented build uses BeebAsm and a Windows make.bat wrapper. Supplied assembly, binary data and disk templates were inspected; no build, byte comparison, emulator or hardware execution was performed. Windows path/case assumptions should not be interpreted as a portable Unix build. Gameplay runs at a different speed on BBC hardware according to the author; preserve the Electron target rather than treating the related BBC implementation as the same machine build.

decisions.title: Galaforce — original BBC Micro source
decisions.reason: Author-released original source with documented SSD build Original Kevin Edwards 1986 shoot-em-up source, converted from tokenized BASIC inline assembly to BeebAsm. PATT.asm contains native alien-pattern state and sequencing logic; Master.mak assembles aliens, bombs, sprite drawing, sound, waves and pattern data, then packages the disk image. The BBC build uses MODE 2; its separate Electron counterpart uses different graphics and sound routines. Author publishes converted original source for preservation; no explicit reuse license or LICENSE file was found. Public availability does not establish open-source permission. Documented build uses BeebAsm and a Windows make.bat wrapper. Supplied assembly, binary data and disk templates were inspected; no build, byte comparison, emulator or hardware execution was performed. Windows path/case assumptions should not be interpreted as a portable Unix build. Contains original binary graphic/font data alongside assembly; not every asset is text source. This root does not include a separately supported Master 128 release.

decisions.title: Galaforce — original Acorn Electron source
decisions.reason: Author-released distinct Electron source with BeebAsm recipe Original Electron version is preserved separately from the BBC Micro root. PATT.asm and SPRITES.asm contain concrete 6502 behavior and rendering; Master.mak selects the Electron code/data and loader. README explains MODE 5 four-color rendering, single-channel music and Plus 1/First Byte joystick support, providing machine-specific distinction from the BBC release. Author publishes converted original source for preservation; no explicit reuse license or LICENSE file was found. Public availability does not establish open-source permission. Documented build uses BeebAsm and a Windows make.bat wrapper. Supplied assembly, binary data and disk templates were inspected; no build, byte comparison, emulator or hardware execution was performed. Windows path/case assumptions should not be interpreted as a portable Unix build. Original graphics remain binary inputs. The author warns that this version runs unusually fast on a BBC Micro; machine support is not inferred from emulator loadability.

decisions.title: Galaforce 2 — original BBC Micro source
decisions.reason: Author-released source; anniversary title-screen modification Kevin Edwards released the sequel source for the BBC Micro anniversary; the original BBC BASIC source and converted assembly coexist. Main.asm and Object1.asm contain native game control/object initialization. Master.mak assembles gameplay modules and packages graphics and loader data. README explains MODE 5 as the memory-saving basis for bosses, pickups and other additions relative to Galaforce. Author publishes converted original source for preservation; no explicit reuse license or LICENSE file was found. Public availability does not establish open-source permission. Documented build uses BeebAsm and a Windows make.bat wrapper. Supplied assembly, binary data and disk templates were inspected; no build, byte comparison, emulator or hardware execution was performed. Windows path/case assumptions should not be interpreted as a portable Unix build. Author changed the title page for the anniversary, so do not label the current output byte-exact to the 1988 retail release. Electron source is promised rather than included. Module filename case and Windows path conventions need attention on a case-sensitive build host.

decisions.title: EDAS 1.8 — recovered C128 editor/assembler
decisions.reason: Recovered original self-hosting source; incomplete user documentation Mike Webb’s circa-1988 C128 editor/assembler, recovered by Kevin Edwards, includes both tokenized native source and a 168 KB readable assembly conversion. The assembly contains editor, parser/assembler and output routines, including C128 bank switching. It is substantive original development-tool source. README specifies self-building with supplied a1.8.prg on a C128 or emulator; creating a disk image and loading tokenized source are required. No explicit source license found; recovery/preservation credit is not a reuse grant. Self-hosted build requires the preassembled tool and .src input. The readable .asm file is for inspection and is not claimed to build using a modern cross-assembler. Documentation is explicitly incomplete. Historical NES and C64 development usage does not mean this editor runs on those machines; C128 is the runtime target.

decisions.title: wav2cas — MSX cassette audio and CAS toolkit
decisions.reason: Implemented cassette converter/synthesizer with embedded tests Pure-Python FSK demodulation and CAS encoding, with adaptive timing/confidence handling and optional ffmpeg conversion; adjacent scripts generate cassette audio and model recording/playback effects. Reviewed decode(), write_cas(), CAS synthesis and cassette DSP implementation; synthetic regression tests are present in source but were not run. This is a distinct MSX audio/CAS tool, rather than another copy of the already tracked PC-88 dwimsy tool. MSX-like is a format claim, not verified support for every retro computer. Default input conversion may use ffmpeg; pure-Python FLAC fallback is documented as slow. Root LICENSE is MIT, while cas2wav.py carries a separate public-domain assertion tied to its AI generation. Record the mixed notices without endorsing the claim that AI authorship automatically resolves rights. Tests and accuracy are upstream assertions/source facilities; no audio recovery or physical cassette test performed.

decisions.title: FAT8 D88 extractor and RBYTE tools
decisions.reason: Working according to upstream with heuristic detection and incomplete format coverage D88 FAT8 extraction implements sector/metadata/FAT-chain analysis and file reconstruction, plus protected-BASIC-save deobfuscation and character conversion. Concrete known-format structures cover PC-6001 mkII, PC-6601/SR, PC-88, PC-98 and Pasopia geometries. RBYTE image decoder code is also present. Distinct disk/filesystem utility from dwimsy’s currently implemented tape path; dwimsy only references this backend for broader integrations. README reports testing only a handful of images; machine detection is heuristic. BASIC detokenization, additional character sets and PC-6001 autostart detection remain TODO. rbyte88.py states that format details were inferred from one game and may be wrong. Root MIT license does not confer rights to input game images. PC-6001 mkII, PC-6601 and Pasopia are genuine extra machines needing catalogue-label review, not aliases for PC-88. Keep variant details in notes unless a new label is approved.

decisions.title: NONTAMA / MSX M-loader tape unpackers
decisions.reason: Implemented game-loader decoding with cartridge-builder support nontama_to_bload.py recognizes PC-6001 mkII NONTAMA headers, decodes loader payloads, and emits BLOAD data; mload_to_bload.py separately handles MSX Hudson/Honeybee loader tapes. mkrom.py generates native Z80 cartridge loader/trampoline bytes for the Warrior cartridge family using decoded data. README lists successful examples; implementation includes detailed analysis of an originally corrupted tape payload and charset smoke tests. PC-6001 mkII is a distinct hardware label that must be resolved before publication; do not relabel it PC-8001. Needs user-supplied P6/P6T or CAS images. MIT tool licensing does not license the games. Compatibility examples and cartridge-register fixes are upstream evidence only. A recent commit explains using port 0x7F for real hardware and PC6001VX compatibility; no cartridge/hardware validation was done.

decisions.title: cas2uef — compact CAS to BBC tape-image conversion
decisions.reason: Narrow format converter; deliberately heuristic tape timing Python converter splits compact CAS carrier blocks and writes UEF 0.10 data/tone/gap records for BBC Model B tape recordings. Actual serialization uses UEF headers and chunks, with a dummy starting block for older BBC OS behavior. Requires compact nonpadded CAS preserving block boundaries, specifically the form produced by DumpListEditor; this is not a general MSX-game-to-BBC port. CAS has lost waveform timing, so generated UEF uses heuristic pauses/default timings and is not audio-archival quality. README only says output appears to work in BeebEm. The script overwrites the named destination file. MIT applies to the converter, not its input tapes.

decisions.title: bin2fds — FDSStick capture-to-disk-image converter
decisions.reason: Narrow Python 2 converter; upstream describes limited success Parses FDS disk blocks and Nintendo-HVC headers from BIN captures, computes CRC diagnostics and emits an FDS header with padded 65,500-byte sides. Handles multiple input sides and rejects an existing output path; substantive recovery implementation rather than a file-extension renamer. Requires legacy Python 2, not Python 3. README says it only sometimes converts captures that other tooling failed to preserve. Code diagnoses CRC mismatches and can skip unexpected data; this is not proof of exact or complete recovery. Test against known-good source data before relying on an output. MIT license covers the tool, not original game disk contents. No input image was decoded during this review.

decisions.title: mzm2met — embedded NES ROM extraction
decisions.reason: Implemented bounded ROM decompressor/extractor with version-specific recipes mzm2met() decompresses headerless SZS data, apply_lzss_ofss() patches LZSS-compressed regions, and the output explicitly receives an iNES header. README gives offsets and input hashes for three 8 MiB MZM variants. Tool execution requires the user-supplied source image and correct per-version ranges. Primary documentation uses the acronym MZM rather than a full commercial title; the record does not expand it or assert an unsupported source-host machine. Version/offset-specific extraction is not an engine reconstruction or game-specific emulation runtime. Code has bounds checks but no independently verified output hash. MIT applies to tool code only. Supplied ROM recipes do not grant input or extracted-game redistribution rights.

decisions.title: kevedwards/timgeofffollinmusicdevdiskarchive
decisions.reason: README explicitly identifies this as a second recovery pass on the same Tim/Geoff Follin Einstein music-development disks previously recovered in already tracked breakintoprogram/archive-follin. Adds repaired/damaged data, raw IMG/DSK images, disk photos and K-prefixed newly archived disks; record as an alternate/additional preservation source rather than a second musical-driver project.

decisions.title: guybrush-atari/sonic-ste
decisions.reason: Tree has only .gitignore, README.md and Sonic-STe-0.8-alpha.zip; no primary implementation/build source inspected. The ZIP was not downloaded or executed, so do not assert its contents are binary-only.

decisions.title: atari-legend/legacy
decisions.reason: Legacy AtariLegend public website and CPANEL PHP/MySQL control-panel implementation, not Atari hardware/software reconstruction, original native retro code, a game port or emulation tool.

decisions.title: CPC Mastering tools
decisions.reason: Build/packaging collection includes already tracked iDSK plus 2CDT and gfx2crtc. Own dump-pal.py (MIT header) and BASIC loader are useful, but conservatively avoid separately counting this mostly vendored mastering bundle as new independent tooling.

decisions.title: SG1000 multicart (xrip)
decisions.reason: README explicitly says heavily based on already tracked aotta/SD-1000 and uses its PCB. Firmware/menu changes are real, but retain as derivative lineage rather than inflate independent project count.

decisions.title: SG1000 target for Crab/tms9918lib
decisions.reason: Platform wrapper/startup for tms9918lib and Crab. Count with accepted cdoty/tms9918lib rather than treating its submodule distribution as another independent library/game.

decisions.title: Conquest
decisions.reason: README calls it a Lords of Conquest remake and says it remains unfinished. The inspected complete client.js renders countries/resources and changes random ownership/icons when clicked; index.html launches it directly. No substantive playable rules implementation is established by the inspected map/click scaffold.

decisions.title: Augmentinel
decisions.reason: README explicitly states the original gameplay runs by emulating the Spectrum version of The Sentinel. Spectrum.cpp accesses original game's memory addresses; repository contains Z80 core, Spectrum ROM and game snapshot, while C++/D3D11 supplies modern rendering/VR. Visual Studio 2019+ build and GPLv3 source license are documented. Game-specific original-CPU emulation is audit-only under current scope; do not promote as a native reimplementation.

decisions.title: kevedwards/exilearchives
decisions.reason: Historical prerelease disk and binary archive, with photos and exported executable files; no substantive newly reconstructed implementation or recovered editable game source identified in the inspected tree. Useful preservation source, not another Exile implementation. Retain as a preservation source; editable recovered implementation evidence needs further inspection before any project promotion.

decisions.title: f-fix/pc88_tape_tools
decisions.reason: Substantive PC-8001/PC-8801 tape implementation, but already tracked dwimsy explicitly extracts/refactors this core and keeps it as its verification baseline. Retain as upstream provenance rather than add another same-core record in this batch. Direct README AI attribution belongs to this upstream and should not be automatically copied to all dwimsy code.

decisions.title: vaspervnp/projectkaptara
decisions.reason: Only CPC setup/title/display and an empty gameplay self-jump are implemented. Retain the inspected evidence as a lead, not a native-game candidate. This applies the same threshold as Conquest.

decisions.title: Dinozorus — original Amiga television-game source
decisions.reason: User-approved substantive repository-level discovery. Author-published source of the 1992–93 ATV television game, credited to Uğur “vigo” Özyılmazel. The repository’s later repair/import dates do not date the original game or an independent reverse-engineering effort. GPL-3.0 is present; graphics, characters, music and PRORUNNER have separately named contributors whose rights are not independently established. The README reports that the ADFs booted in FS-UAE after a 24-April-2022 fix and offers the level-1 binary to run and play. runnable/playable=true record those upstream historical claims only. The 2015 compilable-source statement is scoped to one transition level, so whole-repository compilable stays null. Asm-Pro and a locally edited dh1: include path are required; no present-day build was attempted.

decisions.title: Icarus — native Amiga and Atari voxel engine
decisions.reason: User-approved substantive repository-level discovery. Native Icarus engine/demo with ACE and separate Atari ikbd/SNDH/libcmini support. No predecessor game is identified as a reconstruction subject. No top-level engine/assets license was found; bundled dependency licensing cannot be applied to the whole repository. README explicitly names A3000, supporting the new exact catalogue label Amiga 3000. README documents make -f makefile_amiga and make -f makefile_atari with Bebbo/m68k-atari toolchains. The recipes depend on ACE, ikbd, SNDH and libcmini libraries and include absolute compiler paths. README says the engine works on the listed systems but gives no bounded successful build report for the inspected revision; all build flags remain null.

decisions.title: SDDDE — Amiga A1200 3D engine and map converters
decisions.reason: User-approved substantive repository-level discovery. Native 3D engine by Rst7/CBSIE, with a PC engine/data converter and kd-tree/PVS generator. Windows denotes companion output, not evidence of a Windows release of the Amiga demo. No project license was found. The LOAD_SPYRO option and bundled map data have unresolved provenance, so asset originality or redistribution is not asserted. The README says target/ contains an Amiga binary and converted data and names Bartman’s VSCode toolchain. SDDDE/Makefile supplies a -m68020 ELF-to-Hunk recipe using Windows shell commands. Bundled output is not proof of reproducibility or a completed playtest; compilable, runnable and playable stay null.

decisions.title: R-PAGE — native Amiga adventure-game framework
decisions.reason: User-approved substantive repository-level discovery. Framework from RESISTANCE, with Athanor 2 and other games cited as clients. MIT project license is explicit; miniz, Shrinkler, NRV2, ptreplay and ADPCM retain named upstream provenance and their own terms. It is supporting development infrastructure, not a reconstruction of any cited client game. README explicitly says the portable code builds on SAS/C, but this review found no bounded successful build/test report for the inspected revision. The framework opens AmigaOS libraries and is not itself a complete game. All four build fields remain null rather than treating the generic build badge or library source as a playtest.

decisions.title: Amiga Game Engine 0.4 — system-friendly graphics framework
decisions.reason: User-approved substantive repository-level discovery. Repository code credits Pedro Gil Guirado / Balrog Soft and carries an MIT license. C2P, music and texture components require separate provenance attention. Treat the project as a native framework, not a game reconstruction or independent PowerPC engine. SAS/C SCOPTIONS and smakefile describe compiling/linking Engine and framebuffer, bitmap, sprite, input and music modules. No successful build log or current runtime report was established. The brief README compatibility statement does not prove compilability or complete-game playability; all build flags remain null.

decisions.title: Planar — native Amiga blitter and game framework
decisions.reason: User-approved substantive repository-level discovery. Original Planar C framework by Lorenzo Di Gaetano, with separately sourced ptplayer integration. No project-wide license file was found in the inspected tree. The framework is supporting native development, and no legacy game reconstruction lineage is asserted. README documents vbcc plus Amiga NDK and a make workflow; Makefile also requires vasm and ptplayer. The source implements blits and double-buffered BOB handling, but the project is explicitly work in progress. Build recipe presence is not successful-build evidence; all flags remain null.

decisions.title: SAGE — high-end Amiga RTG game-engine library
decisions.reason: User-approved substantive repository-level discovery. SAGE is Fabrice Labrador’s native high-end Amiga library, with tutorials, demos, LibInclude and external PT-AHIPlay support. Documentation warns the API is in development. No project-wide license was found; external component terms cannot license SAGE as a whole. README documents SAS/C 6.5+ (author uses 6.59), vasm, external LibInclude headers/assigns and three library variants. Source makefile adds prebuilt PT-AHIPlay.o and compiles 68060/68080 modules. The documented recipe and shipped libraries do not establish an independently reproduced build or game playtest; flags remain null.

decisions.title: UIK — original AmigaOS user-interface object toolkit
decisions.reason: User-approved substantive repository-level discovery. Original UIK object engine by Jean-Michel Forgeas, identified as a 1992 release; objbox.c bears a 1990 implementation date and README links contemporary coverage. Those dates identify original development/publication, not reverse-engineering start. No explicit license was found. This is an archival toolkit subject, not an independently reconstructed engine. Historical preferences build requires lib:uik.lib, Amiga libraries, includeg:, lci:, UC: and PR: assigns and locale tools. Repository includes library objects and examples, but a complete reproducible modern build was not established. Compilable/runnable/playable and byte_exact remain null.

decisions.title: Laser Chess — Amiga BASIC-derived browser port
decisions.reason: User-approved substantive repository-level discovery. Explicit lineage: Mike Duppong’s 1987 Compute! Laser Chess, Tim Midkiff’s Amiga BASIC version, then this p5.js port. Supplied scans preserve the source relationship. This is source-derived translation, not an independent binary reverse-engineering project. No project license was found, and magazine-source/image rights remain distinct. README describes serving the directory locally and calls the historical RawGit page playable. That link was not verified operational, and the same README lists rotation, redraw, end-game, sound, scaling and laser-boundary TODOs. No current completed-game/runtime or compile claim is promoted; all flags remain null.

decisions.title: AmiGalaga — native Galaga reconstruction for PAL Amiga 500
decisions.reason: User-approved substantive repository-level discovery. Native reconstruction of Galaga behaviors with extracted user-ROM graphics, flight scripts and sound; MAME measurements and a separate Z80 analysis model supply reference evidence. Third-party hackbar-galaga disassembly is referenced but deliberately not bundled. MIT covers repository code only. Namco revision-B ROMs are user supplied, and README explicitly prohibits distributing generated executable/ADF data containing proprietary Galaga assets. README documents executable/ADF production and reports that the game has run in emulation on A500 through A4000, with one-player play through GAME OVER. runnable/playable=true record those upstream claims, not an independent test. A reproducible build still requires user-supplied Namco revision-B galaga.zip, vasm/vlink, Python 3.13+, uv and xdftool; compilable remains null because this review did not reproduce or inspect a bounded successful build log. byte_exact is null.

decisions.title: GermZ — native four-player Amiga game and map editor
decisions.reason: User-approved substantive repository-level discovery. Original Last Minute Creations game with code by KaiN, music/sound by Luc3k and graphics/levels by Softiron. MPL-2.0 covers code unless stated otherwise; res assets are separately CC BY-SA 4.0. ACE is a dependency, not a predecessor game being reconstructed. README specifies Bebbo/Bartman GCC, CMake, AmigaCMakeCrossToolchains and an ACE-based asset build. CMake provides conversion and native linking steps. The inspected docs are build instructions, not an independent or bounded current successful-build record; all build flags remain null.

decisions.title: Shalatuvaar / amiMelee — native Amiga hex-map game prototype
decisions.reason: User-approved substantive repository-level discovery. Shalatuvaar retains the older amiMelee identity and uses an external ACE checkout. The Melee influence is a rules/design relationship, not evidence of a binary translation or a licensed implementation of another computer game. No project-wide license was found. The old makefile expects ../ace/ace, copies its prebuilt objects and contains host-specific path handling. README is only the old amiMelee name. Actual game.c implements map, camera, character and mouse interaction with TODOs; no full combat, successful build or complete-game claim is supported. All build flags remain null.

decisions.title: Villages — native Amiga tile-and-road strategy-game source
decisions.reason: User-approved substantive repository-level discovery. Native Last Minute Creations game source using ACE. An MIT code license is present, but standalone asset provenance and complete release requirements are not documented in a README. No historical game reconstruction or specific predecessor lineage is asserted. src/makefile expects configured CC_FLAGS and ACE: objects and copies/rebuilds the ACE dependency. No README documents a complete release/build flow; implementation has scoring/traversal logic and TODOs. Source presence is not proof of successful compile or finished gameplay, so all flags stay null.

decisions.title: WeegieNights — AmiBlitz Amiga Game Jam source
decisions.reason: User-approved substantive repository-level discovery. Scottish Amiga Users Group 2022 jam entry with Rob Cranley code, named graphics/sound/level contributors and PHX ProTracker. Code is CC BY 4.0, other assets CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, and Banjo Guy Ollie title music remains separately copyrighted and used with permission. Obtain the matching release assets; these terms do not collapse into one code license. README explicitly states the source was compiled using AmiBlitz 3.8 and 3.9, supporting compilable=true as an upstream report. It uses PHX ProTracker and separate release assets; the .ab3-only source checkout is not assumed self-contained. No independent compile or gameplay verification occurred; runnable/playable/byte_exact stay null.

decisions.title: FitzQuake Amiga 68k — AmiQuake-derived NovaMesa port
decisions.reason: User-approved substantive repository-level discovery. Preserve FitzQuake → NovaCoder’s AmiQuake SDL base → this Amiga 68k/NovaMesa port. This is a source-derived port, not an independent Quake reconstruction. GPL-3.0 root license is present; original Quake game data remains outside engine-source licensing. README says this port tested NovaMesa functionality successfully, but supplies no build instructions. No build script was found in the inspected tree and src/Makefile returned 404. src/amiga_main.c provides native startup/stack handling, not reproducibility evidence. All build flags stay null; no gameplay completion is inferred from the OpenGL test statement.

decisions.title: Breathless SDL2 — Amiga 68020 assembly-to-C port
decisions.reason: User-approved substantive repository-level discovery. Source headers explicitly identify original Amiga assembly modules and an intermediate C translation, but exact source-release ancestry remains unresolved. LICENSE.txt is an unfilled MIT template with [year]/[fullname]; neither original Breathless rights nor valid project-wide relicensing is established. Original game assets require separate rights. Concrete SDL2 replacements show native translation rather than an embedded 68020 interpreter. CMake hardcodes a neighboring SDL2-2.30.11 x64 Windows SDK and copies SDL2.dll. loader.c requires data/Config and data/Breathless.gld, absent from the inspected source tree. No README documents compilation or completion; no successful build or runtime was established and every build flag stays null.

decisions.title: L’Abbaye des Morts — unfinished Amiga source port
decisions.reason: User-approved substantive repository-level discovery. Locomalito/Gryzor87 original game → David “Nevat” Lara’s Linux/SDL adaptation → this unfinished AmigaOS wrapper/port. Source preserves these credits and GPL-3.0 root licensing. Original assets retain separate provenance; the presence of graphics and a partial demo does not establish a finished release or universal redistribution permission. README explicitly says unfinished, super glitchy, far from completed and on hold. src/makefile compiles/link modules with SAS/C; main.c forces exit after one state-loop iteration. These substantiate an incomplete native port, not a complete playable build. Current compilation/runtime and byte comparison remain unknown, so flags are null.

decisions.title: Leonardo — original Amiga puzzle-game source archive
decisions.reason: User-approved substantive repository-level discovery. Archive of the 1989 Leonardo box-moving puzzle game, preserving game/intro/loader sources and assets. Source/Game/makefile directly confirms title identity; unrelated/other historical subtrees are not collapsed into that identity. No README or license was found; archived commercial-era source/assets do not imply reuse rights. source/Game/makefile explicitly names Leonardo, is dated 28-Jan-1989 and uses as, ln and AbsLoad with a:lib2/cdisk.o and historical include/assign paths. The separate pengi/makefile names other objects and is not treated as the definitive Leonardo recipe. No modern build, complete-release recreation or playtest was established; flags remain null.

decisions.title: Snackzone — original Bifi Roll Free Amiga game source
decisions.reason: User-approved substantive repository-level discovery. Original Bifi Roll Free advertising-game archive. Shared Rolling Ronny names in build headers and gameplay objects preserve engine/build ancestry; they do not make this the same project or establish independent reconstruction. No license was found; advertising brand, source and assets retain unresolved rights. makefile lists gameplay/level/character modules and SAS/C, Genim2, SLink/SpecAbsLoad steps. It retains Rolling Ronny headers and Projects:SnackZone paths. The historical recipe and source do not demonstrate a currently reproducible build or complete game package; all build flags remain null.

decisions.title: Brain Braiser — original Amiga strategy-game source
decisions.reason: User-approved substantive repository-level discovery. Original Lutz Großhennig game written in 1990, originally intended for Kickstart magazine; current archive carries an MIT license. The original source date is not a reverse-engineering start date. The in-game computer opponent is game logic, not evidence of generative-AI-assisted development. README explicitly says the game runs fine on a stock A500 with Kickstart 1.2+, with detailed gameplay/control description; runnable/playable=true reflect the author’s claim. Building still requires Profimat dialect features, notably ALIGN/EVEN and IBYTES embedded-data handling. No current assembly or byte-exact recreation was established; compilable/byte_exact remain null.

decisions.title: Baycat Command — recovered unfinished Amiga game source
decisions.reason: User-approved substantive repository-level discovery. Lutz Großhennig’s unfinished original 1989 scrolling-game project, recovered from damaged archival media and published with an MIT license. Dungeons and Ballerspiel are mentioned as other projects, not equivalent subjects or code-proven ancestors. Source restoration is explicit; complete game reconstruction is not. README says damaged disks/files were being recovered and the author was still getting the source compilable. Enemies, sounds, levels and animations are explicitly missing. No rebuild success is claimed; all flags remain null rather than equating unfinished gameplay with proven inability to execute any demo.

decisions.title: Crack — original Amiga breakout-game source archive
decisions.reason: User-approved substantive repository-level discovery. Original 1988 Arkanoid-style game archive with later revisions and construction/intro components. Arkanoid-style describes design similarity, not a licensed port or reconstructed Arkanoid binary. No README/license was found; commercial-era source and game-asset redistribution rights remain unresolved. makefile builds game, construction utility and two intros with Genim2/SAS C/SLink and historical includes. Multiple source/disk revisions coexist without a modern README or proven release manifest. No current successful compile, runnable package, playtest or binary match was established; all flags remain null.

decisions.title: Rolling Ronny — original Amiga platform-game source archive
decisions.reason: User-approved substantive repository-level discovery. Original Rolling Ronny source archive described upstream as a 1990 project, retaining WonderGirl working-title and shared engine/build history. Do not substitute an unsupported commercial release date or call this an independent reverse-engineering effort. No license was found; commercial-era code, graphics, music and loader rights remain unresolved. makefile builds game, intro and Virgin loader modules with Genim2/SLink/SpecAbsLoad, historical h: includes and DH0:Ronny backup paths. Source and associated graphics/sound are present, but exact release completeness and present-day reproducibility are not established. All build flags remain null.

decisions.title: Alien3 — original C64 source
decisions.reason: Accepted at the demonstrated scope. Original historical game source released by Michael J. Archer for preservation, including gameplay, loader, maps, music and graphics. This is original-source preservation, not a binary-derived disassembly or a verified restoration. README states that development used PC/PDS and that the original C64 sprite and level editors are missing. The historical source and data tree do not establish a reproducible modern build or retail-binary identity; all build flags remain null. Michael J. Archer is credited as the original source author. The repository is a historical developer archive, not an independent remake; the original copyright and game/asset rights remain relevant.

decisions.title: Rubicon — disk protection reconstruction
decisions.reason: Accepted at the demonstrated scope. Disk-protection analysis and native protection-track writer/copier for Rubicon. Upstream explicitly reconstructs protection from disk observations without reversing the loader, so this is not a whole-game disassembly. README reports successfully producing a master disk using WP/RUBICOPY and the explanation describes the physical-drive result. Runnable=true is an upstream-only disk-tool claim; no drive writes, assembler build, gameplay or independent comparison were performed. The perfect-master statement does not establish byte_exact. Zibri/RamJam documents new protection-track reconstruction for the existing Rubicon game. The distributed D64 images and game data remain distinct from the new writer code; no repository license grant was found.

decisions.title: Revenge — retro reverse-engineering environment
decisions.reason: Accepted at the demonstrated scope. Pre-alpha browser reverse-engineering environment implementing 6502 disassembly, C64/VIC-20 binary recognition, BASIC decoding and code tracing. Planned Z80 and other systems are not included as supported targets. README says the pre-alpha system works in part and describes tested C64/VIC-20 carts, PRG and BASIC input. Runnable=true records that bounded upstream-only tool report. The test badge and Bun commands do not prove a reproduced build; compilable/playable/byte_exact remain null. The implementation credits mist64/c64ref reference data. That dependency and embedded ROM/sample binaries have distinct provenance; repository GPL-3.0 metadata does not itself clear every included historical binary.

decisions.title: Silk Dust — multi-platform adventure source
decisions.reason: Accepted at the demonstrated scope. Original text-adventure homebrew source written in AWS and converted with AWS2C. Reviewed C64 and Amiga makefiles provide concrete platform build paths; this is not reconstruction of an earlier commercial binary. The C64 makefile generates three AWS-derived C parts and PRG outputs; the Amiga makefile invokes scripts for combined or split parts. These are recipes, not reproduced compilation or gameplay. The hard-coded Exomizer path and expected AWS2C parent/submodule layout need configuration; all build flags remain null. DarwinNE/Davide Bucci supplies the original adventure; AWS2C is the generating tool dependency, not a predecessor game reconstruction. GPL-3.0 repository metadata does not automatically license all packaged disk images or external tools.

decisions.title: Frostbite — native C64 port
decisions.reason: Accepted at the demonstrated scope. Native C64 reimplementation/port of Activision’s Frostbite with actual game, actor/environment, control, HUD and audio assembly modules. The reviewed evidence does not establish binary-derived recovery of the original game. KickAssembler-style game source and bundled graphics/SID assets establish substantive implementation. README supplies little build guidance, and binary/release presence is not a reproduced build or gameplay test. Paths/case may need adaptation; all build flags remain null. Activision’s Frostbite is the original subject, while Tony Savon’s repository is the C64 port. The adapted manual supports Atari 2600 lineage. No repository-wide license was found; original title/art/audio rights are not cleared by source publication.

decisions.reason: Accepted at the demonstrated scope. Native C64 reimplementation/port of Activision’s Crackpots with actual game, actor/environment, control, HUD and audio assembly modules. The reviewed evidence does not establish binary-derived recovery of the original game. KickAssembler-style game source and bundled graphics/SID assets establish substantive implementation.
