decisions.reason: Substantial source adaptation of 0x7f's Black Castle: player weapons, monsters, bosses, level data and platform-specific sound/scrolling implementations. The inspected port has explicit SM83, Z80 and mos6502 targets rather than an embedded guest CPU interpreter.

decisions.title: gb_slideshow — Game Boy slideshow builder and viewer
decisions.reason: Native presentation viewer plus a host-side JSON-to-header compiler. PNG backgrounds, per-text placement/colours, typewriter animation, slide navigation and cartridge-RAM resume are implemented rather than only described.

decisions.title: pattern_maker_for_GBC — interactive Game Boy pattern generator
decisions.reason: A compact but complete-looking native graphics experiment: the user enters a binary sequence with A/B, edits it, then the program repeats the pattern around an expanding square spiral using GBDK drawing primitives. The repository contains approximately 180 lines of project-specific C and pattern.gb.

decisions.title: Better Button Test — native Game Boy input and link diagnostics
decisions.reason: Native diagnostic ROM with per-button counters, invalid D-pad detection, model detection, link-cable exchange, screen alignment/gradient tests, sound feedback and theme persistence. Selected C implements the diagnostic state and flash-save routines.

decisions.title: Game Boy Audio Synthesis & Sample Playback — native channel-3 synthesis experiment
decisions.reason: Native channel-3 audio demonstration implementing timer-interrupt sawtooth generation and variable-rate playback of an embedded sample. The inspected source writes wave RAM and sound registers and exposes pitch/mode controls.

decisions.title: VGM player — native SD-card music player for GB and Sega
decisions.reason: Native VGM file browser/player streams uncompressed register-command music from cartridge SD storage. Separate Game Boy wave/sound, Game Gear stereo PSG and Master System PSG/OPLL implementations are present; inspected implementations decode VGM command bytes directly rather than executing a guest CPU.

decisions.title: gameboy-usb-mouse — native link-port mouse library and drawing demo
decisions.reason: GBDK input integration and a drawing demonstration for an Inside Gadgets USB adapter with modified CH559 firmware. Source implements serial interrupt transfers, a receive ring buffer, three-byte packet decoding, cursor motion and mouse-controlled drawing/scroll/clear.

decisions.title: KPaint — native Game Boy drawing application
decisions.reason: A substantial native four-shade drawing application with 18×15 canvases, up to sixteen in-memory canvases, cursor/menu input and visual colour indicators. README describes Kindle e-ink palette optimisation; the output remains a Game Boy ROM, not a native Kindle port.

decisions.title: hash-bench-gb — native Game Boy hash benchmark
decisions.reason: Native benchmark cartridge measures eighteen checksum/noncryptographic/light-cryptographic algorithms against a generated 1024-byte buffer. Inspected C implements dispatch, paginated/sortable results and frame-counter timing, plus concrete xxHash32 and classical hash implementations.

decisions.title: DummyOSC — native Game Boy waveform oscillator
decisions.reason: Native waveform oscillator with pitch/octave selection, preset waveforms, waveform visualisation and sound-register/timer control. Inspected implementation copies selected packed samples into channel-3 wave RAM and updates the display from waveform contents.

decisions.title: Shifty — native Game Boy PRNG drone experiment
decisions.reason: Native experimental drone generator evolves a 32-nibble shift-register waveform, packs it into channel-3 wave RAM in a timer interrupt, and uses waveform data for scanline distortion. Period controls, waveform reseeding and playback state are implemented.

decisions.title: Kaiju Feeder — native cross-console helicopter game
decisions.reason: Substantial ZGBJam 2019 game adapted for Game Boy, Game Gear and Master System. Inspected source implements helicopter acceleration, landing/death states, hook deployment, collisions and three-level progression; assets and menu/win states are present.

decisions.title: Polka Sheep — native cross-console sheep-launching game
decisions.reason: Substantial BitBitJam 2017 game adapted for Game Boy, Mega Duck and Game Gear. Player aiming/flying/dancing states, launch motion, damage, moving platforms, enemies and banked multi-level maps are represented in source.

decisions.title: CellBoy — native Game Boy cellular-machine remake
decisions.reason: Native Cell Machine remake explicitly crediting Sam Hogan's original. Substantial C implements cell placement/rotation, push/generator/update rules, step/run simulation, scrolling maps, menus and cartridge-RAM save/load state.

decisions.title: PC98 disk image tools — HDM, FDI and HDI format utilities
decisions.reason: Independent PC-98 disk-format analysis and Python conversion suite: synthesizes FDI geometry headers, strips FDI/HDI headers, checks heuristic image validity and creates blank media.

decisions.title: NewView — OS/2 INF and HLP viewer replacement
decisions.reason: Aaron Lawrence and Ronald Brill OS/2 help viewer and replacement HelpMgr.dll, with substantive IPF file parsing, full-text search and native Presentation Manager integration.

decisions.title: PMDLL — OS/2 NE and LX dependency analyzer
decisions.reason: Preserved native OS/2 Presentation Manager utility by Arthur van Beek and Steven Levine that parses executable import tables and diagnoses DLL search-path and load failures.

decisions.title: PMSpy — OS/2 Presentation Manager message inspector
decisions.reason: IBM sample-derived PMSpy source archive with native window selection, message filtering and shared hook DLL implementation for observing posted and sent OS/2 PM messages.

decisions.title: SD386 — preserved OS/2 source and remote debugger
decisions.reason: IBM SD386 5.00 final source archive: native source/assembly debugging, symbol/type inspection, multithread/process control and ESP remote-debug transport support.

decisions.title: RESMGR — OS/2 NE and LX resource decompiler
decisions.reason: Martin Lafaix resource manager/decompiler suite preserving REXX resource-container editing and .RES-to-.RC reconstruction plus C/Pascal packed-resource extraction helpers for OS/2 binaries.

decisions.title: emxomf — partial a.out-to-OS/2 OMF converter source
decisions.reason: Eberhard Mattes emxomf preserved converter implementation, including GNU a.out relocation/symbol handling and STABS-to-IBM HLL3 debug-information translation.

decisions.title: FDAPM — DOS power management and idle TSR
decisions.reason: Eric Auer native DOS APM/ACPI control utility and resident idle handler, implementing POWER-compatible modes, cache flushing, disk/video power controls and reboot/shutdown paths.

decisions.title: NANSI — enhanced DOS ANSI console driver
decisions.reason: Daniel Kegel NANSI preserved and extended DOS console-driver source implementing ANSI escape-state parsing, cursor/video handling and keyboard reassignment with FreeDOS-era maintenance.

decisions.title: FreeDOS GRAPHICS — graphics-screen printer TSR
decisions.reason: Eric Auer native DOS replacement GRAPHICS utility implementing resident CGA/EGA/VGA/MCGA screen capture and PostScript, Epson ESC/P and HP PCL printer output.

decisions.title: SDL Hercules Hyperion — IBM mainframe emulator
decisions.reason: Official Hercules continuation implementing System/370, ESA/390 and z/Architecture processors, devices, hardware console, tracing and historical disk/tape utilities.

decisions.title: DtCyber — CDC 6000 and Cyber system emulator
decisions.reason: Control Data 6000/70/170/180 system simulator with 60-bit CPU and peripheral processors, disk/tape/network devices, dual Cyber 170/180 state operation and historical-system installation automation.

decisions.title: Dubna — BESM-6 monitor-system emulator
decisions.reason: BESM-6 48-bit instruction and extracode emulator with Dubna monitor job processing, embedded system tapes, assembler, simulated drums/disks, text encodings and plotter-output generation.

decisions.title: DG/Emua — Data General MV and AOS/VS emulator
decisions.reason: Ada rewrite of Data General MV/Eclipse emulation, sharing processor and memory code between physical MV hardware simulation and AOS/VS Ring-7 user-program emulation.

decisions.title: retro-B5500 — Burroughs B5500 browser emulator
decisions.reason: JavaScript Burroughs B5500 stack/descriptor processor and multiprocessor central-control emulator with peripheral devices, browser console and software/source recovery artifacts.

decisions.title: retro-220 — Burroughs 220 browser emulator
decisions.reason: JavaScript implementation of the decimal Burroughs 220 processor, arithmetic and control panels with Cardatron, tape and terminal peripheral models, accompanied by BALGOL recovery work.

decisions.title: retro-1620 — IBM 1620 Model 2 browser emulator
decisions.reason: JavaScript IBM 1620 Model 2 decimal processor, memory-cycle state machine, operator panel and card/paper-tape/disk/printer/plotter operating environment with historical software recovery.

decisions.title: Emulator Kit — retro-system development simulators
decisions.reason: Coherent kit of processor, bus, serial, storage and display models for RC2014/RCbus, Retrobrew and other retrocomputers, focused on software development and Fuzix testing.

decisions.title: AXPbox — Alpha ES40 system emulator
decisions.reason: Continuation of discontinued ES40 emulator with DecChip 21264CB EV68 CPU/PALcode, Tsunami chipset, storage/network/display devices and optional x86-64 JIT.

decisions.title: GXemul — multiarchitecture full-system emulator
decisions.reason: Preserved GXemul 0.6 tree with C/C++ instruction translation, full-system DECstation/SGI and other workstation machine models, peripheral/network emulation and debugger infrastructure.

decisions.title: RetroBSD — 2.11BSD port for PIC32
decisions.reason: Historical BSD Unix source port for PIC32 microcontrollers, preserving kernel, libc, userland utilities, native compiler environment and BSD filesystem while supplying board support and cross-build/image tools.

decisions.title: oricOpenLibrary — native Oric support libraries
decisions.reason: Suite of Oric BASIC/Sedoric bindings, joystick support, ROM identification, QR generation and font rendering with native tests.

decisions.title: Orix Shell — native Oric command-shell ROM
decisions.reason: Native ROM-resident shell and built-in command suite for the Orix kernel on Telestrat/Twilighte systems.

decisions.title: WAVE — Twilighte Oric tracker source archive
decisions.reason: Preserved source of Twilighte's native three-channel music tracker, editors, compilers and playback routines.

decisions.title: Antarctic Adventure — MSX annotated disassembly
decisions.reason: Semantically annotated Z80 reconstruction of four official Antarctic Adventure cartridge variants.

decisions.title: Elite — MSX disk-game annotated disassembly
decisions.reason: Annotated reconstruction of the 1987 Firebird/Mr. Micro MSX disk release including loader, game, ship shapes and support programs.

decisions.title: Pinball Construction Set — Atari 800 original sources
decisions.reason: Bill Budge's preserved Atari 800 Pinball Construction Set editor/runtime source and original development disks.

decisions.title: Fort Apocalypse — original Atari 400/800 sources
decisions.reason: Steve Hales' original SynAssembler-format Fort Apocalypse source, fonts and level data.

decisions.title: Martin Galway C64 music — original driver and score sources
decisions.reason: Author-published original C64 music-player and score source for Wizball, Green Beret, Arkanoid, Rambo loader and Game Over.

decisions.title: Ozmoo — Commodore-family Z-machine interpreter
decisions.reason: Modern redistributable native Z-machine interpreter with Commodore-family backends and disk/story build tooling.

decisions.title: Apple II Audit — hardware and emulator behavior tests
decisions.reason: Native audit suite identifying Apple II hardware/ROM/RAM configurations and testing softswitch, memory and video behavior.

decisions.title: Apple II Dead Test — March-U RAM diagnostic ROM
decisions.reason: Diagnostic F8 ROM testing zero-page/stack without relying on working DRAM there, then testing detected Apple II memory.

decisions.title: Zapple-II / BP/M — SoftCard CP/M-compatible environment
decisions.reason: Native dual-CPU CP/M-compatible CCP/BDOS/BIOS environment translating Z80 program file operations into Apple II ProDOS services.

decisions.title: MouseII — Apple II mouse driver and demo
decisions.reason: Native slot-discovering mouse driver with cursor, interrupt and click handling plus demonstration application.

decisions.title: Apple2CoCo — Apple II+ emulator for CoCo 3
decisions.reason: General Apple II+ emulator running natively on CoCo 3, with 6502 opcode engine, ROM loader, keyboard and text/lo-res display mapping.

decisions.title: tinyedit native Amiga UTF-8 editor
decisions.reason: Cross-platform text editor with a substantial native Amiga RastPort/FreeType frontend, multiple buffers, syntax highlighting, text conversion and optional spelling, speech and printing features.

decisions.title: AmiLisp / CL-Amiga Common Lisp implementation
decisions.reason: Native Common Lisp compiler, bytecode VM and runtime for AmigaOS3 and MorphOS, with m68k template JIT, host variants, FASL/heap-image support and an optional Clamacs IDE submodule.

decisions.title: riscos-artworks-js ArtWorks reader/writer
decisions.reason: JavaScript preservation library that reads and writes Computer Concepts-era RISC OS ArtWorks vector files, with JSON unpack/pack and experimental SVG rendering.

decisions.title: miniupnp Atari ST/STE media and utility sources
decisions.reason: Native ST/STE source collection containing DMA AU audio player, CosmosEx media transport, ACSI inquiry tool, IFF/GIF viewers, TOS executable analysis, YM sample playback and reusable assembly routines.

decisions.title: MacVox68 network text-to-speech client
decisions.reason: Native classic Macintosh TCP/text-to-speech work-in-progress with code-driven Toolbox UI, classic/OpenTransport network backends, substantial text/prosody parsing and Speech Manager test output.

decisions.title: Messages for Macintosh iMessage client
decisions.reason: Classic Macintosh iMessage client suite: native C/QuickDraw interface communicates over serial to Node-backed workloads and a modern-Mac GraphQL iMessage service.

decisions.title: Nuklear QuickDraw classic Macintosh GUI toolkit
decisions.reason: Substantial integer-math/monochrome adaptation of Nuklear with native QuickDraw backend, command caching, Toolbox event integration and calculator demonstration for low-end classic Macs.

decisions.title: CoprocessorJS serial workload bridge
decisions.reason: Host-side JavaScript execution bridge for resource-constrained vintage computers: serial framed requests install per-application workloads and invoke functions/evaluation on a modern Node host.

decisions.title: serialperformanceanalyzer Retro68 profiling tool
decisions.reason: Host-side serial/file-log profiler for instrumented classic Macintosh/Retro68 applications, matching PROFILE_START/END markers and rendering timing/call-count charts.

decisions.title: CUBE, Great Battle Ship and SATORI original X68000 sources
decisions.reason: Author-published native X68000 game-source archive for CUBE crystal/barrage avoidance simulator, Great Battle Ship shooter and SATORI bullet-dodging game, including C/assembly, data and old build scripts.

decisions.title: CBLibrary RISC OS application support library
decisions.reason: Native RISC OS C support library implementing drag/drop, clipboard/data transfer, document tracking, directory iteration, timed scheduling and Wimp/Toolbox helpers.

decisions.title: CBOSLib RISC OS SWI veneer library
decisions.reason: Type-safe native C veneers for RISC OS operating-system interfaces not covered by Acorn Wimp/Toolbox libraries, including file catalogues, sprites, modes, messages and task enumeration.

decisions.title: SF3KLib Star Fighter 3000 bitmap conversion library
decisions.reason: Reusable C library for converting Star Fighter3000 planet, sky and tile bitmap formats to/from RISC OS sprites, with explicit game-file structures and progress callbacks.

decisions.title: Iapetus — Saturn hardware development library
decisions.reason: Substantial native Saturn library: CD command/ISO filesystem access, VDP1 drawing lists, peripheral/debug support and cartridge communication, with a separately compiled sound driver. This is hardware-facing implementation source, not a game-specific CPU wrapper.

decisions.title: Flicky's Flock — Saturn twelve-player flap game
decisions.reason: Native Sonic-themed Flappy Bird-style game with per-player movement/lives, collision checks, pipes, power-ups, ranking and multiple game states in substantial main.c. This is unrelated in gameplay and implementation to the older Sega arcade game Flicky.

decisions.title: Disasteroids — Saturn twelve-player asteroid shooter
decisions.reason: Native cooperative/versus asteroid shooter with distinct ship, projectile, asteroid, alien, collision and gameplay implementations. Multiple players share a Saturn-native Jo Engine game rather than executing an original Asteroids ROM.

decisions.title: Sweeper Squad — Saturn twelve-player mine puzzle
decisions.reason: Native multiplayer Minesweeper-style implementation with team scoring, player/grid objects, mine/remaining-square counters, explosions, flags, sprite asset loading and game-state callbacks.

decisions.title: AsteroidsTerra — Saturn native asteroid shooter
decisions.reason: Native Asteroids-inspired game written for Saturn. Substantial asteroid.c implements playfield/collision, game-state update, bullets, power-ups, energy, backgrounds and animation, with main.c entering that implementation.

decisions.title: Circuit Breaker — Saturn 3D arena prototype
decisions.reason: Substantial native Saturn 3D movement/arena prototype with camera, controller polling, continuous travel, boost gauge, gradual turning, 3D walls and rendering helpers. It is more than a starter scene, while a complete finished game is not established.

decisions.title: VUEngine — Virtual Boy native game engine
decisions.reason: Substantial object-oriented Virtual C engine providing scene/actor/component architecture, physics, collision testing, sprite rendering, camera management, audio and hardware abstractions for native Virtual Boy programs.

decisions.title: libgccvb — Virtual Boy hardware library continuation
decisions.reason: VUEngine-Studio-compatible continuation of the native Virtual Boy library by various authors. Inspected affine transform code, hardware pad polling, audio-register mapping, V810 inline assembly and startup vectors.

decisions.title: VUE-MASTER — Virtual Boy stereo-image viewer
decisions.reason: Native stereo-image viewing application and configurable VUEngine template, with image switching, fade transitions, image number/control display and colour-mode handling implemented in VueMasterState.

decisions.title: Multi Color Demo — Virtual Boy brightness demonstration
decisions.reason: Native interactive graphics demonstration with actual mode-switching code for dithering, column-table brightness repeats and frame-alternated blending. It exercises Virtual Boy display hardware through VUEngine.

decisions.title: Flash Cart Test Program — Virtual Boy cartridge QA
decisions.reason: Native cartridge diagnostic which checks retained SRAM data, writes and reads a test pattern, displays results, and selects success/failure sounds. Includes alignment-screen input and low-power support.

decisions.title: DaumenKinosaurier — Virtual Boy stereoscopic flipbook
decisions.reason: Native Virtual Boy adaptation of StereoBoy's 2009 stereoscopic student flipbook, implementing named animation sequences, input, camera effects, transitions and credits through substantial AnimatedImage/AnimationState source.

decisions.title: VUEngine Video Player — Virtual Boy native frame viewer
decisions.reason: Native ROM-resident frame-animation player with pause/play, forward/back stepping, progress display and paired-frame HiColor handling. Included converted Mario footage is media content rather than an embedded executable game.

decisions.title: Capitán Sevilla 3D — Virtual Boy action-platform demo
decisions.reason: Native Virtual Boy action-platformer source, with Captain actor behaviour, event/progress/checkpoint management, camera effects and rumble support. README identifies it as a rebuilt tribute/sequel to the 1988 game and a continuation of the 2010 Capitán Sevilla 2 demo.

decisions.title: FreeDOS DISKCOPY — floppy duplicator and image utility
decisions.reason: Independent DOS diskette duplicator with single/two-drive copy, disk-image operations, extended-memory buffering and bad-sector recovery paths.

decisions.title: SRDISK — resizeable EMS/XMS DOS RAM disk
decisions.reason: Marko Kohtala RAM-disk driver and controller supporting EMS/XMS storage, online resizing and content-preserving FAT/image relocation.

decisions.title: Free Unformat — DOS mirror-based filesystem recovery
decisions.reason: Brian Reifsnyder DOS quick-format recovery implementation with physical/logical sector access and FAT/mirror bookkeeping.

decisions.title: DEVLOAD — load DOS drivers after CONFIG.SYS
decisions.reason: David Woodhouse and Eric Auer dynamic DOS device-driver loader, relocating itself, invoking driver initialization and linking successful drivers into DOS device chains.

decisions.title: FreeDOS APPEND — DOS data-search-path TSR
decisions.reason: Eduardo Casino compatible APPEND implementation, intercepting DOS file-open/search/EXEC calls to extend directory searches with resident and environment-variable support.

decisions.title: RESTAUR — historical DOS BACKUP archive restorer
decisions.reason: Gisbert Selke TapirSoft RESTAUR Pascal implementation decoding and restoring DOS 2.x–4.01 BACKUP archives, preserved alongside FreeDOS BACKUP/RESTORE format-research documentation.

decisions.title: FreeDOS MODE — DOS console and port configuration
decisions.reason: Eric Auer DOS MODE replacement configuring serial/parallel ports, printer redirection, console geometry/fonts, keyboard settings and display codepage operations.

decisions.title: FreeDOS DISPLAY — console and printer codepage driver
decisions.reason: Aitor Santamaria-Merino DOS codepage-management driver implementing generic IOCTL preparation/selection, multiplex handling and EGA/VGA/CGA font backends.

decisions.title: FDSHIELD — DOS resident risky-action blocker
decisions.reason: Eric Auer resident DOS interrupt monitor that blocks selected executable/boot-sector/disk writes and detects attempts to disable legacy antivirus monitors.

decisions.title: FreeDOS NLSFUNC — resident country/codepage service
decisions.reason: Eduardo Casino resident National Language Support service loading country/codepage packages and implementing FreeDOS NLS and IOCTL interfaces.

decisions.title: DiveRace — OS/2 Virtual Pascal 3D driving game
decisions.reason: Michael Mrosowski 1995 DOS-to-OS/2 driving-game port demonstrating DIVE graphics, software 3D transforms, multithreading, palette management and a real-time voice mixer.

decisions.title: The Ultimate OS/2 Game — BattleTech PM source
decisions.reason: Timur Tabi OS/2 Monthly BattleTech/MechWarrior programming-column source with native PM hex maps, BattleMech movement, bitmap sprites, terrain and targeting routines.

decisions.title: SimBlob / BlobCity — native OS/2 environmental simulation
decisions.reason: Amit Patel 1994–1999 OS/2 strategy/environment simulation source, with hex terrain, water/moisture simulation, military units, adjustable pathfinding and multithreaded PM/DIVE rendering.

decisions.title: Ribble — OS/2 Boulder Dash-style game and Watcom port
decisions.reason: J.R. Shannon and D.J. Neades 1993/1994 OS/2 cave puzzle game preserved with a 2026 Open Watcom 32-bit modernization, editor, levels, monster logic and PM interface.

decisions.title: aap PDP-11 — early CPU and Unibus simulators
decisions.reason: Independent implementations of DEC PDP-11/05, /20 and /40 processors, with instruction/state models derived from microcode and schematics, Unibus peripherals and experimental microcoded /40 and /45 models.

decisions.title: retro-205 — Datatron 205 browser emulator
decisions.reason: JavaScript reconstruction of ElectroData/Burroughs decimal drum-memory 205 CPU, supervisory console, Cardatron, magnetic tape and data-file devices; also preserves and reconstructs historical ALGOL compiler materials.

decisions.title: retro-g15 — Bendix G-15D browser emulator
decisions.reason: Browser-based reconstruction of the Bendix G-15D binary drum machine with processor, delay-line registers, front panel, typewriter, paper-tape devices and recovered-software support.

decisions.title: z80pack — 8080/Z80 system simulators
decisions.reason: Mature machine simulator suite for CP/M and Altair, IMSAI, Cromemco, Mostek and Intel development systems, with real 8080/Z80 interpreters, front panels, BIOS sources, assembler and disk utilities.

decisions.title: usim — MIT CADR Lisp machine emulator
decisions.reason: Brad Parker CADR emulator continuation interpreting the actual boot PROM and loaded microcode, with disk, memory, X11 console, Chaos networking and disk/load-band utilities.

decisions.title: Einstein — Apple NewtonOS device emulator
decisions.reason: Long-running Apple Newton emulator with ARM processor/JIT, memory/MMU, display, interrupt, serial/network and PCMCIA emulation plus debugger and cross-platform frontends.

decisions.title: Tek405xEmulator — Tektronix 4051 browser emulator
decisions.reason: JavaScript 6800 CPU and Tektronix 4051 hardware emulation running original ROM images, with vector display, keyboard, GPIB devices and browser-local tape/file storage enhancements.

decisions.title: Research UNIX v7 — Raspberry Pi native port
decisions.reason: Actual historical Research UNIX v7 kernel and userland port to Raspberry Pi, retaining filesystem/process/syscall code with ARM startup, MMU, interrupt and SD-card drivers rather than simulating a PDP-11.

decisions.title: Coherent — Mark Williams OS source archive
decisions.reason: Preservation mirror of historical Mark Williams Coherent kernel, commands, compiler/toolchain and documentation repositories, including 386 kernel source and archival RCS/build files.

decisions.title: IBM650 — independent drum-timed machine simulator

decisions.title: Tek4010 — storage-tube graphics terminal emulator

decisions.title: RJExplorer — CPC M4 file-browser ROM

decisions.title: HippoPlayer Amiga module player

decisions.title: Fireworkz integrated word processor and spreadsheet
decisions.reason: Colton Software Fireworkz and RISC OS Fireworkz Pro source release, combining word processing, spreadsheet evaluation, charting, import/export and native desktop interfaces for RISC OS and Windows.

decisions.title: Puzzles RISC OS native frontend

Includes real gameplay classes, collision/animation logic and multiple console builds, not an emulator wrapper.

decisions.title: SuDokuL
decisions.reason: Original C++ SDL1.2/SDL2 Sudoku game with on-demand puzzle generation, pre-generated harder puzzles, controller/touch/mouse input, saves and scalable graphics. Includes extensive native console build support and its own game-logic implementation; no reverse-engineering origin is claimed.

decisions.title: StoicGoose
decisions.reason: Independent C# WonderSwan/Color emulator with its own V30MZ core, hardware devices and desktop interfaces. A Windows Forms player and Dear ImGui/OpenGL debugger/disassembler share the core; this is reusable console emulation and inspection tooling, not a game-specific runtime.

decisions.title: Holani
decisions.reason: Cycle-stepped Atari Lynx emulator library in Rust, exposing Lynx CPU/bus, cartridge/EEPROM, Mikey display/audio/UART and Suzy sprite/math hardware. Its reusable core serves several separately packaged frontends, rather than embedding emulation for one game.

decisions.title: NitroGrafx
decisions.reason: Long-running reusable PC Engine/TurboGrafx-16 emulator for Nintendo DS-family hardware, with its own native emulation loop, HuC6280 integration, VDC/VCE/PSG state, CD-ROM and Arcade Card handling. Distinct target-specific emulator in FluBBa library family.

decisions.title: JollyCV
decisions.reason: Jolly Good API educational emulator for ColecoVision/Super Game Module, CreatiVision and My Vision, with documented hardware models, memory mapping, state serialization, controller devices and TMS9918/PSG integration. This libretro-hosted source also includes an actual reusable core and JG API build.

decisions.title: ws-test-suite
decisions.reason: Native WonderSwan hardware-behavior and emulator validation test ROM collection, covering CPU quirks, timing, DMA, display, EEPROM, interrupts, sound and RTC, with interactive timing/memory/I/O inspection utilities. Substantial C/assembly tests and own ROM build graph rather than a list of tests elsewhere.

decisions.title: rehover
decisions.reason: Original GameCube/Wii homebrew hovercraft racing project inspired by Diddy Kong Racing. Source includes component-based scenes, controller input, hovercraft behavior, camera/math, graphics/resources and rendering systems. It is an independently written native racer prototype, not a port or Diddy Kong Racing reconstruction.

decisions.title: NitroSwan
decisions.reason: Reusable native Nintendo DS emulator for WonderSwan, Color/Crystal and Benesse PocketChallenge V2, with V30MZ execution, hardware scanline integration, cartridge/EEPROM save states and ROM loading. Its WonderWitch/BootFriend transfer tools also support handheld development workflows.

decisions.title: LineWars II — reconstructed DOS C engine
decisions.reason: The 1994 Safari Software space-combat game reconstructed from its shipped binary into a modular C engine. Flight/combat implementation cites original byte offsets; DOS graphics, cockpit, missions, keyboard, music and sound drivers are present. It targets semantic equivalence rather than byte-identical recompilation.

decisions.title: pcrecomp — reusable PC static recompilation toolbox
decisions.reason: A reusable analysis, disassembly, x86-to-C lifting and runtime toolkit extracted from multiple PC recompilation projects. Includes MZ/NE/LE/PE and NeXTSTEP Mach-O readers; x86-16/32/64 lifters and differential tests; DOS, Win16, Win32-on-POSIX and native32 runtime components. It is infrastructure rather than a game-specific interpreter wrapper.

decisions.title: osFree Janus — Windows 3.0 environment reimplementation
decisions.reason: A separate osFree subproject reimplementing the 16-bit Windows 3.0 environment on DOS/VDM, with kernel, USER, loader, drivers and system components. Source incorporates and adapts Wine, TWIN, ReactOS and HX-DOS code. KRNL286 selector allocation and its Watcom/JWasm build are present, not merely a compatibility proposal.

decisions.title: FamilyAPI — dual-mode DOS and OS/2 API
decisions.reason: Independent osFree Family API implementation for binary dual-mode applications that run without recompilation on DOS and OS/2. Contains KAL, VIO/KBD/MOU, memory/file/NLS, static and dynamic API libraries, and a Wine-derived NE DOS loader.

decisions.title: STris — OS/2 Presentation Manager source continuation
decisions.reason: Continuation of Rene Straub's 1995–1996 Tetris-style OS/2 Presentation Manager game. The maintained 1.50 tree retains the historical playfield engine and adds multilingual UI/help, configurable input, sound and modern Open Watcom builds; legacy source/material is separated.

decisions.title: Brick Blaster — WinEOS source restoration
decisions.reason: Original source of Media Pocket's 1999 Brick Blaster and WinEOS 4.00 Alpha, restored to match the released game by comparing disassemblies. Includes translation-length/coordinate corrections, updated makefiles and narrowly documented compatibility patches for Windows.

decisions.title: Amulets & Armor — original source and maintained ports
decisions.reason: Original open-source release and continued maintenance of the 1997 first-person role-playing game. The large C engine preserves DOS renderer/game/network modules alongside SDL-based native ports and a newly integrated Emscripten target.

decisions.title: KEEN70HZ — reconstructed Keen 4 70-fps patch
decisions.reason: A substantive Commander Keen 4 EGA source modification derived from K1n9_Duk3's reconstructed Keen 4–6 sources. Changes the engine timing/render pipeline to 70-fps operation, adds smooth one-pixel panning options and CRT Terminator synchronization support, while retaining the reconstructed C/assembly game tree.

decisions.title: watcom-game-dev — native DOS VGA game engine
decisions.reason: Native homebrew DOS game-engine framework with VGA Mode 13h double buffering, compiled x86 sprite blitting, Korean/Latin bitmap fonts, PIT timing, keyboard IRQs, OPL2 VGM playback and Sound Blaster PCM mixing. Includes an actual game/smoke-test harness and TypeScript asset tools.

decisions.title: Space Panicco — VMAP editor and PC-98 format research
decisions.reason: Historical archive by an original author augmented with concrete Space Panicco technical analysis and a working browser VMAP level editor. The editor imports/exports the original stage format, paints stage cells and validates playable actor/enemy placement. Promoted for implemented tooling and format analysis, not as recovered game source.

decisions.title: ELRIC — native CGA DOS game
decisions.reason: A native Turbo Pascal DOS action game made for the 2026 CGA Game Jam. Its nine Pascal modules implement timed gameplay, player/enemy behavior, HUD, sprites, scoring, background and menu, using the CGA BGI driver.

decisions.title: DOSBox Cheat Engine — emulated-memory scanner
decisions.reason: A reusable Python-standard-library memory scan/edit/freeze tool for DOSBox Staging's HTTP memory API. A local Python server serves its JavaScript UI, scans memory and maintains cheat tables; it targets arbitrary DOS software rather than wrapping one game.

decisions.title: keen-nes — Commander Keen Galaxy NES port
decisions.reason: A clean-room NES reimplementation of Commander Keen Galaxy episodes 4–6 with a PC-side pipeline extracting the original DOS executable tables, graphics, maps and audio into NES assets. Native C/6502 game code targets MMC5, with rescaled 60-Hz player physics, actor logic, HUD, audio and banked graphics.

decisions.title: Dwarf — Xerox 6085 and Guam Mesa-machine emulator
decisions.reason: Java implementation of the Xerox Mesa machine architecture in two machine profiles: Draco emulates the 6085 Daybreak/Dove and Duchess reconstructs the Guam environment used by GVWin. Implements Mesa CPU, virtual memory, traps, disk/floppy formats, display/input, networking and execution debugging.

decisions.title: apollo — Domain workstation and token-ring emulator
decisions.reason: C23 Apollo Domain family emulator with Motorola 68020/68030/68040 machine profiles, storage controllers and a reconstructed proprietary Apollo token ring. Implements ring framing/MAC/PHY and firmware-visible devices; includes differential/oracle tooling and a substantial test suite.

decisions.title: sgi-emu — SGI Indigo IP12 workstation emulator
decisions.reason: Rust/C++ emulator of original SGI IRIS Indigo IP12, centered on the MIPS R3000A with instruction decoding, MMU/cache/coprocessors, PIC1/HPC1/INT2 devices, SCSI, graphics, network and a Qt debugger UI.

decisions.title: Ecliptic — Tapwave Zodiac native-application emulator
decisions.reason: Reusable high-level execution environment for Tapwave Zodiac native ARM applications. Uses Unicorn for ARM and 68k launch code while reconstructing the 612-entry TwGlue/Palm OS interface, graphics, input, sound, VFS and application callbacks. This is an application-class emulator, not a wrapper for one game.

decisions.title: DateFix — Palm OS calendar-window patch
decisions.reason: Native Palm OS utility that shifts the system calendar epoch/window, converts stored dates with backup, reinstalls after reset and patches date conversion/formatting/select-day APIs on 68k Palm OS 3.5–4.x and ARM Palm OS 5. Source contains separate 68k installer and native ARM patch implementation.

decisions.title: Ridge32 — Ridge workstation emulator
decisions.reason: C# partial reconstruction of Ridge32 workstations with custom 32-bit CPU/instruction decoder, virtual/physical memory, traps, disk controllers, display and a debugger/disassembler. Actual CPU integer/floating instruction dispatch and Priam device sources exist.

decisions.title: IFS — Xerox PUP network services reconstruction
decisions.reason: C# reconstruction of Xerox PARC PUP/Interim File Server protocols: BreathOfLife network boot, EFTP, FTP, CopyDisk disk imaging, time/name service, routing and mail. Serves Alto emulators or real Alto machines using UDP/raw Ethernet and optional BeagleBone interface.

decisions.title: CTSS — recovered and corrected operating-system sources
decisions.reason: Recovered Compatible Time-Sharing System source tree cleaned against historical listings. Contains FAP/MAD operating-system, filesystem/loader, commands, libraries and tools plus tape/disk staging and SIMH boot instructions, rather than documentation-only preservation.

decisions.title: Centurion — CPU-6 minicomputer emulator
decisions.reason: C emulator reconstructing Centurion CPU-6 and known peripherals from Eldorado EE200 material, diagnostics and reverse-engineering discoveries. Includes CPU/MMU/DMA/interrupt state, scheduler, disks, mux, disassembler and CBIN loader.

decisions.title: z390 — mainframe assembler and runtime environment
decisions.reason: Java mainframe programming environment implementing HLASM-compatible macro assembly, linkage editing, zCOBOL compilation and a runtime emulator with QSAM/VSAM/CICS services. Substantial assembler, processor and service implementations, macro libraries and regression tests exist.

decisions.title: M-20 — Soviet mainframe simulator
decisions.reason: C/SIMH-based reusable simulator of Soviet M-20 45-bit mainframe with machine arithmetic, memory, card reader/punch, drum, tape and printer devices, Russian/English frontends and media/autocode tools.

decisions.title: ROPE — IBM 1401 programming and simulation IDE
decisions.reason: Java Swing integrated development and simulation environment for IBM 1401. Combines source editing, Autocoder invocation, SIMH process control, execution/breakpoints, memory/console/printout views and timer/UI support; original frontend source is maintained separately from bundled external engines.

decisions.title: Py1620 — IBM 1620 Model 1 emulator
decisions.reason: Python implementation of IBM 1620 Model 1 decimal CPU with 20,000-digit default memory, flag bits, instruction execution, card-file and typewriter I/O, CMEM loading and built-in debugger. Supports varied historic programs and compiler/assembler workflows rather than a game-specific wrapper.

decisions.title: Konami's Synthesizer — MSX commented disassembly
decisions.reason: Reconstruction of Konami's 1986 RC-741 MSX software synthesizer, including the annotated 32 KB Z80 listing, DAC output timing, tone engine and tape-data formats. This is a non-game application disassembly with supporting Python research tools.

decisions.title: Hole in One — MSX commented disassembly
decisions.reason: Annotated recovery of HAL Laboratory's 1984 16 KB MSX golf cartridge. Includes address-anchored names/notes, executable Z80 listing and Python reconstruction of course maps, scripts and compression.

decisions.title: Casio World Open — MSX commented disassembly
decisions.reason: Annotated Z80 recovery of Casio's 1985 32 KB MSX golf cartridge, with address-stable analysis notes and course/3D rendering tools derived from the ROM.

decisions.title: 3D Golf Simulation — MSX BASIC source recovery
decisions.reason: Recovery of T&E Soft's 1983 Normal Edition golf cartridge as a 246-line tokenized MSX BASIC program, with complete line commentary, course-data decoding and a retokenizer. It contains no game Z80 machine code.

decisions.title: Parodius — MSX banked-ROM disassembly
decisions.reason: Full sixteen-bank Z80 disassembly of Konami's 1988 RC-759 Parodius MSX cartridge. Includes bank-aware tracing, labeled code/data and ROM-derived graphics, text and audio reconstruction.

decisions.title: Kaypro — ROM, BIOS and CONFIG disassemblies
decisions.reason: Annotated recovery of multiple Kaypro II/IV boot ROMs, CP/M BIOS revisions, CONFIG utilities and character generators, with original images, assembly listings and binary-comparison scripts.

decisions.title: RODOS — CPC disk-ROM reconstruction and fixes
decisions.reason: Disassembly of Romantic Robot RODOS 2.19 for Amstrad CPC, developed into relocatable, bug-fixed RODOS 2.22. Includes annotated ROM source, debug commands, test disks and release/build machinery.

decisions.title: Space Raiders — Spectrum SkoolKit disassembly
decisions.reason: SkoolKit reconstruction of Psion's 1982 ZX Spectrum Space Raiders, including annotated game listing, control/reference files, snapshot input and recipes for documentation, assembly and runnable TAP output.

decisions.title: Topo Soft logo animation — MSX disassembly
decisions.reason: Annotated Z80 disassembly of the first MSX Topo Soft cassette-loading logo animation, with decoded graphics attributes/self-modifying code and cassette wrapper source.

decisions.title: Dino Eggs — C64 annotated disassembly
decisions.reason: Commodore 64 Dino Eggs recovery with extensively labeled 6510 assembly, hardware constants, original PRG/disk images and separate disk-protection/error-check build options.

decisions.title: ISX — ISIS-II emulator disassembly and P112 port
decisions.reason: Recovery of the CP/M ISX.COM ISIS-II compatibility environment, plus modified BDOS and Z80182 P112 BIOS needed to run Intel development tools. Includes disassembly, system-image build scripts, utilities and floppy-image data.

decisions.title: disasm6502 — Rust 6502 analysis library
decisions.reason: Reusable Rust crate for 6502 binary disassembly with undocumented opcodes, addressing modes, cycle counts, register-use and status-flag metadata. Source includes complete opcode model and tests.

decisions.title: xasm65 — Swift 6502 disassembler library
decisions.reason: Swift library and macOS command-line tool for MOS 6502 assembly analysis, including label/comment-aware disassembly, opcode definitions, Woz Monitor fixtures and an unfinished assembler parser.

decisions.title: XSP X68000 sprite management library
decisions.reason: A native X680x0 sprite-management system by Yosshin, used in Cho Ren Sha 68K and other games. Its raster-time sprite doubler supports up to 512 displayed sprites, dynamic PCG assignment over 32768 patterns and triple buffering. This is the reusable assembly library, not a Cho Ren Sha port or CPU wrapper.

decisions.title: FTX X68000 text-plane font library
decisions.reason: A native X680x0 text-plane renderer by Yosshin for 8x8 and 16x16 sixteen-color fonts, including sprite-PCG-to-font conversion and palette/scroll operations. The published assembly implementation and C examples preserve a library originating in 1994.

decisions.title: gdbserver-x68k
decisions.reason: A Human68k remote-debugging server derived from bet4it/gdbserver, adapted to m68k programs built with elf2x68k. It runs the X-format target on X680x0 and serves GDB over serial, with exception/register/process control and pthread-aware thread support. Native debugger software rather than an emulator.

decisions.title: SectorC68k
decisions.reason: A m68k re-expression of xorvoid SectorC: a 512-byte C-subset compiler that runs on X68000 and emits native m68k instructions. It contains token parsing, expression and control-flow compilation, branch fixups and direct instruction emission, plus examples and a test harness.

decisions.title: kata68k X68000 native game collection
decisions.reason: An author-maintained collection of X68000 games sharing a C/68000-assembly hardware and asset framework: BINGO de PRO-68k, Ball und Panzer Golf/BattleKata, Over Kata racing, Suikata ball-merging and X68ZKeeper match-three. Kept as one collection record to avoid inflating shared-engine directory paths into separate projects.

decisions.title: xtracker X68000 music tracker
decisions.reason: A native X68000 FM music-tracker/editor implementation. Its C sources implement phrase editing, pattern rendering, channel commands, playback timing and OPM-register updates; it is a tracker application rather than a desktop MDX decoder or emulator.

decisions.title: smbfs / smbclient for X68000
decisions.reason: A Human68k SMB filesystem driver, mount tool and interactive client using libsmb2. It translates Human68k filesystem request packets into remote share operations, manages directory/file handles and converts Shift-JIS/UTF-8 names, making network shares available as native drives.

decisions.title: x68kserremote
decisions.reason: A native Human68k remote-drive driver paired with a Windows/macOS serial service. It exposes the connected host filesystem over RS-232C/UART with request packets, cached reads/writes and directory operations, emulating the practical host-drive facilities available in X68000 emulators.

decisions.title: xdfboot
decisions.reason: A native X680x0 utility that loads XDF floppy images outside the configured usable memory and patches boot-time ROM access to boot directly from those RAM-resident images. Includes original C image/SRAM control and 68000 ROM-patching code, not an emulator wrapper.

decisions.title: joynetd Ethernet Joy-kun driver
decisions.reason: A Human68k network driver for a W5500-based Ethernet adapter connected through the X680x0 joystick port. It provides a Keisoku Giken inetd-compatible socket/control interface and DHCP support through original driver and bit-banged hardware access implementation.

decisions.title: SQLite3 for X68000
decisions.reason: A lightweight SQLite3 port to Human68k, combining upstream amalgamation with a custom stdio-backed VFS, OS-bridge stubs, compact SQL shell and disk-backed UTF-8/Shift-JIS conversion. Supplies native static-library and MicroPython wrapper integration as well as the command-line application.

decisions.title: CCres RISC OS resource converter
decisions.reason: Dave Appleby and John Tytgat resource converter for Acorn RISC OS. It reads and writes Toolbox Resource RESF v1.00/v1.01 and Wimp Template binary files through editable text, with class/gadget/icon reconstruction and relocation handling. Includes native desktop front end and portable command-line build.

decisions.title: Grab II RISC OS system sprite grabber
decisions.reason: Chris Bazley native RISC OS Toolbox application that extracts the Window Manager ROM/RAM sprite pools or window-tool sprites into valid Sprite files. Replaces Dave Thomas original Grab with a fresh implementation and fixes sparse/invalid sprite-area layouts when saving.

decisions.title: Conway-Macintosh
decisions.reason: A native classic 68000 Macintosh Conway Game of Life application written in modern C++ and built using Retro68. Includes cell-field state updates, compact bit matrices, QuickDraw-oriented grid renderers, window/event handling and buttons.

decisions.title: Mesen 2
decisions.reason: Multi-system emulator with C++ console/hardware implementations and a C# desktop/debugger interface. The selected SourMesen repository is the archived roughly-2.1.1 mid-2025 codebase; its pinned README redirects ongoing development to MesenCE. One Mesen lineage record is proposed, not a separate count for the successor.

decisions.title: jgenesis
decisions.reason: Independent Rust multi-console emulator organized into reusable CPU, console backend, renderer, GUI, debugger and web crates. Implements Sega 8/16-bit systems and expansions plus Nintendo consoles and PC Engine; not a game-specific wrapper.

decisions.title: jsSMS
decisions.reason: JavaScript Sega Master System/Game Gear emulator evolved from a JavaGear port into an optimizing dynamic recompiler. Includes explicit bytecode parsing, control-flow analysis, AST generation and optimization and generates executable JavaScript functions for arbitrary loaded ROMs.

decisions.title: SMS Plus — standalone reference port
decisions.reason: Modernized standalone Charles MacDonald SMS Plus lineage, intended as a small reference Sega Master System/Game Gear emulator for homebrew and emulator developers. Contains actual CPU, memory, VDP, sound and shell source.

decisions.title: MasterEmu
decisions.reason: C-language Android Master System/Game Gear emulator by Phil Potter with Java Android UI and native SDL-based emulation. The published cleaned-up open-source project includes its own substantial Z80 instruction implementation rather than only calling an external console core.

decisions.title: crater
decisions.reason: Independent C Sega Game Gear emulator with built-in Z80 assembler and disassembler, written as a learning and hardware-development reference project. Includes tests for CPU, graphics, assembly/disassembly and integration.

decisions.title: Sandopolis
decisions.reason: Portable Zig multi-system Sega emulator integrating native hardware scheduling, video/audio, memory and reusable external CPU cores. Supports Genesis, Sega CD, Master System, Game Gear and SG-1000 with desktop, web and libretro frontends.

decisions.title: Rustual Boy
decisions.reason: Rust Virtual Boy emulator with reusable core, middleware and a command-line frontend/debugger. Implements V810 CPU, display and sound devices and supports arbitrary commercial or homebrew ROM inputs.

decisions.title: Red Viper
decisions.reason: Virtual Boy emulator native to Nintendo 3DS, continuing r3Ddragon/Reality Boy/Red Dragon with a V810 dynamic recompiler, busywait detection and hardware-accelerated stereo rendering. Selected as the active representative of that lineage.

decisions.title: VirtualFriend
decisions.reason: Independent Rust Virtual Boy emulator designed for Apple Vision Pro, with Swift Apple-platform integration and an additional Rust desktop frontend. Core explicitly models V810 state, bus activity, timing and interrupts.

decisions.title: Handy/SDL
decisions.reason: Portable Atari Lynx emulator from Keith Wilkins Handy through SDLEMU, with a modern SDL2 renderer, GUI, controller input, settings and ComLynx networking. One representative of the Handy core/SDL lineage is proposed.

decisions.title: Oswan — OpenDingux port
decisions.reason: Oswan WonderSwan/Color emulator port for OpenDingux and Windows, containing NEC V30MZ CPU, video, APU, input and cartridge/file implementations with a handheld UI. Selected representative of the Oswan lineage, rather than counting each downstream port.

decisions.title: v64tng — The 7th Guest engine and semantic disassembly
decisions.reason: Native C++23 re-creation of The 7th Guest engine with GRV scripting, VDX decoding, puzzle logic and separate preservation disassemblies for DOS, Win32, Classic Mac and CD-i players.

decisions.title: Wing Commander II — Kilrathi Saga reconstruction and SDL2 port
decisions.reason: Recovered C game core and C++ ix audio library for the 1996 Kilrathi Saga Win32 Wing Commander II, with modern SDL2 port and comparison tooling.

decisions.title: Fire & Forget II — DOS reconstruction and SDL2/Web port
decisions.reason: Function-by-function C11 transliteration of the DOS/EGA racer engine, recovered game tables and wave/music virtual machines, with native SDL2 and WebAssembly outputs.

decisions.title: LIBC Next — OS/2 C runtime
decisions.reason: Maintained kLIBC-0.6 lineage fork implementing Unix-compatible C runtime facilities on OS/2, with its own DLL/version identity and backward ABI/API compatibility.

decisions.title: Odin32 — Win32 API implementation for OS/2
decisions.reason: Preserved Odin32 compatibility-layer source, here in a branch aimed at SWT/OS2 and Eclipse with Win32 API libraries, loader/runtime integration and test applications.

decisions.title: Doszip Commander — DOS and Windows file manager
decisions.reason: LFN-aware Norton Commander-style TUI file manager with built-in Zip/UnZip, editor, panel and file operation source for 16-bit DOS and modern Windows.

decisions.title: Neetan — Japanese computer and PC/AT emulator
decisions.reason: Rust multi-system emulator for PC-98/9821, PC-88/88VA, PC-6001, MSX, FM Towns/FM7, Sharp X68000/X1 and IBM PC/AT.

decisions.title: PM123 — OS/2 audio player
decisions.reason: Native OS/2 Presentation Manager audio player with plugin playback/decoding infrastructure, playlists, audio controls and historical source distribution/build documentation.

decisions.title: FAT32 — OS/2 filesystem driver
decisions.reason: Preserved native OS/2/eComStation FAT32 installable filesystem driver and UFAT32 support DLL source, attributed to Henk Kelder and netlabs.

decisions.title: AE — OS/2 Pascal E.EXE replacement
decisions.reason: Aaron Lawrence native Pascal/OS2 graphical text editor with find/replace, printing, autosave and language resources, preserved as original source.

decisions.title: eFTE2 — OS/2 folding text editor
decisions.reason: OS/2 continuation of the eFTE/FTE folding editor with text buffers, syntax highlighting, configuration and native console/PM integration.

decisions.title: p50em — Prime 50-Series system emulator
decisions.reason: Jim Wilcoxson's independent C emulation of Prime 50-Series minicomputers, with disk/MAGSAV boot, R-mode save-image loading, peripheral support, tracing and PRIMOS operation.

decisions.title: em50 — Prime 50-Series emulator
decisions.reason: Jan Jaeger's separately authored Prime 50-Series implementation, with CPU instruction groups, disk/tape, AMLC networking, configuration and debugger support.

decisions.title: Meroko — TI Explorer 1 hardware emulator
decisions.reason: Preserved Daniel Seagraves hardware-level Texas Instruments Explorer 1 emulator, including Raven microcoded CPU, NuBus, memory, NUPI storage, SIB display/input and SDL frontend.

decisions.title: PDP-8 Emulator for iPad — Codea implementation
decisions.reason: Robert Martin's Lua/Codea implementation of a 4K-word, 12-bit PDP-8 with interactive front panel, ASR-33 teletype, paper-tape reader/punch, debugger-like controls and historical tape programs.

decisions.title: pdp11-js — Takahiro's browser PDP-11/40 emulator
decisions.reason: JavaScript PDP-11/40 system emulator with MMU, registers, clock, terminal, RK05 disk model, disassembler and debug UI; loads and exports disk-image buffers and is documented running Unix V6.

decisions.title: js-pdp11 — aiju's browser system emulator
decisions.reason: Compact, independent browser PDP-11 emulator implementing kernel/user registers and memory mapping, traps, interrupts, console and RK05 disk I/O, with a disassembler and runnable Unix-oriented HTML frontend.

decisions.title: pdp10-js — DECsystem-10 KI10 browser emulator
decisions.reason: Paul Nankervis's JavaScript 36-bit DECsystem-10 KI10 emulator, with floating-point, device I/O, front-panel controls, diagnostics and RP03 disk configuration for TOPS-10 v6.03A.

decisions.title: UKNCBTL — UKNC Back to Life emulator
decisions.reason: Substantial C++ Win32 emulator/debugger for the Soviet Elektronika MS-0511 UKNC dual-processor educational machine, with CPU/PPU, memory controllers, video, disks, tapes, sound, disassembly and console debugging.

decisions.title: Burroughs B1700 Emulator — microcode machine and tools
decisions.reason: C++20 implementation of the B1710 microinstruction processor and B1700 bit-addressable architecture, paired with microcode debugger/disassembler, MIL and S-language assemblers and a historical tape reader.

decisions.title: B500Emulator — Burroughs B500 browser implementation
decisions.reason: Browser-based reconstruction of the Burroughs B500 decimal/BCD computer, with processor operations, console panel, asynchronous worker execution, card/printer/tape I/O and a disk module.

decisions.title: Unix V4/V5/V6/V7 Resurrection — recovered Unix and browser environment
decisions.reason: Source-preservation and browser integration project for Research Unix V4 through V7, combining recovered historical C/PDP-11 source and media with an educational TypeScript frontend, source overlays and a Paul Nankervis PDP-11 bridge.

decisions.title: Nova — Go Data General minicomputer emulator
decisions.reason: Jeremy Hall's Go implementation of the 16-bit Data General Nova CPU, interrupt/device framework, console, clock, loaders and disassembler, with instruction/logic tests and example command tools.

decisions.title: Stars — Amstrad CPC star-field demo
decisions.reason: Interactive native CPC star-field demo by Diego Freniche, with separate entity lifecycle, star generation, directional physics and rendering systems; includes keyboard direction and hyperspace effects.

decisions.title: Spectrum Workbench — Rust Spectrum debugger and assembler
decisions.reason: Reusable ZX Spectrum 48K workbench containing its own machine-cycle Z80 core/disassembler, Spectrum memory and ULA/tape/audio model, source-level debugger, macro assembler and desktop/CLI frontends.

decisions.title: ZQLoader — Spectrum audio turbo loader
decisions.reason: Host-side tape/snapshot conversion and playback tool paired with a native Z80 turbo-loader for real Spectrum 48K/128K machines. Handles TAP/TZX/snapshots, pulse generation, WAV output, compression and optional Qt UI.

decisions.title: Spectrum Game Compressor
decisions.reason: Reusable batch and Z80 loader pipeline that extracts game blocks, rearranges/crops SCREEN$ data, compresses with ZX0, and packages replacement compressed TAP/TZX or disk loaders. Per-game configurations and multilevel disk loaders are included.

decisions.title: Miss Input 2 — Amstrad CPC platform game
decisions.reason: Native Z80 assembly sequel for CPC 464 by Daniel Saura Martínez and Enrique Vidal Cayuela. Contains modular game/menu/entity managers, collision and physics systems, power-ups, sprites, level maps and Arkos music assets.

decisions.title: Miss Input — Amstrad CPC platform game
decisions.reason: Original 2019 native CPC game by Enrique Vidal Cayuela and Daniel Saura Martínez, with Z80 player/entity/enemy logic, keyboard/game state loop, sprite animation and two dozen Tiled maps.

decisions.title: Robobit — CPC 464 game
decisions.reason: Native CPC 464 game created for an Automatic Reasoning course and CPCRetroDev 2016 by Cristina Rivera, Miguel Sancho and Fernando Verdejo, with map-based movement, enemies, knives, scoring and custom pathfinding.

decisions.title: Riichi Mahjong — BBC Micro
decisions.reason: Native BBC Micro four-player Riichi Mahjong implementation in one substantial BeebAsm source, with Mode 7 tile display, human controls, computer opponents, scoring and practice hints.

decisions.title: Androidz Redux — BBC Micro remaster
decisions.reason: Stephen Scott’s remaster of his 1993 BBC Micro arcade game, retaining BBC BASIC source while upgrading from MODE 5 to MODE 2, graphics/sound, bugs and late-level difficulty. Includes a BeebAsm disk-packaging script.

decisions.title: BBC 6502 Web Assembler
decisions.reason: Self-contained JavaScript browser assembler/editor with symbolic two-pass NMOS 6502 assembly, undocumented opcodes, multiple sources and ORG regions, listing/symbol output and bootable BBC DFS SSD generation.

decisions.title: Scorch — Atari 8-bit artillery game
decisions.reason: Long-running native 6502 Scorched Earth-style multiplayer artillery game by Tomasz Pecko and Pawel Kalinowski, with deformable terrain, weapon shop, computer opponents, POKEY audio and Atari 5200 support plus a work-in-progress C64 port.

decisions.title: Bananaland (!Ba) recovered sources
decisions.reason: Recovered 1990–1992 SICK graphics/music demo, preserving a byte-exact RISC OS source tree and readable BBC BASIC V with inline ARM2 assembler. This is source restoration of the released v2.02 demo, recovered from PackDir SCSI-drive backups, not a new emulation wrapper.

decisions.title: Tertis recovered sources
decisions.reason: Recovered final 1993 working tree of SICK !Tertis v2.05, including original application, assets, source/build scripts and readable detokenised sources. A distinct game from the authors’ Bananaland demo.

decisions.title: RISC OS disc recovery tools
decisions.reason: Three standalone modern Python tools recover BBC BASIC V text, PackDir archives, and ADFS floppy images from Acorn RISC OS media. Implementation handles inline ARM assembler tokens, line-number references, LZW, metadata and load/execute address preservation.

decisions.title: System Interrupt Demo V recovered source
decisions.reason: Preservation collection of System Interrupt demos I–V with actual recovered BBC BASIC/inline ARM implementation for Demo V v1.01, dated 5 February 1989. Only Demo V qualifies as source recovery; I–IV are contextual released binaries.

decisions.title: !ARCbbs source archive
decisions.reason: Author-released source recovery of Hugo Fiennes’s Archimedes bulletin-board software, last used around 1994. Substantive server, file/mailbase, transfer protocols, editors and ARM modules survive with historical Acorn build scripts.

decisions.title: X68000 BDIF format tools
decisions.reason: Reverse-engineered specification, Python parser/applier and encoder for K. Higashide’s 1992 BdifSet .bfd binary patch format. Recovered from disassembly of Human68k 68000 binaries, with bidirectional delta operations and CRC handling implemented.

decisions.title: FDFORMAT / FDFORMAT2
decisions.reason: X68000 floppy formatter lineage: original personal utility preserved in fdformat and redesigned FDFORMAT2 implements parallel per-drive state machines, physical formatting, BPB/FAT/root-directory/minimal-IPL logical formatting and sector sliding. Represented as one project lineage.

decisions.title: depace Macintosh PACE analysis tools
decisions.reason: Python decryption and patching implementation for early Macintosh PACE-protected software, explaining on-the-fly self-modifying decryption, bad-block floppy checks and debugger/timing checks. Multiple per-title scripts recover inspectable 68000 program bytes and alter protection checks.

decisions.title: miniscsi Macintosh SCSI driver
decisions.reason: Compact native Macintosh boot disk driver implemented in C with m68k assembly entry/header shim. Implements Apple partition scanning, registering/mounting HFS volumes, SCSI READ(10)/chunked WRITE(10), DriveStatus and drive icon in a position-independent raw driver.

decisions.title: ClaudeLander
decisions.reason: Clean-room C++20/raylib reconstruction of Lander behavior using Mark Moxon’s annotated Archimedes ARM analysis as specification. Implements terrain, ship dynamics, mouse polar control, rendering and collision rather than executing an embedded original CPU.

decisions.title: Freecell68k
decisions.reason: Native classic Macintosh FreeCell homebrew with full C game rules, deterministic Microsoft-compatible numbered deals, undo and Toolbox window/menu/event handling. Original source implementation, not claimed decompilation.

decisions.title: Pendulum68k
decisions.reason: Classic Macintosh native pendulum simulator with C numerical integration, configurable angle/velocity/resistance/length/gravity, Toolbox event handling, preferences dialogs and drawing. Original homebrew application, not source reconstruction.

decisions.title: Super Bomberman — SNES disassembly and asset rebuild
decisions.reason: Regional Super Bomberman reconstruction with a remade source/asset build, decoded graphics, levels, DBoot songs and samples, plus bugfix/debug configurations. This is the original SNES game, not an emulator wrapper.

decisions.title: Shin Megami Tensei — SNES J1.0 annotated disassembly
decisions.reason: Work-in-progress annotated reconstruction of Japanese v1.0, including banked CPU code, reset/WRAM logic, symbols and a substantial independently decoded SPC sound engine.

decisions.title: SimCity — SNES reconstruction
decisions.reason: Game-specific SNES disassembly in Yoshifanatic1’s ROM framework, with its own bank/routine macros, native memory maps, SPC audio engine and original-ROM asset extraction/reassembly workflow. CPU reset/main/NMI routines and explicit compressed SPC engine are present; only USA supported despite generic multi-region menu entries.

decisions.title: Wario’s Woods — SNES reconstruction
decisions.reason: Game-specific SNES disassembly in Yoshifanatic1’s ROM framework, with its own bank/routine macros, native memory maps, SPC audio engine and original-ROM asset extraction/reassembly workflow. Read native CPU register initialization, bank macros and SPC source. Only USA ROM map exists; extraction explicitly rejects PAL despite assembly menu scaffolding.

decisions.title: Spider-Man & the X-Men in Arcade’s Revenge — SNES reconstruction
decisions.reason: Game-specific SNES disassembly in Yoshifanatic1’s ROM framework, with its own bank/routine macros, native memory maps, SPC audio engine and original-ROM asset extraction/reassembly workflow. Read native reset, lives/level-state initialization and bank reconstruction. USA is the documented supported release.

decisions.title: Pac-Man 2: The New Adventures — SNES reconstruction
decisions.reason: Game-specific SNES disassembly in Yoshifanatic1’s ROM framework, with its own bank/routine macros, native memory maps, SPC audio engine and original-ROM asset extraction/reassembly workflow. Large bank/routine source, text tables and decoded SPC engine are present. Only USA map/extraction supported; JP/EU/French/German assembly menu options are framework scaffolding, not evidence of completed support.

decisions.title: Keitai Denjuu Telefang — Power/Speed GBC disassembly
decisions.reason: Partial multi-version disassembly of the creature-collecting RPG, with extensive reconstructed system, battle, script and graphics components. English translation lives on a separate patch branch; this record reviews the default source branch.

decisions.title: Network Adventure Bugsite — Alpha/Beta GBC disassembly
decisions.reason: Partial two-version reconstruction of Network Adventure Bugsite with reconstructed bytecode VM, game filesystem, window manager, text and banking components, plus Python format/assembly utilities.

decisions.title: Kirby’s Tilt ’n’ Tumble — GBC bank disassembly
decisions.reason: Bank-by-bank RGBDS disassembly of the original accelerometer-based GBC title, with native reset/interrupt vectors, header, all 64 assembly banks and checksum manifests.

decisions.title: Flipull — Game Boy US/JP disassembly
decisions.reason: Annotated partial disassembly of the compact, mapperless Game Boy puzzle game; regional assembly generates US and Japanese ROMs and supports study of the level-49 kill screen.

decisions.title: Harvest Moon 3 — translation-oriented GBC reconstruction
decisions.reason: Deliberately partial source reconstruction sufficient for translation, including text engine, HUD, status screen and save routines. German translation with variable-width font lives on de branch and is not the reviewed default branch.

decisions.title: GB Disassembly Tools — shared pret analysis and asset utilities
decisions.reason: Standalone shared tooling extracted from Pokémon disassemblies, with RGBDS map parsing/free-space analysis, source/symbol utilities and 1bpp/2bpp-to-PNG asset conversion.

decisions.title: PSY-Q libraries — matching PlayStation SDK reconstruction
decisions.reason: Matching decompilation of original PlayStation SDK libraries, with substantive reconstructed sound sequencing, SPU and compression functions, version-conditional implementations and object/library comparison infrastructure.

decisions.title: Legend of Mana — matching PSX US/JP reconstruction
decisions.reason: Readable C reconstruction of original Legend of Mana main executable and 17 overlays for US and Japan. Pinned README claims full byte-identical links and recompressed overlay binaries for both releases, while original SDK library assembly is retained.

decisions.title: 2ine — OS/2 executable loader for Linux
decisions.reason: Ryan C. Gordon’s independent OS/2 compatibility implementation loads OS/2 NE/LX executables and maps their APIs to Linux libraries. Pinned lx_loader.c validates modules and native/doscalls.c implements OS/2 calls; this is substantive reusable compatibility software.

decisions.title: WarCraft: Refurbished — DOS executable enhancement patches
decisions.reason: Joel Ek’s unofficial patch project for Blizzard’s WarCraft: Orcs & Humans. Actual JavaScript patch definitions contain version-specific x86 addresses and assembly bytes; the C DOS patcher checks, applies and restores binary slices.

decisions.title: RSXNTDJ — preserved DJGPP Windows toolchain and IDE
decisions.reason: Preserved RSXNTDJ 1.5.1 source distribution, including Win32 runtime/startup code, GCC wrapper, libraries, RSXIDE and examples. gccw32.c configures RSXNTDJ includes/libraries and invokes GCC; rsxide.c implements project and target handling.

decisions.title: PMD — original PC-98 music driver, compiler and player sources
decisions.reason: M. Kajihara’s Professional Music Driver source release, preserved in a mirror. Includes PMD sound drivers, MC music compiler, PMP player and IBM-PC variants. Actual PMD.ASM playback initialization and OPTASM/OPTLINK build batches were inspected.

decisions.title: Win16 reverse engineering tools — segment mapping and OPTLOADER unpacking
decisions.reason: Reusable Python tools for Windows 3.1 binary research: derive NE segment maps from DOSBox memory, convert CPU coverage into IDA/Lighthouse addresses, and reconstruct OPTLOADER-compressed executables. optloader.py contains an explicit modeled loader and decompression logic.

decisions.title: Win16Tools — Windows 3.x diagnostics and compatibility utilities
decisions.reason: Japheth’s source collection of DOSAlloc, DosMonW, GDIStat, Notify, SetMode and Share. Inspected implementation reads USER/GDI heap status and hooks DOS calls, with C++ UI and 16-bit assembly sources.

decisions.title: HTTPd16 — native Windows 3.11 web server
decisions.reason: Josh Patterson’s native retro-developed Windows 3.11 HTTP server. C++ Winsock implementation binds/listens from XML configuration, with a custom segmented-memory manager and static-file server UI.

decisions.title: PC98src — onion software original PC-98 sources
decisions.reason: Onitama/onion software’s original NEC PC-9801 archive contains historical games, BASIC sources, C utilities, Advanced SOUP compiler and assembly graphics routines. Inspected Crazy World BASIC gameplay, ASC C compiler entry/parser setup and .8086 graphics-bank assembly.

decisions.title: Cyberdogs — original DOS Pascal source
decisions.reason: Ronny Wester’s circa-1994 Cyberdogs source release, preserved in LibreGamesArchive. dogs.pas contains the application and mission flow; game.pas implements movement, collisions, enemies and bullets, with source units for input, graphics and sound.

decisions.title: osFree Janus PIF Editor — restored Qualitas Win16 application
decisions.reason: Restored and adapted Qualitas PIF editor for osFree Janus. Original 1992/1993 C source implements standard/advanced PIF property UI and binary PIF loading/saving.

decisions.title: osFree Janus System Editor — restored Qualitas MAXEdit
decisions.reason: Qualitas MAXEdit configuration-file editor source adapted as Janus System Editor. Actual historical C source implements MDI document windows, configuration paths and INI/PRO editing.

decisions.title: osFree Janus Notepad — Wine-derived native Win16 editor
decisions.reason: Self-contained native Windows 3.x Notepad adaptation derived from Wine Notepad. C source implements file operations, editor state and Win16 API integration; README explicitly describes removal of Win32-specific dependencies.

decisions.title: osFree Janus Clock — Wine-derived native Win16 clock
decisions.reason: Wine Clock adapted to native Windows 3.x for Janus. Actual C drawing code creates analog hands/ticks and digital/time display; repository includes its own resources and makefile.

decisions.title: Liberty — preserved Palm OS Game Boy emulator
decisions.reason: Aaron Ardiri and Michael Ethetton's Liberty 1.3.1 source archive preserves a reusable original Game Boy emulator written for Palm handhelds, including 68k CPU/video/sound code and a ROM-to-PDB converter.

decisions.title: ApPalm II — native Palm OS Apple II emulator
decisions.reason: Hilary Cheng and David Schmenk's Apple II/IIe emulator for Palm PDAs combines a substantial hand-written 68k 6502 interpreter, memory-mapped Apple I/O, video and disk-image conversion tools.

decisions.title: Phoinix — native Palm OS Game Boy emulator
decisions.reason: Bodo Wenzel's formerly PalmBoy Game Boy emulator source is preserved with a 68k execution core, video/memory implementation, VFS, saved states and multilingual Palm resources.

decisions.title: u1100 tools — UNIVAC 1100 disk-image inspection
decisions.reason: The implemented portion of Patrick Barron's planned UNIVAC 1100 emulator is a usable C image-inspection toolkit. uimage2strings unpacks paired 36-bit words from disk-pack images and decodes 9-bit ASCII or 6-bit FIELDATA for external analysis.

decisions.title: Angular PDP-1 — browser machine emulator
decisions.reason: A reusable TypeScript PDP-1 interpreter with 18-bit memory/registers, instruction groups, console switches, paper-tape loading and vector display, presented through an Angular front panel.

decisions.title: retro-LGP21 — LGP-21 browser system emulator
decisions.reason: Paul Kimpel's detailed General Precision LGP-21 implementation reconstructs the processor, rotating fixed-head disk memory, arithmetic mechanisms, control panel, Flexowriter and Tally paper-tape devices from machine manuals.

decisions.title: SEL810 — emulator and paper-tape analysis suite
decisions.reason: Kenneth Gober's C# SEL 810 suite includes a substantial processor/memory/console model, TCP peripheral links, tape server, BASIC tape construction, loader-aware tape dumper and control-flow-assisted disassembler.

decisions.title: TRIPOS — preserved multiarchitecture operating-system sources
decisions.reason: Historical TRIPOS BCPL operating-system and tool sources shared with permission from Tim King, covering the shell and utilities plus Nova, PDP-11, LSI4 and Motorola 68000 assembly/compiler support. This is the historical lineage underlying early AmigaDOS, not an AmigaDOS replacement.

decisions.title: Elliott 803 — operator-console system emulator
decisions.reason: Peter Onon's Elliott 803 emulator models 39-bit arithmetic and processor operations alongside an unusually physical operator experience: charger, contactor, hours-run counter, sound and console wiring.

decisions.title: EDSAC — command-line emulator and replica-support tools
decisions.reason: Andrew Herbert's maintained extension of Lee Wittenberg's EDSAC emulator implements machine orders/arithmetic and tape-style I/O, adding tracing, binary store upload and execution limits for the EDSAC Replica Project.

decisions.title: Dersch PDP-8 — compact Python machine emulator
decisions.reason: Josh Dersch's independently written Python implementation of a standard 4K-word PDP-8 includes instruction dispatch, memory, console Teletype and paper-tape loading; it is broader than a single program wrapper.

decisions.title: Fast Assembler 1.8
decisions.reason: Maintained native 6502 assembler for SpartaDOS X and BW-DOS, restoring Marek Goderski's historical Fast Assembler and adding parser, arithmetic, diagnostics and memory-management fixes. Reviewed FAMAIN's multi-pass assembly driver and FAPARSE implementation establish substantive tooling.

decisions.title: VARIUS
decisions.reason: Original native Atari sliding-tile puzzle from ABBUC 2021: combines colored tiles, with deterministic progression rather than a random generator. Inspected INCMAIN initializes GTIA colors, input and game transitions; the source set includes Atari computer and 5200 entry points.

decisions.title: Kermit-65 for Atari
decisions.reason: Historical Atari Kermit terminal and reliable-transfer implementation maintained in ca65-compatible source. Its large implementation documents Apple-to-C64-to-Atari ancestry, Atari CIO/850 I/O conversion and decades of transfer and terminal fixes, rather than only shipping binaries.

decisions.title: Night Knight Atari
decisions.reason: Native Atari port of Juan J. Martinez's MSX single-screen platformer, written in WNF and 6502 assembly. Inspected night-knight.wnf implements hardware setup, game state, enemy dispatch, lives and PAL/NTSC timing, with 80 level data files and sprite/runtime modules.

decisions.title: Young Lumberjack
decisions.reason: Substantial native Atari timber-chopping arcade game, also identified as Timberman in source and assets. The 96 KB assembly implementation includes player state, branch/playfield display lists, PAL/NTSC timing, difficulty and RMT music integration.

decisions.title: Harrier Revenge
decisions.reason: Native Amstrad CPC shooter implemented in C with CPCtelera. Inspected game.c contains player/bullet/entity state, health display, six connected maps, enemies, bases and screen redraw logic; source assets, entity and animation modules are present.

decisions.title: Maze Dash
decisions.reason: Original C64 maze arcade game by Stefan Wessels, featuring generated mazes, guards, boost/shoot mechanics and survival/escape modes. Reviewed game.c implements game state and loop; maze/player/monster/platform source modules provide substantive native implementation.

decisions.title: Flying Saucers
decisions.reason: Native C64 arcade flying/shooting game written in XC=BASIC by Csaba Fekete with graphics by Daniel Fekete. Reviewed main BASIC source implements raster interrupts, SID effects, joystick movement, scrolling, wave transitions and collision/action modules.

decisions.title: The Wall
decisions.reason: Native C64 brick-smashing puzzle/action game in C by Johan Berntsson. Reviewed main.c implements native screen/game mechanics and brick scoring; the 2020 revision added multi-brick bonuses, cursor controls and instructions, followed by a cc65-format update.

decisions.title: Wasteland IDE64 enhanced fix
decisions.reason: Binary-patching and replacement-loader project for C64 Wasteland, moving disk I/O to IDE64 and separating saves, fixing PAL/NTSC timing and turbo-speed behavior. Reviewed wasteland_fix.asm patches fixed-address game routines, requesters and interrupt vectors, and incorporates loader/fileops modules.

decisions.title: Vortex II C64 network game
decisions.reason: Client/server space-game proof of concept with a native C64 assembly client and Java server. Reviewed vortex.s initializes DHCP/UDP, login, interrupts, sprites and music; server Universe.java creates the shared map, entities, planetoids and destructible scenery.

decisions.title: Flynn classic Macintosh Telnet and Finger client
decisions.reason: Native classic-Mac network terminal with Telnet IAC negotiation, VT100/VT220/xterm rendering, Finger, multiple sessions and settings. Independent application from the author's Geomys Gopher client; variants remain one project.

decisions.title: mac68k-asm Macintosh assembler toolchain
