decisions.reason: Modern C implementation of a Macintosh MDS-style 68000 assembler, linker, resource compiler and MacBinary writer. Handles A5 globals, instruction encoding, branch sizing and classic project/resource dialects.

decisions.title: mac68k-disk MFS and HFS image editor
decisions.reason: Dependency-free C disk-image tool implementing classic Macintosh MFS/HFS allocation, catalogs/B-trees, Finder folder metadata, resource forks and MacBinary import/export. It edits actual disk structures rather than wrapping an emulator.

decisions.title: Terminal 2.2 classic Macintosh source restoration
decisions.reason: Restoration and Retro68 adaptation of Erny Tontlinger's 1992 serial-terminal source distribution, preserving C interpreter, serial I/O, capture/scrolling, MacBinary and X/Y/ZModem/QuickB transfers with THINK C/MPW artifacts.

decisions.title: SF3KUtils RISC OS game-data editors
decisions.reason: Coherent four-utility suite for Star Fighter 3000 game data: SFToSpr graphics conversion, FednetCmp compression, SFSkyEdit skies and SFColours palette mapping. Contains native GUI code, data backends and tests, kept as one suite.

decisions.title: ChocToObj Chocks Away model converter
decisions.reason: Command-line parser and geometry converter for compressed/raw Chocks Away and Extra Missions model/index files into Wavefront OBJ/MTL. Source includes primitive decoding, material/color mapping and normals generation.

decisions.title: Portable MDX decoder
decisions.reason: Portable 32/64-bit MDX playback library derived from GORRY's MXDRVg C conversion of disassembled X68000 MXDRV.X and X68Sound chip emulation. Adds isolated contexts, register/key-on APIs and sample WAV/player frontends.

decisions.title: Z-MUSIC v2 X68000 sources and reconstructed variants
decisions.reason: Preserved/normalized source of Zenji Nishikawa's Z-MUSIC 2.08 driver/compiler/player plus rebuilt MZL 2.08e sources and later patched variants. Repository documents matching 2.08e from base sources and unified sources intended to reproduce original executables.

decisions.title: WebXpressionPlus X68000 browser modernization
decisions.reason: Modernization of Mitsuky's WebXpression native Human68k browser, adding UTF-8 to Shift-JIS conversion and TLS support while retaining HTML parsing, images/cache/history and 68k display routines.

decisions.title: FxBox Amiga multitrack loop processor
decisions.reason: AMOS BASIC audio editor/loop processor with IFF/AIFF/WAV/MP3/OctaMED handling, multichannel arrangements and realtime effects. Actual current ASCII source, historical AMOS versions, custom 68k music extension and Windows VST bridge are included.

decisions.title: AIVE Amiga GIF and IFF viewer source
decisions.reason: Original small-memory Amiga Image ViewEr 1.7 source with C UI/screen setup and 68000 assembly GIF/IFF decoding, scaling, Floyd-Steinberg dithering and display routines. GPL re-release preserves substantive 1994 native application.

decisions.title: Push 64KB Acorn Archimedes demo
decisions.reason: Native ARM assembly Revision 2024 64KB demo with sequence/music synchronization, particle systems, palette/graphics code and packed loader. Complete effects implementation and asset build scripts establish more than a binary release.

decisions.title: Mikroreise Acorn Archimedes anaglyph demo
decisions.reason: Native ARM assembly stereoscopic/anaglyph production with dual-eye dot tunnel, 3D scene projection, scroller, music and sequence assets. Deadline 2023 production distinct from later Push despite shared build/framework code.

decisions.title: Rail Gunner C64 and Archimedes game
decisions.reason: Original C64 rail shooter in 6502 assembly plus source-derived portable C simulation, SDL frontend and substantive native Archimedes port. Archimedes-specific rendering, input, sound/synthesis and ARM assembly support share a coherent game core.

decisions.title: Asteroids Neo — NGPC native asteroid shooter
decisions.reason: A native Neo Geo Pocket Color homebrew reinterpretation of Atari's Asteroids. Its own C entity pool implements rotating ship sprites, thrust, asteroid splitting, aimed UFO fire, collisions, waves and flash high scores; it is neither an arcade CPU wrapper nor a recovered Atari binary.

decisions.title: Tutankham NGPC — native maze-action adaptation
decisions.reason: Native C adaptation of Konami's 1982 arcade maze shooter for Neo Geo Pocket Color. Separate game, map, screen and entity modules implement keys, treasure, teleport zones, doors and enemy spawn/chase/patrol behavior, rather than emulating the arcade board.

decisions.title: Frogger Neo — NGPC native river-crossing game
decisions.reason: A native Neo Geo Pocket Color Frogger adaptation with implemented scrolling traffic, logs, diving turtles, homes, timer, fly bonus and pond progression. Source variants support arcade portrait and Coleco-style VFD presentations within one project lineage.

decisions.title: Pengu — native NGPC ice-block arcade game
decisions.reason: Original Neo Geo Pocket Color homebrew inspired by Pengo. C modules implement authored grids, sliding ice blocks, crush rules, hatching and pursuing Sno-Bees, wall stuns, lives and level timing. README explicitly says no original Pengo code, artwork, audio or data is used.

decisions.title: QBert Neo — native NGPC pyramid-hopping game
decisions.reason: Native C Neo Geo Pocket Color adaptation of Q*bert with pyramid tile states, Coily pursuit, falling balls, rescue discs, rotated D-pad movement and high-score entry. It packages its own NGPC ROM rather than running an arcade emulator.

decisions.title: Blue Print Neo — native NGPC maze-and-parts game
decisions.reason: A clean-room-labelled Neo Geo Pocket Color homage to 1982 Blue Print. Native C modules implement searching houses, carrying machine parts, chasing bombs, a timed rope scene, blueprint completion and monster defeat; authored maze data is compiled into the game.

decisions.title: VUEngine Studio — Virtual Boy development IDE
decisions.reason: A substantial Eclipse Theia/Electron IDE dedicated to VUEngine and Nintendo Virtual Boy development. Custom TypeScript/React extension implements project-aware code generation, hardware-specific editors and build integration, including a layer/frame pixel editor with tile grids. Distinct development tool from the already tracked VUEngine runtime.

decisions.title: Storm Storm — Vectrex paddle-action game
decisions.reason: Native Motorola 6809 Vectrex assembly game with title, logo, gameplay and game-over states. Gameplay updates a paddle, accelerated ball, enemies, missed-enemy markers, particles, score and screen timing, with Vectrex BIOS vector drawing.

decisions.title: Satlink Linux — Saturn USB DataLink utility
decisions.reason: Linux C host utility implementing Sega Saturn USB DataLink packet/checksum and FTDI transport logic. It can dump the BIOS, read/write Saturn memory and upload/execute homebrew, enabling native console development and inspection without the original Windows-only software.

decisions.title: Seta GX — Sega Saturn emulator for Wii
decisions.reason: Reusable Sega Saturn emulator for Nintendo Wii derived from Yabause Wii and selected Yaba Sanshiro improvements. Substantial fork includes Hollywood GPU rendering and its own SH-2-to-PowerPC dynamic recompiler, with dual SH-2 machine state, rather than being a game-specific emulation wrapper.

decisions.title: Zygo3D — Saturn 3D platformer and map builder
decisions.reason: Native Sega Saturn C 3D platformer/demo built on Jo Engine and SGL. A substantial main.c implements player movement/collision, enemies, powerups, title and level selection, camera modes, object viewing and an interactive map builder, with Saturn texture/map assets and Jo entry point.

decisions.title: SaturnCue — Saturn homebrew CUE-sheet generator
decisions.reason: Cross-platform Go command-line tool for constructing Sega Saturn homebrew CUE sheets from an ISO and numbered audio track files. Actual implementation locates tracks, identifies WAVE/BINARY formats, sorts by track number, formats pregaps and writes the cue file.

decisions.title: ded — DOS executable disassembler
decisions.reason: Standalone C++ disassembler for 16-bit DOS MZ and COM images. It uses Capstone for instruction decoding and implements its own binary loading and experimental recursive traversal and cross-reference discovery.

decisions.title: Spice86 — real-mode PC reverse-engineering emulator
decisions.reason: Reusable PC emulator and reverse-engineering environment that records real-mode DOS execution, builds control-flow graphs and emits C# override projects. This is the maintained C# continuation of the original Java Spice86.

decisions.title: MBBSDASM — segmented NE disassembler
decisions.reason: C# disassembler and analyst for 16-bit NE binaries, originally designed for MajorBBS and Worldgroup modules but also supporting general Win16 EXE/DLL files. Enhanced analysis resolves imports, relocation references, strings and compiler idioms.

decisions.title: le_disasm — DOS LE/LX reassembly-oriented disassembler
decisions.reason: C++ libopcodes-based executable disassembler derived from swdisasm. It parses DOS MZ/LE/LX linear executable structures and emits AT&T/GAS-style assembly intended to support analysis and reassembly.

decisions.title: AITD-tools — script, archive and memory analysis suite
decisions.reason: Alone in the Dark-family research tools: LIFE/TRACK script disassemblers, PAK extraction/repacking and background export, live DOSBox memory/variable views, and recorded-session playback for inspection.

decisions.title: dizzy — tracing DOS EXE disassembler
decisions.reason: Small but substantive C++ disassembler for 16-bit DOS MZ programs, following branches from initial CS:IP to separate reachable instructions from data and allowing function annotations.

decisions.title: winevdm / otvdm — Win16 compatibility emulator
decisions.reason: Wine-derived compatibility layer that runs Windows 1.x–3.x executables on 64-bit Windows using CPU emulation, Win16-to-Win32 API conversion, DOS services and handle translation.

decisions.title: Win3mu — Windows 3 emulator
decisions.reason: Open-source release of Topten Software Windows 3.0 emulator. Sharp86 CPU emulation loads Win16 applications while implemented APIs are mapped to modern Windows calls; includes debugging and NE module/heap management.

decisions.title: Nuvie — Ultima VI and Worlds of Ultima engine
decisions.reason: Independent SDL engine for Ultima VI, Martian Dreams and The Savage Empire, using original data with reconstructed game logic, conversation interpretation and Lua game scripts. This repository is the standalone engine before its integration into ScummVM.

decisions.title: Cosmo-Engine — Cosmo’s Cosmic Adventure native engine
decisions.reason: SDL2 C reimplementation of Cosmo’s Cosmic Adventure with actors, collision, effects, level/container loading, audio and UI. Address-style variables and decoded actor dispatch remain in recovered engine logic.

decisions.title: OpenTitus — Titus the Fox and Moktar engine
decisions.reason: Native SDL engine recreated from the original Titus the Fox/Moktar games, with ported movement/game behavior, level/sprite decoding, OPL playback and configurable data layout.

decisions.title: OpenDW — Dragon Wars C engine reconstruction
decisions.reason: Attempt to translate Interplay Dragon Wars’ 16-bit real-mode assembly engine to portable C. Includes annotated original-engine disassembly and reconstructed resource, script, UI, party and rendering subsystems.

decisions.title: The Bard’s Tale DOS — Microsoft C source reconstruction
decisions.reason: C and NASM reconstruction of the 1987 DOS BARD.EXE, with reconstructed root and overlay modules and a reproducibility-focused Microsoft C 4.0/LINK 3.51 build/compare pipeline.

decisions.title: Might and Magic III DOS — byte-exact source reconstruction
decisions.reason: C and x86 assembly reconstruction of Might and Magic III: Isles of Terra including resident code, VROOMM overlays, data and script/gameplay modules. Build tooling reconstructs and compares the original packed executable.

decisions.title: UNIVAC 1219 — Rust emulator, assembler and disassembler
decisions.reason: A reusable Rust implementation of the InfoAge UNIVAC 1219 machine and its programming tools. The shared crate implements 18-bit register/memory execution, instructions, arithmetic, I/O and tape handling, with CLI assembler/emulator/disassembler frontends and a browser UI. It is a substantive implementation inspired by Duane Craps’s earlier tools, rather than a packaged museum image.

decisions.title: RISC-V on UNIVAC-1219 — native interpreter and C toolchain
decisions.reason: A native UNIVAC 1219 assembly implementation of a 32-bit RISC-V interpreter, with OCaml decoding/code-generation/fuzzing tools and a C build environment. This lets modern C programs compile to RISC-V instructions and execute through an interpreter on the historical 18-bit machine. Its opcode dispatch and arithmetic/memory/branch handlers are present as UNIVAC assembly sources.

decisions.title: Lilith 1983 — preserved bootstrap emulator
decisions.reason: The actual K&R C Lilith emulator Andreas Borchert developed in 1983 to bootstrap ETH Modula-2 onto a Perkin-Elmer 3220 running Unix VII. The repository preserves the execution engine, loader, storage, Unix service bridge and tracing code. This is historical development software preservation, with known period-compiler dependencies, rather than a new browser emulator.

decisions.title: ETH Lilith C18 — adapted Modula-2 multipass compiler sources
decisions.reason: Preserved ETH Zürich C18 Modula-2 multipass compiler sources, derived from the 1981 compiler and adapted at Ulm in 1983 for a Lilith emulator under Unix VII. The repository contains actual compiler passes, symbols, code-generation modules, build recipes and steady-state C18 binaries, so it is a source-preservation/toolchain record separate from the emulator that runs it.

decisions.title: ND-120 — reconstructed Norsk Data CPU in Verilog
decisions.reason: A reconstruction of the 1988 Norsk Data ND-120 3202D CPU board from original design documents, first represented in Logisim and now maintained as Verilog. Includes CPU/decode gate arrays, PAL translations, microcode, MMU and bus devices, simulation harnesses and FPGA board integrations. This is a hardware/firmware reconstruction distinct from the catalogued nd100x and nd500x software emulators.

decisions.title: Tawny Petrel — TMS9900 simulator and assembler
decisions.reason: A C# TMS9900 instruction-level development simulator with a Forth-like interactive monitor, assembler, memory access, single stepping and status/workspace-register state. Source implements the architecture’s RAM-backed register workspace, context switching, flags and instruction dispatch, with tests and usable assembly examples; it deliberately models the CPU rather than recreating a complete TI 990 system.

decisions.title: VIEW-1108 — Apollo window-view program reconstruction
decisions.reason: A source-grounded new reconstruction of NASA MSC’s lost VIEW visualization program from its surviving reports, plots and film output. Fixed-form period-style Fortran implements trajectory, projection, spacecraft and celestial line drawing; a modern shell compiles it for live browser presentation. The project explicitly labels conjectures, modern substitutions and restomod additions rather than claiming recovered original source or an exact UNIVAC executable.

decisions.title: tnz — IBM 3270 terminal and automation library
decisions.reason: IBM’s Python implementation of 3270 terminal interaction, including a TN3270 data-stream engine, zti terminal UI and ati automation compatibility layer. The code implements terminal orders, screen state, EBCDIC handling, session management and protocol negotiation, providing reusable access to historical mainframe interfaces rather than merely launching another emulator.

decisions.title: IronTerm — browser 3270 and 5250 terminal implementation
decisions.reason: A static JavaScript implementation of IBM 3270 and 5250 terminal protocols for mainframe and AS/400/IBM i access. Browser modules implement datastream parsing, fields, screen state, TN3270E/TN5250E negotiation and ENPTUI behavior; connection uses an external TCP-to-WebSocket bridge. Substantive parsers and protocol tests distinguish it from a skin around an existing emulator.

decisions.title: PilRC — Palm OS resource compiler and tools
decisions.reason: Preserved and maintained PilRC source for compiling Palm resource scripts into application resource data, including bitmap/font processing and optional preview UI. The implementation includes the real resource parser/serializer, language/type tables, bitmap encoders and font tools, with Palm examples. This is the long-running original Palm tool lineage, not another Palm SDK mirror.

decisions.title: pilot-link — Palm HotSync protocol libraries and utilities
decisions.reason: The historical pilot-link C libraries and command-line conduits for communicating with Palm handhelds from Unix-like systems. Implements Palm DLP and lower-level link/socket protocols plus record packers, synchronizers and install/backup/debug tools. This is an independent original protocol/tooling lineage, not the already catalogued modern JavaScript palm-sync or palm-pdb projects.

decisions.title: Castaway (ZX Spectrum)
decisions.reason: Original 2016 platform/action game source by Juan J. Martinez for the ZX Spectrum 48K, with room data, enemies, collectibles, keyboard/joystick selection and a bespoke loader. This is the native game, not an emulator wrapper.

decisions.title: Good Shepherd
decisions.reason: Simon Springett’s 1984 ZX Spectrum BASIC shepherding game preserved as readable source with tape/audio artifacts and a source-to-tape utility. Shepherd, sheep chain and pursuing wolf are simulated by the game itself.

decisions.title: The Lighthouse of Doom
decisions.reason: Text adventure independently implemented in portable C and then hand-ported to Z80 for CP/M and the 48K Spectrum. A turn-limited lighthouse crisis supports inventory/object puzzles and two solutions.

decisions.title: Operation Jeff
decisions.reason: Mouse-aimed native Spectrum Next arcade defense game. Players eliminate approaching Jeffs using delayed explosions, charge management and numerous bonuses while advancing through areas.

decisions.title: ZX Wonky One Key
decisions.reason: Native single-control-key Spectrum game with levels, collectibles, doors, teleporters, slowdown effects and a countdown. Full game source includes source-level trace/debug support and designer utilities.

decisions.title: The Virus (ZX Spectrum)
decisions.reason: Original Spectrum action/puzzle game built around integer-optimized flocking/Boids behavior. The player manipulates levels to clear a swarm under a time limit.

decisions.title: Grazers
decisions.reason: Native ecological hunting/puzzle game in which grass spreads, grazers eat/reproduce/starve and a hunter intervenes in an evolving world. One source tree supports Spectrum, C64, MSX and Master System.

decisions.title: ZlaloX
decisions.reason: Native slalom/obstacle arcade game for the Spectrum, also ported to Amstrad CPC 464. Shared C code switches hardware/rendering and keyboard backends between the machines.

decisions.title: Sami Troid
decisions.reason: Alfonso Saavedra’s Metroid-inspired Spectrum fan game using La Churrera. The player explores a spaceship and carries fourteen eggs one at a time to an incubator before reaching the control room.

decisions.title: ZX Log Chopper
decisions.reason: Original compact Spectrum timing game: activate a moving chopper at log markers, earn round scores and progress through logs while maintaining a high score.

decisions.title: worzxle
decisions.reason: Wordle-style five-letter word puzzle implemented for the ZX80, ZX81 and Spectrum/Timex family. Six guesses receive positional/letter feedback and feed a running score.

decisions.title: BubbleDuck
decisions.reason: Native Amstrad CPC platform/action game by Samuel Bolanowski and Atharuddin Syed, built with CPCtelera and a duck/bubble-themed character and enemy set.

decisions.title: Creepers (Amstrad CPC)
decisions.reason: Native Worms-like turn-based artillery game for CPC 464/6128 with destructible procedural terrain, teams, hotseat/CPU opponents, multiple weapons and persistent score storage. Includes attract-demo programs.

decisions.title: Chaos Groove (GLX restoration)
decisions.reason: Raylib-based Windows/Linux/Web restoration port of Richard Phipps’s 2008 Chaos Groove, itself a remake of Julian Gollop’s Spectrum Chaos: Battle of the Wizards. Preserves native board/spell gameplay rather than wrapping a Spectrum CPU emulator.

decisions.title: Hotpot — Double Juggle Vegatabobble
decisions.reason: Reservoir Gods' original Atari ST vegetable-juggling game source, identified by the HOTPOT.PRJ header as Double Juggle Vegatabobble: This Is Vegetable Juggling (2002). The repository currently contains the Hotpot implementation rather than a separate new game per directory.

decisions.title: Midisurf
decisions.reason: Original MIDI rhythm game for Atari ST: one or two players guide dragons to collect notes while the ST sound chip plays selected MIDI tracks. Actual gameplay, MIDI parsing and native GEM graphics are present.

decisions.title: Deputy Arsh
decisions.reason: Monochrome endless runner written from scratch for Atari ST, with jump, kick and slide mechanics, custom raster/PSG routines, interrupt vectors and keyboard/mouse drivers.

decisions.title: 2048 — Atari GEM port
decisions.reason: Native Atari GEM adaptation of John Elliott’s C/GEM 2048, retaining his sliding-block board logic and GEM front end while adding an m68k Atari build and NatFeats support.

decisions.title: DownRoll
decisions.reason: Native Atari ST arcade game by Daniel Bahrami and Scott Charles, with moving platforms, ball physics/collision, music, custom interrupt/input handling and double-buffered rendering.

decisions.title: Man Over Board
decisions.reason: Original Atari ST typing/rescue game whose model tracks swimmer movement, word rows, score and decorative state; includes native raster, PSG, interrupts and input code plus module tests.

decisions.title: Mitosis
decisions.reason: Ataxx-style RISC OS desktop board game in RiscLua, including full board/rules classes and native Toolbox wrapper integration. Source and a bundled standalone runtime application are present.

decisions.title: CentiBug
decisions.reason: Gavin Cawley’s Centipede-like game, begun on an Archimedes A410/1 in the late 1980s and revisited from backup. Includes earlier character-based gameplay and newer desktop/sprite implementation.

decisions.title: Lode Runner for RISC OS
decisions.reason: Native C/OSLib recreation of Lode Runner for RISC OS, with destructible terrain, climbing/digging, enemy navigation, sprite rendering, WIMP integration, configurable scaling and saved level progress.

decisions.title: Pegs
decisions.reason: Stephen Fryatt’s desktop Peg Solitaire game, with original untokenised BBC BASIC WIMP event handling, drag/board interaction, resource files and a reproducible-source packaging layout.

decisions.title: SHOT68K
decisions.reason: Playable Space Invaders-style shooting sample for X68000/X68000Z, intentionally simple for learning native game programming. Scene, enemy/player/bullet state, sprites, input and sound are actual C/assembly implementation.

decisions.title: Wire Drift Racers
decisions.reason: Bare-metal X68000 wireframe battle-racing game with local one/two-player modes, three tracks, drift/boost/slipstream mechanics, fixed-step simulation and double-buffered display. Boots from XDF without Human68k runtime.

decisions.title: Squared
decisions.reason: Original Ludum Dare 40 Amiga game built around Amiga C Engine, including gameplay state, map/square simulation, HUD/scores and native blitter-based graphics.

decisions.title: Soliton
decisions.reason: Preserved Soliton Klondike/Freecell source by Kai Nickel, Dirk Stoecker and contributors, with MUI card-game widgets, profiles/statistics, datatype/cardset loading and native Amiga-family build recipes.

decisions.title: Tobu Tobu Girl
decisions.reason: Original arcade platformer with upward scrolling, timed stages, enemy bounces, dash/boost movement, unlockable skins, high scores and MML music. game.c implements concrete player/entity collision, spawning, level progress and native Game Boy video/audio control.

decisions.title: Evoland GB
decisions.reason: Fan-made native Game Boy demake of Evoland. Source implements tile-map movement, player sword animation, chest activation and progressive controls/game features. This is a work-in-progress original implementation rather than an original-binary interpreter.

decisions.title: piuGBA
decisions.reason: Native Game Boy Advance Pump It Up-style rhythm simulator consuming StepMania SSC charts. Judge.cpp implements timing windows, hold judging and score feedback; SongScene orchestrates native sprites, audio, chart play and multiplayer/hardware effects. It does not emulate an arcade CPU.

decisions.title: Tone’s Adventure
decisions.reason: Unfinished original Game Boy Color exploration/platform game developed in 2011–2012. next.c handles camera and banked world tile streaming; player.c implements acceleration, jumping, swimming and underwater movement against chunk-based maps.

decisions.title: CrossConnect
decisions.reason: Native Numberlink-style Game Boy/Game Boy Color puzzle game. Concrete C board representation, tile drawing and connection logic are backed by assembly save, effects, level manager and sound subsystems, with generated puzzle packs.

decisions.title: Flooder
decisions.reason: Native Game Boy Color flood-fill puzzle game with a randomized 14×14 board, limited moves, palette selection, win/loss scenes, transitions and sound. Source uses CGB tile attributes and palette registers rather than emulated predecessor code.

decisions.title: Max Pirate
decisions.reason: Original native Game Boy top-down pirate action game with anchor melee, cannon shooting, enemies, collisions, level state, pause/menu transitions and hUGE/CBT-FX audio integration. main.c and hero.c contain concrete hardware-facing game logic.

decisions.title: Petris
decisions.reason: Native Game Boy Color falling-piece pet-building puzzle game with multiple game types, special pieces, hinting, variable difficulty, music, statistics and two-player link-cable play. gameplay.c implements drop progression, linked-player game-over handling and input/state updates.

decisions.title: YM2017
decisions.reason: Native Mega Drive music-cartridge software, with track browser, ordered/shuffle playback, on-screen visualizations and custom cartridge LED-array support. Main C program uses native VDP/joypad routines; XGM driver manages the Z80 sound processor.

decisions.title: Speedrun Tower
decisions.reason: Original native 68000 Sega Genesis speedrunning adventure demo with randomized elevator/floor connectivity and scripted conversations/events. Main X68 source builds native vectors/header/init and game systems; ActionScript routines implement scene-exit resolution and event handling.

decisions.title: Undertale NES demo
decisions.reason: Native NES homebrew recreation of Undertale’s Lesser Dog battle. Assembly main source initializes PPU/APU/RAM and includes custom graphics, text, input, coroutine/generator and battle/menu modules. It creates a real NES ROM rather than wrapping the PC game in a CPU interpreter.

decisions.title: File Fixers
decisions.reason: Original computer-themed NES RPG made for Game Off 2021. C main controls desktop/window-style UI and game state; dungeon source creates sector layouts, tracks completion and loads entities, supported by MMC3 mapper and native assembly runtime.

decisions.title: BPCore-Engine
decisions.reason: Native GBA Lua game framework built from parts of the author’s BlindJump C++ engine. Concrete BPCoreEngine.cpp embeds Lua APIs and allocator; gba_platform.cpp accesses GBA hardware. Lua manifest/build script packages resources/scripts behind a native engine ROM to enable small games.

decisions.title: mzretools — MZ reconstruction analysis toolkit
decisions.reason: Reusable C++ toolkit for analyzing 8086 DOS MZ executables and comparing instruction-level reconstructions even when routine and data layout changes. Includes header, map, signature, pointer and duplicate-code tools plus an instruction decoder and analysis library.

decisions.title: JDasm — interactive DOS binary format analyzer
decisions.reason: Java/Swing interactive disassembler, binary format analyzer and hex editor. Includes concrete DOS COM loading/disassembly and MZ header/relocation readers alongside PE, ELF, Mach-O and media-format analyzers.

decisions.title: 386SWAT — preserved protected-mode DOS debugger
decisions.reason: Original Qualitas 386SWAT protected-mode debugger source archive with extensive assembly, instruction decoding, source-symbol tools, VCPI/DPMI integration and Windows VxD components. Supports debugging native protected-mode and virtual-8086 clients.

decisions.title: debxxf — DOS DPMI and Win16 debuggers
decisions.reason: Source release and continuation of Deb16f, Deb32f and Deb16fw, a family of native DOS DPMI and 16-bit Windows debuggers originating in 1992. Provides protected/real-mode breakpoint handling and symbol/file support.

decisions.title: dosdebug — DOSBox GDB and trace analysis
decisions.reason: Reusable Python tools connecting GDB/pygdb to DOSBox guest registers and memory, processing instruction traces, decoding selected DOS system calls and substituting multi-instruction patterns with readable pseudo-operations.

decisions.title: CodeViewParser — NB00 DOS debug-symbol reader
decisions.reason: Small Python implementation for locating early Microsoft CodeView NB00 data appended to DOS MZ executables and reading module/public-symbol subsections. Intended for symbols produced by Microsoft LINK 3.x through 5.03.

decisions.title: OS2Linux — OS/2 API source-port library
decisions.reason: Preserved OS2Linux source library implementing OS/2 C APIs on Linux, allowing applications with available source to be recompiled and linked natively. Contains file, process, memory, module, semaphore, pipe and resource API modules.

decisions.title: OS2API — OS/2 DOSCALL library for Windows NT
decisions.reason: Preserved Ivan Skytte Jørgensen OS2API library mapping OS/2 DOSCALL APIs onto Win32. Recompiled OS/2 program source links against OS2API.LIB to execute natively under Windows NT.

decisions.title: COMUNP — hardware-assisted DOS COM unpacker
decisions.reason: Original 1995 assembly unpacker for programs that started as DOS COM images and were packed into EXE form. Uses Intel 386 debug registers and real-mode execution to recover the unpacked image.

decisions.title: DOS-Expander 4 — Pascal reconstruction and Rust port
decisions.reason: Reconstruction of Heinz Hombergs DOS-Expander 4.0 file manager and program menu, with Borland Pascal/assembly sources plus a modern-terminal Rust behavioral port. Rebuild scripts compare recovered modules against original binaries.

decisions.title: pcZIP-remade — DOS ZIP drive driver reconstruction
decisions.reason: C/assembly reconstruction of Chris Van Genderen pcZIP V1.00.000B/D parallel-port Iomega ZIP/Jaz driver and manager binaries. Includes byte-identical assembly baseline, C command dispatch and differential hardware-protocol oracle.

decisions.title: Fractint legacy — DOS source release reconstruction
decisions.reason: Historical source-release reconstruction/archive of DOS Fractint versions up to 19.6, preserving the Stone Soup Group fractal generator, optimized assembly arithmetic, graphics drivers and help compiler. This is source restoration rather than binary decompilation.

decisions.title: XXDP+ monitor — restored PDP-11 diagnostic OS
decisions.reason: Ian Hammond’s reconstruction of the XXDP+ HMDLD0 monitor by reverse assembling the XXDP23 binary. A complete monolithic annotated monitor source is preserved alongside binary reference and listings.

decisions.title: Fuzzball — PDP-11 network operating-system sources
decisions.reason: Preserves David Mills’s Fuzzball operating-system/network suite, including MACRO-11 implementation modules, RT-11 command files, libraries and distribution disk images.

decisions.title: ELF — PDP-11 ARPANET operating-system archive
decisions.reason: Historical ELF system files recovered from SAIL, with PDP-11 operating-system/network source, linker code, manuals and PDP-10 host-side tools. The archive explicitly records conversion of SAIL 36-bit words into ASCII octets.

decisions.title: MOS — original PDP-11 Micro Operating System
decisions.reason: Original MACRO-11 Micro Operating System source provided by J. Noel Chiappa, including processor/storage management, asynchronous I/O, network modules and Terminal Interface Unit configuration.

decisions.title: MINITS — PDP-11 mini ITS source archive
decisions.reason: Preserved Mini ITS executive and device/network software for assorted PDP-11 front ends, terminal concentrators and bridges, with selectable machine configurations and PALX assembly instructions.

decisions.title: RSTS/E V10.1 — Y2K and networking maintenance patches
decisions.reason: Tony Nicholson’s RSTS/E maintenance repository contains actual BASIC-PLUS FIT date-word fixes, build commands, DECnet/E ONLPAT patches and related PDP-11 utility sources. Scope is maintenance patches, not a complete reconstructed RSTS kernel.

decisions.title: RUST/SJ — RT-11-compatible PDP-11 OS sources
decisions.reason: Original legacy HAMMONDsoftware RUST/SJ and RUST/RTX operating-system source/binary collection, with MACRO-11 monitor, boot, EMT and device routines plus utilities and Windows-side support. It is unrelated to the modern Rust programming language.

decisions.title: Xinu68k — Motorola 68000 operating-system port
decisions.reason: Actual Xinu version-7-derived kernel/tree being ported to Motorola 68000, with 68k startup and context switching, scheduler/network C sources and freestanding m68k toolchain recipes.

decisions.title: Pilot VT100 — native Palm OS serial terminal
decisions.reason: Preserved 1990s Pilot VT100 application source and later Palm OS 4 SDK compatibility patch, implementing serial terminal I/O, escape parser, screen handling and configurable keys.

decisions.title: LISPF4 — preserved Interlisp interpreter and C port
decisions.reason: Mats Nordstrom’s early-1980s FORTRAN Interlisp interpreter, preserved in original form and translated with f2c into a subsequently hand-maintained portable C interpreter, with Lisp libraries, image-building scripts, manuals and regression tests.

decisions.title: TENEX — PDP-10 operating-system source archive
decisions.reason: Substantial preserved TENEX monitor/source archive with multiple historical revisions, MACRO-10 memory/scheduler/file modules, EXEC and utility sources, assembler/linker command files, manuals and hardware documentation.

decisions.title: S1130 — C# IBM 1130 emulator and assembler
decisions.reason: Reusable C# IBM 1130 CPU/system emulator and assembler with instruction classes, memory/interrupt handling, card devices, partial disk support, tests and optional Web API/frontend.

decisions.title: CenturionJS — TypeScript CPU6 minicomputer emulator
decisions.reason: Independent TypeScript Centurion minicomputer emulator with substantial CPU6 opcode/addressing-mode implementation, RAM/ROM/diagnostic/multiplexer cards and debugging support.

decisions.title: pappadf/lisa-c
decisions.reason: Primary README, Makefile and implementation tree establish a substantial Apple Lisa 68000 cross-development environment with custom object, filesystem, runtime and emulator-test tooling.

decisions.title: pappadf/lisa-paint
decisions.reason: Primary README and C implementation establish a distinct original Lisa Office System painting application, not merely a lisa-c example directory.

decisions.title: skoolkid/pyskool
decisions.reason: Primary documentation and implementation establish a substantial playable Python/Pygame reimplementation of Skool Daze and Back to Skool with configurable remix variants.

decisions.title: skoolkid/t2sfiles
decisions.reason: Primary README and companion analysis tools establish a substantial SkoolKit-based pristine-snapshot corpus and Z80 register/RAM comparison workflow for Spectrum software preservation.

decisions.title: maylay/sg1000
decisions.reason: GitHub metadata identifies this as a direct fork of already reviewed barbeque/sg1000; inspected README remains the Soggy-1000 hardware-clone project and establishes no distinct retro-software contribution.

decisions.title: kvanderlaag/sg1000
decisions.reason: GitHub metadata identifies this as a direct fork of already reviewed barbeque/sg1000; the inspected changes remain within the Soggy-1000 hardware-clone lineage rather than a distinct retro-software project.

decisions.title: VWarlock/SEGA_sg1000
decisions.reason: GitHub metadata identifies this as a direct fork of already reviewed barbeque/sg1000; the README remains focused on hardware-clone boards, BOM and electrical revisions, not a distinct software project.

decisions.title: txuswashere/Homebrew
decisions.reason: The repository describes a multi-system collection of homebrew ROMs but provides no source, author-level provenance or distinct development contribution in the inspected root documentation; a third-party binary collection is not promoted.

decisions.title: skoolkid/conan2-13692
decisions.reason: The connected GitHub metadata reports a zero-size repository and the default branch exposes no README or project artifact, so no substantive project can be verified.

decisions.title: skoolkid/ZXDB
decisions.reason: GitHub identifies this as a fork of zxdb/ZXDB. The inspected README describes the canonical general Spectrum metadata database and converters; no distinct fork contribution or separate retro-development implementation is established.

decisions.title: California Games — BBC Micro conversion
decisions.reason: Routine-by-routine reverse-engineering-derived conversion of all six C64 California Games events to a 32K BBC Micro Model B. Native 6502 game rules are adapted directly, with rebuilt BBC graphics, disk overlays and sound; not a game-specific emulation wrapper.

decisions.title: GNW64 — Game & Watch emulator for C64
decisions.reason: Reusable native C64 emulator for Sharp SM5A Game & Watch ROMs, supporting Ball, Vermin, Fire and Helmet through a shared CPU interpreter and per-title display adapters. Distinct from native C64 gameplay remakes.

decisions.title: Crow Boy — C64 side-scroller source
decisions.reason: Author-released abandoned college-project side-scrolling game demonstrator, with a controllable running/jumping character, scrolling graphics buffers, IRQs, object/action logic, level and sprite resources.

decisions.title: Castle Dungeon — Locomotive BASIC engine
decisions.reason: Native CPC didactic RPG/platform engine demonstration with tile map, limited camera window, collision, coins, doors/keys, enemies and combat scenes. Complete text BASIC listing is the substantive implementation.

decisions.title: BONEKEEP — PCW and CP/M dungeon game
decisions.reason: Native K&R C dungeon game for Amstrad PCW CP/M Plus with alternative generic CP/M VT100 build, eleven dungeon levels, combat/inventory logic and native map encoder, decoder and editor tools.

decisions.title: Race 'n Smash — C64 source
decisions.reason: Complete author-released smooth-scrolling C64 racing game and earlier prototype from the Lemon64 Fun and Games with Assembly tutorial; converted from native Turbo Assembler development to ACME/C64Studio source.

decisions.title: Slug vs Lettuce — C64 survival platformer
decisions.reason: Author-released single-screen platform survival game created for Scene World issue 32's Let's Make a C64 Game tutorial, including native graphics/music and KickAssembler source.

decisions.title: Para Lander DX — C64 source
decisions.reason: Expanded 16-level parachutist landing/high-score game developed natively on C64 after a 2KB competition entry, then transferred into cross-assembly source including disk high-score support.

decisions.title: Spider Maze — C64 source
decisions.reason: Full 16-level C64 arcade maze game for Scene World issue 29 with crystals, pursuing spiders, temporary invulnerability, lives, high scores and ending sequence; distinct from abbreviated tutorial version.

decisions.title: River Barrage — enhanced SEUCK game source
decisions.reason: Complete C64 River Barrage project adapting Martin Piper's reusable scrolling/SEUCK engine, with new title/high-score frontend, shield, animations, score panel, audio choices and picture-loader intro.

decisions.title: RAGE1 — Retro Adventure Game Engine
decisions.reason: Reusable C/Z80 engine for native ZX Spectrum 48K and 128K adventures, with SP1/JSP sprite backends, hero/enemy/bullet collision, generated game data, banking, maps and flow rules.

decisions.title: Mind Field — Atari 8-bit C/assembly source
decisions.reason: Native Atari 8-bit minefield/action game implementation by Peter J. Meyer combining C game logic, 6502 interrupt/graphics/audio routines and cartridge/XEX layouts.

decisions.title: KC Munchkin Amiga Blitz source
decisions.reason: Gary James’s native Blitz Basic maze game, preserved and adjusted by earok. This is editable Amiga game implementation, including map, player/enemy/pill updates and IFF assets, rather than a WHDLoad slave or emulation wrapper.

decisions.title: Mr Zen Amiga source
decisions.reason: Mike Cooper’s Amiga Format competition platform game, supplied with permission and detokenized to readable Blitz Basic by the preservation repository. It has multiple playable characters, world logic and original graphics/sounds.

decisions.title: Space Man The Ultimate Game source
decisions.reason: Recovered isometric action shooter by Peter & Kalle K, originally entered in the Amiga Format Blitz Basic competition and recovered from an Acid Software hard drive. earok’s preservation adds fixes to oxygen timing, corrupt levels and end-of-game looping.

decisions.title: Scorpion Christmas game
decisions.reason: earok’s open Scorpion Engine Christmas puzzle-platformer source, with Santa, Rudolph and pushable presents. The repository contains executable visual-script command graphs, actors, maps and platform data, rather than screenshots or an engine-only demo stub.

decisions.title: Jump N Bump Scorpion port
decisions.reason: Scorpion Engine adaptation of the DOS multiplayer rabbit arena game. Contains original-style gameplay scripts for bunny motion, collisions, spring/water/ice behavior, gore, spawning and scoring, plus full maps and assets.

decisions.title: ClearView RISC OS restoration
decisions.reason: Merlyn Kline’s native ClearView hypertext reader/compiler preserved with a 32-bit-clean RISC OS build path. Supports wrapped multi-font text and inline Sprites, Draw files and Ace Films; source includes reading, compilation, search, bookmarks and printing.

decisions.title: Jacknife Atari disk-image tools
decisions.reason: George Nakos’s Atari ST media-handling plugin and SamariTan CLI, supporting ST/MSA/DIM floppy images and AHDI/ICD-style hard disk images. Contains image decoding, FAT filesystem integration and create/extract/update operations on modern hosts.

decisions.title: USM Atari cartridge builder
decisions.reason: Atari cartridge-image creation tool by ggnkua. Parses TOS PRG inputs, writes cartridge application headers, performs relocation, and embeds a native 68000 loader that copies programs from ROM to RAM before running them.

decisions.title: brownout m68k ELF to TOS converter
decisions.reason: George Nakos and Douglas Little’s linker-stage conversion utility turns m68k ELF into native Atari TOS PRG, including relocations and optional symbol tables. It is useful to cross-development workflows and preserves a dedicated Atari executable-format implementation.

decisions.title: Ascent classic Mac source restoration
decisions.reason: Eduardo Ojeda’s original 2002 two-player Classic Mac arena game and its 2026 native SDL3 restoration. Original C code and art are retained; a replacement SAT/QuickDraw compatibility layer allows the physics, ball, ships, missiles and power-ups to run on modern macOS and Windows.

decisions.title: Wizard Apprentice SDL reconstruction
decisions.reason: Tom Pickering’s C++ recreation of Fantasia’s 1997 RISC OS puzzle game using original assets with permission. Implements 100 levels over five worlds, with wizard/blob switching, ladders, falling/pushable/breakable blocks and collectables.

decisions.title: Daleks RISC OS desktop game
decisions.reason: Stephan Kleinert’s original BBC BASIC RISC OS desktop implementation of the Robots/Daleks survival game. Retains tokenized editable BASIC source in !RunImage, desktop templates, sprites, scores, lives and teleport mechanics.

decisions.title: Fractal Explorer Falcon source
decisions.reason: Kochise’s archived native Atari Falcon030 Mandelbrot/Julia explorer. Full 68030/FPU assembler implementation controls the Falcon video mode, screen memory and blitter before computing fractal iterations.

decisions.title: Moon Knight — Vectrex homebrew
decisions.reason: Native vector action game with player/enemy movement, projectiles, frenzy and scoring. MKnight.asm contains the cartridge entry, title/credits states, game state, player/enemy updates and vector/speech data; it is substantial cartridge source rather than a ROM-only archive.

decisions.title: Computer Space — Vectrex measured-hardware port
decisions.reason: Native 6809 recreation of the 1971 discrete-logic arcade game. Gameplay, artwork, timing and sound were measured from the companion FPGA recreation and schematics. game.asm implements missile lives, game flow, scores, collisions, explosions and hyperspace rather than emulating an original CPU.

decisions.title: VecNIST — native Vectrex digit recognizer
decisions.reason: Interactive Vectrex handwriting recognizer: joystick or experimental light-pen stroke input, 12×12 integer rasterization and a 144–64–10 neural network running on the console CPU. vecnist.asm implements drawing, scaling, first-layer accumulation, second-layer multiplication and score displays; weights and training/test twins are supplied.

decisions.title: R-Type Neo — Pocket Trilogy
decisions.reason: Native C89 scrolling shooter consolidating Star Rise, Bydo Incursion, Star Fall and Final Strike into one cartridge. main.c has chapter loading, ship selection, force pod, charged beam, waves, bosses and chapter-unlock flow; graphics swap by chapter to fit tile memory.

decisions.title: Last Resort Neo
decisions.reason: Native NGPC fan reimagining of SNK’s Last Resort with two ships, five stages, orbital option-pod control, charged wave cannon, multiple pod weapons and monochrome mode. main.c has stage terrain installation, pod movement/fire and independent game progression.

decisions.title: Super Puzzle Fighter II Turbo: SNK vs CAPCOM — NGPC homebrew
decisions.reason: Native puzzle-fighter proof of concept with falling gem pairs, rotations, gravity, crashes, rectangular power gems, chain damage, CPU garbage attacks, story/endless modes and unlocks. src/game.c contains actual grid/phase resolution and difficulty tables; field.c renders through NGPC tile hardware.

decisions.title: Zork Neo
decisions.reason: Button-driven native C reimplementation of Zork I with verb/noun selection and scrolling text. engine.c directly implements room/object accessibility, light sources, inventory, puzzles, score, troll/thief interactions and victory state; this is not a Z-machine CPU-wrapper port.

decisions.title: NGPC Sound Creator
decisions.reason: C++/Qt tracker, piano-roll, instrument/SFX and project tool for native NGPC sound export. polling_driver.cpp supplies real Z80 polling-driver bytes and command host logic; project includes clean-room Z80/T6W28 preview cores and C/ASM output.

decisions.title: NgpCraft Studio
decisions.reason: Material NGPC-targeting fork of GB Studio 4.3.2 with V3 Python compiler, native C generation, audio conversion and emulator-backed play/debug. v3Build.ts snapshots project/resources and invokes V3 export/build-ROM; compiler.py validates reachable IR and creates specialized build plans.

decisions.title: Simple Battle FX
decisions.reason: Original turn-based homebrew battle/RPG for the PC-FX. main.c implements player HP/MP/stats, two-player and survival flow, battle choices and sound, while game.c handles native PC-FX controller/rendering interfaces through liberis.

decisions.title: Final Fantasy — ColecoVision C reimplementation
decisions.reason: Explicit native C/Z80 rewrite of NES Final Fantasy rules using Disch’s disassembly as specification and user-ROM extracted assets, not 6502 translation/emulation. Battle overlays, fixed-bank services, maps and quest state run through 512KB MegaCart banking with SGM RAM.

decisions.title: Potator — Watara Supervision emulator
decisions.reason: Reusable Supervision emulator with 6502 interpreter, memory and I/O maps, interrupts, scanline GPU and sound implementations. common/gpu.c renders actual packed Supervision pixels and palette state; not a title-specific emulation wrapper.

decisions.title: megata — Gamate emulator
decisions.reason: Independent reusable Gamate emulator with CPU opcode/cycle engine, LCD, bank/protection/memory and UI implementations. CPU.cpp contains concrete execution and cycle tables; Emulation.cpp handles BIOS/ZIP/ROM loading and machine state.

decisions.title: Gomoku — native OS/2 source continuation
decisions.reason: Jasper de Keijzer’s 1996 five-in-a-row game, preserved as original ICC sources and a 2026 OpenWatcom Presentation Manager continuation. The 19×19 game implements position updates, computer move search and win detection; this is its own native game lineage.

decisions.title: LitesOut — native OS/2 source continuation
decisions.reason: Herbert Bushong’s 1996–1997 OS/2 Lights Out puzzle continued as a plain-C 32-bit Presentation Manager rewrite of its preserved Borland OWL source. The 6×8 board has two-state and three-state modes, scoring and persistent settings.

decisions.title: HalfWorm — native OS/2 source continuation
decisions.reason: Jan M. Danielsson’s 1997 two-player worm combat game restored for OpenWatcom with native DIVE graphics, MMPM/2 audio and configurable keyboard/joystick input. Its substantial game-thread code implements worms, missiles, apple powerups and round results.

decisions.title: BallsBall — native OS/2 source continuation
decisions.reason: Dmitry Ivanov’s native OS/2 enclosure game, continued from the 2002 open-source release and modernized to OpenWatcom. The player builds walls to contain moving balls; implementation includes runner/hunter motion, ball collisions and territory replacement.

decisions.title: Drift — native OS/2 source continuation
decisions.reason: Dirk Vandenheuvel’s 1995 Asteroids-style Presentation Manager shooter, released as GPL source in 2002 and continued with an OpenWatcom build. Native C implements vector objects, shots, enemies, asteroid geometry and powerups, with keyboard, mouse and GAME$ joystick controls.

decisions.title: Kaboooom! — native OS/2 source continuation
decisions.reason: Michael G. Slack’s 1997–1998 Sibyl OS/2 adaptation of Alex Lane’s 1990 minefield-walking puzzle, translated to C/OpenWatcom in 2026. The game implements mine placement, travel/marking and a new bounded safe-cell deduction solver.

decisions.title: TwentyOne — native OS/2 source continuation
decisions.reason: Michael G. Slack’s 2001 Sibyl blackjack game translated to native C/OpenWatcom for OS/2. The rules implementation covers multi-deck shuffling, dealer/player scoring, splitting, doubling and insurance, with original Pascal retained.

decisions.title: Othello for OS/2 — native OS/2 source continuation
decisions.reason: Peter Wansch’s 1994 native Reversi game continued in OpenWatcom with preserved ICC sources. Its independent engine implements legal-move detection, disc flipping, positional evaluation and recursive multi-level computer search.

decisions.title: Kniffel for OS/2 — native OS/2 source continuation
decisions.reason: Andreas Kieser’s 1996–1999 VisPro/REXX Yahtzee-style dice game rebuilt in C for native OS/2 Presentation Manager. It supports one to five players and implements category scoring, held dice, bonus calculations and score lists.

decisions.title: PM Maze — native OS/2 source continuation
decisions.reason: James L. Dean’s 1988 native maze game, carried through a 2023 GCC/ArcaOS port and a 2026 OpenWatcom restoration. It generates window-sized mazes, tracks path/backtracking and computes a visible solution.

decisions.title: Mine/2 — native OS/2 source continuation
decisions.reason: Michael Bruestle’s 1997 native OS/2 Minesweeper game, maintained as a separate lineage from the already tracked Mine Sweeper/2 project. Its own PM field widget implements mine creation, neighbor counts, reveal/mark interactions and statistics.

decisions.title: TypeFast — native OS/2 source continuation
decisions.reason: Turgut Kalfaoglu’s 1992 OS/2 typing-practice game restored to OpenWatcom. The native PM program presents falling words and accepts typed input before they reach the bottom, retaining original source alongside the current port.

decisions.title: Game of Numbers — native OS/2 source continuation
decisions.reason: Dr. R. Grothmann’s native OS/2 arithmetic puzzle continued in OpenWatcom C++. Players combine six supplied numbers with arithmetic operations to reach a target; the implementation also searches for a solution.

decisions.title: DOSMid — native DOS MIDI/MUS player with CMS output
decisions.reason: Mateusz Viste’s low-requirement DOSMid music player extended by Tronix with Creative Music System/Game Blaster output and simple percussion. Real-mode C includes MIDI/MUS decoding, timing, hardware outputs and a substantial CMS voice/register implementation; this is a substantive native application branch.

decisions.title: QuuBee — reusable PC-98 browser and HLE-DOS platform
decisions.reason: Reusable browser player and test platform for floppy-era PC-98 freeware/doujin software. Integrates NP2kai hardware emulation with independently implemented DOS executable loading, INT 21h services, EXEC/TSR/MCB/XMS support, archive/FAT extraction and a browser UI. It accepts multiple user-supplied programs and is not a game-specific CPU wrapper.

decisions.title: Snyder C — preserved portable compiler
decisions.reason: Alan Snyder’s original portable C compiler archive, including machine-independent compiler phases, target descriptions, assembly runtime, ITS/WAITS/TOPS-20 variants and technical reports.

decisions.title: KCC — original PDP-10 C compiler source
decisions.reason: Preserves K. Chen and Ken Harrenstien/SRI’s PDP-10 C compiler, with parser, typed syntax trees, optimizers, register allocator and PDP-10 code generation.

decisions.title: Muddle / MDL — original language implementation archive
decisions.reason: Original MIT Muddle interpreter/compiler archives in PDP-10 MIDAS assembly, with 1970s SUMEX copies, TOPS-20 interpreter/compiler, manuals and later machine-independent MDL material.

decisions.title: Rutgers Common Lisp — TOPS-20 implementation archive
decisions.reason: Rutgers TOPS-20 Common Lisp distribution with Uppsala modifications, native bootstrap/LAP code, compiler and reader/library implementation, Flavors and Portable CommonLoops branches.

decisions.title: Rutgers Pascal — PDP-10 compiler and runtime sources
decisions.reason: Historical Rutgers Pascal compiler sources recovered from University of Utah, including Pascal compiler implementation, MACRO-10 runtime/debugger/I/O modules, command files and detailed manuals.

decisions.title: TENEX BCPL — BBN compiler source archive
decisions.reason: BBN’s native TENEX BCPL implementation, including BCPL parser/translator/code-generator sources, MACRO runtime support, compiler-generation command files and historical manuals.

decisions.title: F40 — DECSYSTEM-10 FORTRAN IV compiler source
decisions.reason: Original DEC FORTRAN IV compiler and LIB40 runtime sources, including FX compiler passes, native arithmetic/I/O libraries, assembly/link control files and manuals.

decisions.title: Harvard PPL — polymorphic-language source archive
decisions.reason: Preserves Harvard’s extensible interactive PPL implementation from SAIL/TENEX, including assembly interpreter/parser/runtime modules, build/link command files, manuals and an additional archived Unix distribution.

decisions.title: SITBOL — recovered PDP-10 SNOBOL4 implementation
decisions.reason: Recovered Stevens Institute SITBOL compiler/runtime modules, extracted from historical University of Arizona archive material, covering lexer, syntax, interpreter, strings, arrays, I/O and garbage collection.

decisions.title: TYMCOM-X — Tymshare PDP-10 operating-system source
decisions.reason: Substantial Tymshare PDP-10 monitor archives with scheduler, swapping/memory, filesystem, devices and many machine/site configuration variants, plus build control files and operational documentation.

decisions.title: FOONEX — Foonly TENEX-derived operating-system archive
decisions.reason: Foonly-specific TENEX-derived monitor source with changed scheduler, storage/forks/device code, MFEXEC command executive and F2/F3 microcode collections.

decisions.title: Ulm Modula-2 — historical m68k compiler toolchain
decisions.reason: ETH M2M-derived multi-pass Modula-2 compiler retargeted for Motorola 68020 Nixdorf Targon/31 and Sun-3/SunOS, with native runtime libraries, compiler driver and debugging/profiling utilities.

decisions.title: Interlisp-10 — original PDP-10 environment sources
decisions.reason: Original native PDP-10 Interlisp environment archive with MACRO-10 Lisp kernel, Interlisp compiler/editor/assembler/loadup sources, historical SUMEX/Linköping/PARC distributions and manuals.

decisions.title: MUXX — experimental PDP-11 operating system
decisions.reason: Original experimental Mostly Useless eXperimental eXecutive for DEC PDP-11, with C/assembly kernel, process creation and task loading, trap/MMU/clock handling, drivers, shell and sample tasks.

decisions.title: Q*bert — Amstrad Plus native edition
decisions.reason: Native Z80 implementation of the pyramid-hopping arcade concept for Amstrad Plus, with ASIC sprites, synthesized sound and separate cassette, disk and CPR cartridge packaging. Substantial native game implementation rather than emulation.

decisions.title: Sugar Byte — CPC match-three game
decisions.reason: Original 64K Amstrad CPC match-three game with special-candy combinations, diagonal gravity, obstacles, ingredient objectives, 60 levels and AY voice samples. Native Z80 source is the primary project; optional desktop emulator wrappers are secondary packaging.

decisions.title: GRAVASSIST — CPC gravity puzzle game
decisions.reason: Native CPC 6128 puzzle game in which a stick figure changes gravity in eight directions and walks around corners; rooms, hazards, doors and crates provide puzzle progression. Includes a separate optional .NET/browser room editor, without substituting emulation for the native game.

decisions.title: HOMEPLANET — CPC fleet-strategy game
decisions.reason: Native CPC 6128 fleet-strategy game featuring a shrinking refugee convoy, 3D ship rendering, squadrons, combat and cockpit/minigame sequences. Banked Z80 source and disk streaming are genuine target-specific implementations.

decisions.title: Goldorak GX4000 — native shooter source
decisions.reason: Large Z80 homebrew shooter based on Goldorak/Grendizer, targeting the CPC Plus ASIC and GX4000 cartridge system. Source covers movement, enemy waves, weapons, bosses, HUD, shop and ending sequences.

decisions.title: LUDIC break the loop — CPC and Enterprise game
decisions.reason: Source for the CPCRetroDev 2019 story-driven action/adventure game LUDIC, with contemporary CPC and Enterprise builds. Shared C gameplay and target wrappers implement native output for both Z80 computers.

decisions.title: Redsea — CPC submarine shooter
decisions.reason: Original Amstrad CPC single-player shoot-em-up produced by Gameroid students for CPCRetroDev 2018. Native Z80 source includes player/enemy/bullet/control/render modules, compressed tilemaps and interrupt-driven music.

decisions.title: Wire Run — CPC circuit-routing puzzle
decisions.reason: Original Pipe Mania-inspired electronic-circuit puzzle for CPC 6128, written in ugBASIC and cross-compiled to native Z80. Grid routing, piece placement, distance and win checking are implemented in the included BASIC source.

decisions.title: Don’t Dither! — BBC territory-control game
decisions.reason: Original two/four-player BBC Model B territory-control game whose ownership state is encoded in 35 CMYK dither patterns. Native 6502 game has tanks, paint splats, ink reservoirs, AI opponents, keyboard remapping and 32 level layouts.

decisions.title: Polymer Picker — BBC machine-code edition
decisions.reason: Substantial 6502 conversion of the author’s ecological BBC game, originally released in mixed BASIC/assembler in 2022. The new engine owns per-frame diver/fish/shark/jellyfish collision, oxygen, sound and score while BASIC retains setup, scenery and level flow.

decisions.title: Mutant Fly — recovered BBC BASIC and browser port
decisions.reason: Original author’s preservation and direct JavaScript port of FLY, published in The Micro User in July 1985. Includes detokenized/tokenized cassette source, a faithful classic browser presentation and an extended 3D game sharing line-number-annotated rules.

decisions.title: Galaforce — BBC to C64 source port
decisions.reason: Work-in-progress native C64 adaptation of Kevin Edwards’s released BBC Galaforce source. A substantial C64 implementation replaces hardware setup, bitmap rendering, keyboard input and sound while retaining real alien types, waves and flight-pattern data from the original.

decisions.title: FALLOUT.BAS — TRS-80 terminal-hacking game
decisions.reason: Native TRS-80 Model 4/4P recreation of Fallout’s terminal-hacking password puzzle, implemented in LS-DOS/TRSDOS BASIC with selectable difficulty and intelligence options. Complete readable listing plus interpreted, compiled and bootable disk forms are included.

decisions.title: Rayoïd — Atari ST original source
decisions.reason: Raymond Hill’s author-published 1992 Atari ST arcade game source, with single-player asteroid-style combat and a modem-linked two-player mode. The repository preserves original C plus extensive 68000 drawing, collision, input and modem routines, project definitions and a distributed PRG.

decisions.title: Sam Nasty — STOS game and level editor
decisions.reason: Jérôme Mahieux’s Atari ST board/puzzle game and level editor, originally dating to 1995 and released with complete STOS listings, assets and a Python floppy/source-template generator. This is the game implementation and editor, not just a launcher.

decisions.title: Zamboozal Poker Dice — STOS source archive
decisions.reason: Jeff and Steve Fulton’s 1990 Atari ST poker-dice game archive includes the original tokenized STOS BASIC GAME.BAS, compiled PRG, graphics, sound/data and detailed original instructions. Read-only structural analysis identifies the Lionpoulos STOS header and a complete ordered tokenized BASIC program, not merely a binary with incidental strings.

decisions.title: The Oil Game — historical GEM-PC source
decisions.reason: Author archive of the historical GEM-PC adaptation of an oil-company economic strategy game originally written for Atari ST GEM in the 1980s. The substantial C source tree preserves economics, drilling, transportation, newspaper events, GEM UI and IBM DOS compatibility routines; comments include 1986 development dates. This record covers the recovered PC implementation, not an established native Atari ST build.

decisions.title: Amiga Tools — Peter Heinrich historical source
decisions.reason: Author-released 1990–1993 Amiga tools: Hunk executable/object inspector, Hunkhack self-decompressing-file manipulator, UnStuff Macintosh SIT extractor, DXF-to-SDF Sega CD model converter and line-ending converter. C implementations preserve real parsing and conversion logic.

decisions.title: ArcadeGameSelector 2 — Amiga menu source
decisions.reason: Per Olofsson’s joystick-operated native Amiga game menu, with OCS/AGA layouts, directory navigation, responsive asynchronous IFF screenshots, slideshows, per-game scripts and configuration. Full Amiga E sources are provided for launcher, menu and helper.

decisions.title: Untangle — native Amiga puzzle source
decisions.reason: Grzegorz Kraszewski’s system-friendly native Amiga implementation of the line-untangling graph puzzle, containing window/menu interaction through Amiga Intuition, coordinate transforms, graph generation/solving tests and level loading.

decisions.title: Synthwave — AmigaOS game framework
decisions.reason: Robin Southern’s native AmigaOS 3.x C game framework supplies event, time, memory, window, input and planar/chunky framebuffer implementations, including a 68000-family chunky-to-planar assembly component. This is a reusable native framework, not an emulator wrapper.

decisions.title: Blitlife — Atari ST BLiTTER Life
decisions.reason: Keli Hlodversson’s Conway’s Game of Life implementation performs cellular-automaton work using the Atari ST BLiTTER, wrapped in a GEM application. Source includes BLiTTER register definitions, counting tables, update routines and window/display code.

decisions.title: PySprint — Atari ST Super Sprint reconstruction
decisions.reason: Python/Pygame reimplementation of the Atari ST edition of Super Sprint, aiming to reproduce original gameplay while adding custom cars/tracks/music and improving waits and controls. The source implements vehicle dynamics, collisions, track logic, AI opponents, menus and asset managers.

decisions.title: Atari ST Vector Tank — original prototype source
decisions.reason: Alan Richardson’s early-1990s Atari ST tank/vector-game prototype, released by its author with C and 68000 assembly for vector graphics, line drawing and joystick handling, plus historical object and PRG files.

decisions.title: IKBD4GFA — Atari ST input subsystem
decisions.reason: Sandor Drieënhuizen’s reusable Atari ST 68000 assembly subsystem exposes keyboard scan/ASCII tables, last scan code and two joystick states to GFA BASIC via an inline binary and documented fixed jump table. Full assembly and GFA demo are included.

decisions.title: Amiga Assembly Space Adventures
decisions.reason: Native Amiga 500 space-shooter homebrew in 68000 assembly, with direct custom-chip video/DMA/sound, double buffers, player/enemy/laser logic, lives, score and title/game-over screens. Includes source modules and raw graphics/audio assets.

decisions.title: S1C88 C Tools for Pokémon Mini
decisions.reason: Cross-platform installation/build integration for the EPSON/TASKING S1C88 compiler, including Pokémon Mini headers, locator configuration, startup assembly and an executable hello-world source example. This is an SDK integration project, not a reconstruction of the proprietary compiler.

decisions.title: mindis2 — Pokémon Mini ROM disassembler
decisions.reason: Python control-flow-aware Pokémon Mini binary disassembler with explicit opcode tables, BIOS mode, symbol input, user entrypoints and execution-path output.

decisions.title: minlibtowav — Pokémon Mini music extractor
decisions.reason: Python decoder/converter for Pokémon Mini Minlib song streams, reconstructing note duration, pitch and duty-cycle information and emitting WAV or MIDI.

decisions.title: Pokémon Mini Tile Tool
decisions.reason: Tkinter desktop graphics-conversion tool that previews bitmap tiles and generates Pokémon Mini tile and masked sprite byte data.

decisions.title: Pokémon Mini C graphics and input libraries
decisions.reason: Header-based S1C88 support library with hardware registers, inline assembly pixel plotting, character/font rendering, key polling and scrollable tile-map routines.

decisions.title: BUFO — Channel F road-and-river homebrew
decisions.reason: Original 2 KiB Channel F road-and-river crossing game written from scratch in Fairchild F8 assembly; includes palette tests, branch-range checks and emulator snapshot-analysis tools.

decisions.title: Fairchild VES WebAssembly emulator frontend
decisions.reason: Rust/WebAssembly Channel F emulator application with browser canvas video, audio, controller/front-panel handling and URL-based BIOS/cartridge loading, using the same author’s separately sourced chips::fairchild_f8 board core.

decisions.title: FreeChaF — reusable Channel F emulator core
decisions.reason: Portable libretro Channel F emulator created by David Richardson, with a complete F8 instruction implementation, memory/port/video/audio/controller models and optional BIOS high-level routines.

decisions.title: ExtFriend — WonderSwan EXT USB firmware
decisions.reason: RP2040 firmware turning the WonderSwan EXT port into USB serial and digital stereo audio devices; dual-core TinyUSB service plus UART, PIO and DMA hardware handling.

decisions.title: DSP Emulator — Pascal multi-system emulator
decisions.reason: Long-running Delphi/Lazarus emulator suite with native Pascal CPU and device implementations and reusable arcade, computer and console drivers, including relatively uncommon Casio PV-1000 and Super Cassette Vision.

decisions.title: Gearlynx Debugger — Lynx source-level VS Code extension
decisions.reason: Independent TypeScript DAP frontend for cc65 Lynx programs, driving Gearlynx through TCP debug-monitor and framebuffer protocols; source/symbol parsing, breakpoints, stepping, overlay selection and memory visualization.

decisions.title: Sadist (1998 DOS source)
decisions.reason: Author-published recovery of Grzegorz Drozd’s 1998–1999 Polish DOS game; the main Pascal implementation includes character physics, combat and environmental effects, with graphics, sound, mouse and XMS units.

decisions.title: In The Dark
decisions.reason: Original 2022 survival roguelike sharing dungeon, item, monster and player implementation across CP/M, 16-bit DOS and modern Pascal targets; this is an original game, unrelated to Alone in the Dark.

decisions.title: Paybacktime 2
decisions.reason: Preservation of the 1994–1997 multiplayer, isometric, turn-based DOS tactics game by Niko Nevatie and Kari Luojus, including the game, editors and original Turbo Pascal/i386 assembler source.

decisions.title: GameMinder
decisions.reason: Original lightweight DOS game launcher created in 2022, with metadata filtering, play-time tracking and a PathMinder-inspired text UI. Pascal implementation launches games using a separately credited ExecWithSwap module.

decisions.title: Fruit Popper!
decisions.reason: Original two-player MS-DOS action game by Gered King for the June 2021 GDR 4x4x4 challenge, with a Pascal state machine, match simulation, map editor, assets and GDlib mode-13h routines.

decisions.title: Bob’s Fury
decisions.reason: Ongoing Pascal version of Andrew Danson’s DOS platform game, started around 1999 and retaining levels from his earlier QBasic version. Includes engine, XT and standard builds, level editor, graphics modes and sound drivers.

decisions.title: PUDR (Pohřební ústav)
decisions.reason: Original Czech graphical/text adventure for PC XT, DOS, CGA and mouse, created for and winning the 2019 DOS game competition. The Pascal implementation includes parser/command regions, inventory, room logic and graphics objects.

decisions.title: Wake on LAN for Windows 3.1
decisions.reason: Preserved Pascal source of Depicus’s Windows 3.1 Wake-on-LAN utility, with VCL application/forms and a component implementing socket-based magic-packet transmission.

decisions.title: PointDBF 96 Delphi password-dialog component
decisions.reason: Author-published source accompanying Patrick Prémartin’s January 1999 PointDBF article: a Delphi VCL login/password-change component and demonstration applications, with event hooks for application-defined password handling.

decisions.title: FONTSEL DOS font selector
decisions.reason: Assembly reimplementation of the IBM PS/2 Model 30-286 font-selector experience for ordinary VGA DOS machines, with live preview, font loading and a persistent INT 10h/INT 2Fh TSR.

decisions.title: DiskLamp 3.17 source
decisions.reason: Author-published 1991–1993 DOS resident utility source for visual disk-activity indication and selective drive read/write restrictions, implemented by hooking BIOS INT 13h.

decisions.title: DOS APM Control
decisions.reason: Small original real-mode DOS COM utility suite implementing shutdown, standby and suspend through the APM 1.0–1.2 BIOS interface, with basic error reporting.

decisions.title: doskeys / kbd
decisions.reason: Original low-level keyboard scan-code diagnostic for DOS, with IRQ1 handling and an alternative standalone boot-sector mode; build tooling can package it into FreeDOS floppy/CD images.

decisions.title: DosGameMenu
decisions.reason: Original graphical DOS game menu in QuickBASIC, enumerating game subfolders, displaying thumbnails and launching PLAY.BAT, plus helper tools storing long game names inside reserved bitmap palette entries.

decisions.title: Toadman 2: Space Shock
decisions.reason: Preserved original 1.0 source of Joe King’s 2000 Delta Code BASIC action game, with one/two-player combat, laser guns, maps, sprites and a Toadman 1-to-2 map conversion program.

decisions.title: Multics MR12.7 — revived system source archive
decisions.reason: Source copied from an operating MR12.7 Multics instance and reconstructed from simulated backup tapes with mxload; preserves and extends the Bull HN/MIT source release, including substantial PL/I and ALM system implementations.

decisions.title: B Compiler Collection — x86-64 and BESM-6 language tools
decisions.reason: Collection of BCause, a single-pass B-to-x86-64 compiler, and bbesm, a B-written compiler for BESM-6 under Dubna; also preserves the PDP-7 B compiler that bbesm explicitly derives from.

decisions.title: Elbrous-B PCC — recovered 1988 compiler backend
decisions.reason: PCC revival tree containing a substantial Elbrous-B machine backend and runtime startup sources; local.c/local2.c retain MIPT 1988 Serge Vakulenko headers and actual stack-machine code generation.

decisions.title: Banay Smalltalk-80 — Bluebook C++ virtual machine
decisions.reason: Independent by-the-Bluebook C++ implementation of the 16-bit Smalltalk-80 VM, object memory, BitBlt and SDL host integration; restores use of Xerox release-2 images and source browsing via a POSIX filesystem layer.

decisions.title: ST80 — Java Smalltalk-80 V2 and DV6 virtual machine
decisions.reason: Independent Java-8 translation of the Bluebook VM with normal and Stretch object memory, Alto disk emulation, and Tajo/XDE filesystem emulation; supports original V2, DV6 and converted Analyst images.

decisions.title: Crosstalk — bare-metal Raspberry Pi Smalltalk-80 port
decisions.reason: Hardware-specific port of Dan Banay’s Smalltalk-80 VM to Circle, replacing desktop SDL/OS facilities with Raspberry Pi kernel, framebuffer, USB input and SD/FAT storage integration.

decisions.title: Smalltalk-80 by the Book — Pharo-hosted VM
decisions.reason: Independent implementation of the complete Bluebook Smalltalk-80 VM and environment in Smalltalk itself, with Tonel-format interpreter, object memory, BitBlt, display and filesystem adapters for Pharo.

decisions.title: jff-algol — restored ALGOL 60 to C translator
decisions.reason: Author’s 2002–2003 hobby compiler recovered from old disk archives and updated; full C frontend maps ALGOL-60 scope, arrays, call-by-name and procedures into C with a driver and runtime.

decisions.title: Awe — ALGOL W compiler and runtime
decisions.reason: OCaml compiler and C runtime implementing the June-1972 ALGOL W language description and intended to compile OS/360 ALGOL W programs with little or no modification.

decisions.title: X1 ALGOL — Dijkstra compiler revival and simulator
decisions.reason: Revives Dijkstra’s 1960 Electrologica X1 ALGOL compiler through preserved Pascal transcription and p2c-derived C, bundled with an X1-like simulator, procedure library, decoding tools and tests.

decisions.title: Algol-68RS a68toc — historical compiler continuation
decisions.reason: Portable RSRE/DRA ALGOL-68RS frontend extracted from ELLA and continued from Sian Mountbatten’s Linux port, with ALGOL68 sources, generated C, runtime preludes and self-hosting build path.

decisions.title: Oberon System — LuaJIT and Qt hosted port
decisions.reason: Port of the historical Oberon System to an Oberon-to-LuaJIT compiler/runtime and Qt backend, preserving substantial text/viewer/editor/application modules and replacing original inner system services.

decisions.title: OP2 — restored Oberon System 3 cross-compiler
decisions.reason: Restores OP2 from Native Oberon 2.3.7 Alpha, converts native file format to UTF-8, refactors machine dependence, and adds standalone C99 compiler builds plus ARMv7 and RV32 code generators and bootlinkers.

decisions.title: Inferno — Bell Labs distributed OS source continuation
decisions.reason: Full Bell Labs/Vita Nuova Inferno system source including native and hosted kernels, Dis VM, Limbo compiler, libraries, device services and applications, maintained as a portable distributed operating environment.

decisions.title: TRS-80 Level II BASIC ROM reconstruction and enhancements
decisions.reason: Commented Z80 reconstruction of TRS-80 Model I/III Level II BASIC ROMs, with enhanced variants and EACA System-80 support. The author explicitly identifies the material as a derivative disassembly rather than original Microsoft/Tandy source.

decisions.title: Princess and Frog — Ed Fries Atari source release
decisions.reason: Preservation release of Ed Fries’ Romox Atari 8-bit game, with original source disk and Kay Savetz’s exported text files. Kept as one source-release family.

decisions.title: ATasm — Mac/65-compatible Atari cross-assembler
decisions.reason: Reusable C cross-assembler implementing Mac/65-compatible syntax, macros, Atari directives, binary/image output and emulator-state injection. Selected maintained Peter Hinz fork as the single ATasm lineage record.

decisions.title: CoCo Tools — BASIC translation and image conversion
decisions.reason: Expanded maintained Python collection for TRS-80 Color Computer software development. Its substantial DECB-to-BASIC09 translator is beyond the small image-conversion ancestor; retained as one CoCo Tools family record.

decisions.title: sdcc-msx — shared MSX/Linux development framework
decisions.reason: C/assembly development framework with MSX hardware backend, SDL host backend, Konami-5 mapper linker and font/MIDI conversion utilities. It lets the same application sources be tested on Linux then compiled to MSX cartridges.

decisions.title: File-Hunter Browser — native MSX network downloader
decisions.reason: Native MSX-DOS browser/downloader for the file-hunter.com archive, with search/type/generation filters, MSX2 text interface and UNAPI TCP/IP transfer code.

decisions.title: m100LE — Wordle for Model 100 family
