decisions.reason: Commented native BASIC Wordle-like game for Tandy Model 100 and related Kyocera/NEC/Olivetti machines, with compressed yearly dictionaries and platform-specific terminal/date handling.

decisions.title: NEON REVENANT — native MSX rail-shooter family
decisions.reason: Native MSX pseudo-3D rail shooter with separate MSX1, MSX2, Turbo R/V9958, V9990 and experimental V9968/Geo3D configurations. One family record prevents counting each hardware experiment as a new game.

decisions.title: MSXgl — native MSX game library and build tools
decisions.reason: Configurable C/Z80 game-development runtime covering MSX graphics, input, audio, storage and memory banking, plus build and asset tools. Many sample games/demos are examples within one reusable library project.

decisions.title: Cross-Lib — portable 8-bit game library and games
decisions.reason: Portable C game library with target-specific graphics/input/sound and a coordinated game collection including Cross Chase, Shoot, Bomber, Snake and Horde. Canonical upstream supersedes the stale miguelqvd/CROSS-CHASE fork discovered first.

decisions.title: Batman — Acorn Archimedes ARM port prototype
decisions.reason: An independently written ARM implementation of the Amiga Batman game with converted graphics, scrolling tile maps, compiled sprites, player movement/collision tests and projectile updates. This is a partial game port, not the already tracked MarkyTurtle Amiga source reconstruction.

decisions.title: ADiffView — native Amiga text comparison viewer
decisions.reason: A native C++ side-by-side text-file difference viewer with an Amiga GUI, Myers-derived diff engine, selection/search/navigation and background worker code.

decisions.title: AmiExpress 5 — Amiga E BBS rewrite
decisions.reason: Darren Coles’s substantial Amiga E rewrite of the historical AmiExpress BBS, authorised to use the name by the former rights holder. Includes the node/controller, setup/user tools, file-transfer protocols, mail, FTP and HTTP services.

decisions.title: DiskMaster2 — Amiga file manager source archive
decisions.reason: Rudolph Riedel’s maintained source and historical release archives for Greg Cunningham’s DiskMaster2 file manager, including the later C and AmigaOS4 adaptation, command processing, windows, preferences and ARexx support.

decisions.title: FrexxEd — programmable Amiga text editor
decisions.reason: Daniel Stenberg and Kjell Ericson’s historical Amiga editor sources, continued by Vidar Hokstad, with editing/undo, text folding, scriptable FPL integration, ARexx and syntax-sensitive display.

decisions.title: MagicMenu — native Amiga menu enhancer
decisions.reason: Historical open-source Intuition menu enhancer with popup-menu drawing, remapping, preference editor, menu hooks and screen/bitmap management.

decisions.title: NiKom — Amiga KOM-style BBS
decisions.reason: Niklas Lindholm’s Swedish KOM-model Amiga BBS, originally developed 1990–1996, later maintained by Tomas Kärki, and revived from NiKom 1.60 sources in 2015. Contains node/server code, conferences, file areas, Fido support and utility libraries.

decisions.title: SimpleMail — Amiga-family mail client
decisions.reason: Hynek Schlawack and Sebastian Bauer’s open-source MUI mail client with POP3, IMAP, SMTP, MIME handling, configuration, address book and Amiga-family platform backends.

decisions.title: YAM — Yet Another Mailer
decisions.reason: Long-running Amiga-family MIME mail user agent, begun by Marcel Beck in 1995 and continued by the YAM team, with MUI GUI, POP3/SMTP transport, folders, identities, filters, encryption integration and ARexx.

decisions.title: Planet Rocklobster — Amiga OCS demo and framework
decisions.reason: Oxyron’s Amiga OCS demo source plus reusable trackmo framework: floppy track loader, Doynamite-derived 68k depacker, P61 player, memory manager, effect launcher and many individual demo parts, with host asset tools.

decisions.title: FakeJoystick — RISC OS joystick simulation module
decisions.reason: Chris Bazley’s native RISC OS relocatable module implements joystick SWIs using keypad input, with switched, analogue and damped modes, chiefly to test game joystick support without hardware.

decisions.title: ADF tools — native Amiga floppy read/write/copy
decisions.reason: Three native Amiga commands read floppy tracks into ADF images, write ADF images to real drives and copy disks with verification, backed by shared track-device I/O code.

decisions.title: Avalanche — Amiga ReAction archive manager
decisions.reason: Native ReAction GUI for xadmaster, xfdmaster and Deark with tabbed archive browsing/extraction, LhA/Zip modification, optional virus scanning, disk images and ARexx integration.

decisions.title: iGame — Amiga WHDLoad game launcher
decisions.reason: MUI frontend for organising and launching Amiga WHDLoad games and demos, with repository scanning, metadata/properties, game images and several native CPU/OS builds.

decisions.title: GoSnap — Amiga Workbench window snapping
decisions.reason: Amiga E commodity that monitors window drags and snaps/resizes windows at screen edges and corners, including screen-change notifications, configurable zones and Shift bypass.

decisions.title: Banana Ghost
decisions.reason: Original WIP LynxJam 2021 game with a ghost, explorer, holes, maze gates, level maps, title and results screens. game.c contains native sprite structures, explorer states and level/game processing rather than a ROM wrapper.

decisions.title: Space Invaders for Atari Lynx
decisions.reason: Native Space Invaders-style WIP with moving enemy formations, player shots, linked-list bombs, collision flags, bunkers and joystick-controlled player. This is an authored C adaptation, not an Intel 8080 reconstruction.

decisions.title: AC2016 Atari Lynx contribution
decisions.reason: Native Game & Watch-style Lynx game with two game modes, segmented number sprites, score, rabbit position, cocotte timer, lives and action-speed state. ingame.c is substantive implementation and generated assembly is also retained.

decisions.title: TreeJumper
decisions.reason: Commented educational native Lynx game with animated boy/tree sprites, jump arcs, collision and falling state, score/lives, intro and sound. A distinct game-level implementation on a reusable template.

decisions.title: Airaki
decisions.reason: Full native tile-matching RPG/puzzle game released in 2014. Assembly contains horizontal/vertical matching, board solvability checks, combat, animation, sound and link multiplayer, with art and auxiliary checksum tool.

decisions.title: Aqua and Ashes
decisions.reason: Native Game Boy game prototype inspired by the football section of Tiny Toons Adventures: Buster Busts Loose. Includes fixed-point object acceleration, active-object bitfields, animation, sprites, joypad and smooth parallax/background implementation.

decisions.title: Game Boy Color Shader ROM
decisions.reason: Real-time native GBC lighting shader demo. Assembly computes simplified dot products with log-space cosine/power lookup tables, run-length encoded normal data and packed Game Boy tile output; Python prepares normal-map sequences.

decisions.title: hng64kit
decisions.reason: Very early native Hyper Neo Geo 64 SDK with MIPS startup/vector setup, TLB/core initialization, linker/build rules and an implemented Go ELF-to-cartridge ROM packer. The empty sample is only an example of the reusable SDK, not a separate game.

decisions.title: Neo Geo Rapid Fire Tester
decisions.reason: Native controller test application that counts presses of a selected button over ten seconds. Actual C state machine reads BIOS current/previous input, detects rising edges, tracks VBlank time and displays totals.

decisions.title: Virtua Skimmer
decisions.reason: Native 3D skimboarding game WIP: wave movement, board and character meshes, trick rotations, fall/landing checks, input and scoring. Repository contains several historical variants of the same game; selected .03 code is substantive Jo Engine implementation.

decisions.title: Checkers — OS/2 Presentation Manager source continuation
decisions.reason: Charles Petzold’s September 1990 Microsoft Systems Journal checkers game, preserved with its original sources and a 2026 Open Watcom 32-bit PM continuation. The implementation includes board/judge windows, legal-move generation, recursive jump enumeration and a threaded computer strategy.

decisions.title: Asteroid — Todd Crowe’s native OS/2 game continuation
decisions.reason: Todd B. Crowe’s native OS/2 vector-style Asteroids clone, updated for Open Watcom and ArcaOS. This is the OS/2 game’s source continuation, distinct from the Atari arcade disassembly and unrelated Asteroids homebrews already catalogued. The implementation has game modes, two-player scoring, motion/drawing helpers and configurable keyboard/mouse/joystick input.

decisions.title: JigSaw — OS/2 Toolkit sample restoration
decisions.reason: Restoration and 32-bit OS/2 PM continuation of Microsoft’s 1988 OS/2 Toolkit JIGSAW sample. It slices a BMP into 36 draggable pieces and preserves GPI retained-segment transforms, piece/island manipulation, zooming and asynchronous drawing. The original 16-bit source is retained in legacy; this is unrelated to the similarly named Jigsaw electronic-puzzle game already indexed.

decisions.title: PM Equator — OS/2 arithmetic-puzzle source continuation
decisions.reason: Frank Sven Nestel’s 1995–2001 PM arithmetic-puzzle game and associated generator/evaluator/solver sources, updated in 2026 for Open Watcom. Actual source implements several legal equation families, randomized puzzle generation, evaluation and a threaded Presentation Manager interface.

decisions.title: Jeu de Taquin — 16-to-32-bit OS/2 puzzle port
decisions.reason: Charles Petzold’s magazine-published 1989 OS/2 15-puzzle code, continued as a 32-bit PM application. Source handles row/column tile slides, blank tracking, scramble/reset, solved-state detection and the elapsed timer, with 2026 localization and settings additions.

decisions.title: Boggle — native OS/2 C reconstruction and source archive
decisions.reason: David Boudah/Bou Software Systems’ 1996 IBM Open Class Boggle game, with original C++ preserved under legacy and a 2026 plain-C PM rewrite. Board source implements Fisher-Yates dice shuffling and Qu handling; dictionary and UI modules validate words and run the timed game without the original IBM C++ class libraries.

decisions.title: ZeroPoint — 1990s polygon game and OS/2 SDL2 port
decisions.reason: Enumerate Inc.’s 1996–1999 polygon-stopping game, preserving its original V GUI/X11/Windows95 C++ sources and a 2026 OS/2 SDL2 front end. Polygon and walk classes maintain vertices and motion; the new main loop handles input, menus, timed bonuses, lives and drawing.

decisions.title: Mastermind/2 — OS/2 single-executable source continuation
decisions.reason: Rene Auberger’s 1999 native OS/2 Mastermind game, with its legacy C source and a 2026 Open Watcom continuation that consolidates the language/resource DLL design into one executable. Source renders guess rows, drag/drop pins, exact/color-only feedback, timers and high scores.

decisions.title: Birdman — native OS/2 shooting-game source continuation
decisions.reason: Mike of Vienna’s 1998 OS/2 bird-shooting game, preserved with original C and an Open Watcom/ArcaOS continuation. The PM message procedure moves bird sprites, performs mouse hit tests, counts kills, supports the all-birds action and manages pause/focus/timer state.

decisions.title: Bingo/2 — multimedia OS/2 source continuation
decisions.reason: E. L. Zapanta’s IBM-era 1992–1994 native 32-bit OS/2 bingo game, preserved with original C and a 2026 Open Watcom build. Source contains randomized card/number creation, multiple bingo-pattern checks, score tracking, printing, virtual hall players and MMPM/2 sound support.

decisions.title: Rollball — multithreaded OS/2 game source continuation
decisions.reason: Stangl Roman’s 1992 ball-rolling OS/2 PM game, including its 2017 anniversary-era source and a 2026 Open Watcom continuation. The draw thread manages the playfield, weighted random symbols, deflectors, holes, movement and points while the UI accepts mouse input and maintains settings.

decisions.title: PM Robots — native OS/2 puzzle-game source continuation
decisions.reason: Kent Lundberg’s 1993–2002 native OS/2 Presentation Manager version of robots, continued for ArcaOS. GAME.C implements robot pursuit, collisions forming heaps, legal moves, teleport, sonic screwdriver, scoring and level progression; separate source covers PM UI and high scores.

decisions.title: Cribbage — Sibyl OS/2 card-game source archive
decisions.reason: Michael G. Slack’s OS/2 Sibyl/Object Pascal cribbage game source archive, with an engine tracing back through a DOS Turbo Pascal port to David Addison’s Amiga A-basic game. The recovered OS/2 engine scores hands and play, recommends discards and chooses computer cards; visual forms, configuration and resources are included.

decisions.title: ADV98 — native PC-98 adventure-game engine
decisions.reason: New native PC-98 MS-DOS adventure engine by PokuG/Yarufu. It interprets Shift-JIS story scripts with branching, choices, flags and save/load, drives PC-98 planar graphics and GRCG output, and optionally uses PMD BGM and DOS mouse input. This is native homebrew, distinct from recovered ADV98V commercial-engine research.

decisions.title: B5500 Software — recovered compilers, interpreters and utilities
decisions.reason: Independent preservation repository containing transcriptions and tape-derived source for Burroughs B5500 software, including University of Washington APL, Wirth EULER, Heriot-Watt Pascal, SNOBOL, Lisp, system patches and CUBE user-library tapes. Substantial recovered implementations and per-program provenance distinguish this from an emulator-only record.

decisions.title: NOAA 940 BASIC — recovered compiler and runtime
decisions.reason: Howard Bussey preserves the SDS-940 BASIC implementation he extended at NOAA around 1970 with formatted output, multiple file I/O and strings. Source returned through the Hawaii BCC-500 lineage contains the compiler, runtime and scratch-page sections rather than a modern BASIC clone.

decisions.title: CP/67 CMS — tape-recovered operating-system sources
decisions.reason: Recovered original CMS assembler source, macro definitions and assembly listings from old CP/67-format tapes. Recovery used VM/370 and z/VM conversion before ASCII extraction. The repository name mentions CP/67; inspected payload is specifically CMS, with source headers dated 1973 as well as older material, not a verified complete CP kernel.

decisions.title: LISP 1.5 — IBM 7090 card-deck reconstruction
decisions.reason: Pascal Bourguignon reconstructs the 1961 IBM 7090 LISP 1.5 punched-card source from Bonnie’s Birthday Assembly listing, preserving card layout and known typographical quirks while generating some tables and inferring five obscured cards. Includes original listing PDF, reconstructed assembly, generator Lisp, assembler patches and run recipe.

decisions.title: aap LISP 1.5 — manual-derived C implementation
decisions.reason: Independent C reimplementation of LISP 1.5 as described in its manual, with eval and evalquote REPLs, reader, evaluator, cons-cell memory management and library examples. This is neither a mirror nor the IBM 7090 card transcription.

decisions.title: TiogaViewer — Xerox Cedar/Mesa source-file viewer
decisions.reason: C++/Qt tool decodes the Tioga rich-text file format used for most Xerox Cedar/Mesa archived sources, displays documentation and syntax-highlighted source, and supplies a Cedar lexer plus experimental parser. Derived partly from archived Andrew/Emacs decoder plugins to make the 1993 Solaris Cedar tree inspectable.

decisions.title: Conway Squasher — historical coroutine assembly ports
decisions.reason: Reimplements the asterisk-squasher coroutine example from Melvin Conway’s 1963 compiler paper in modern x86/x86-64 assembly, with Linux, macOS and Windows versions, both subroutine and coroutine styles and smoke-test fixtures. Focused historical programming-technique reconstruction rather than a full compiler.

decisions.title: A940 — Elixir SDS-940 cross-assembler
decisions.reason: Elixir implementation of an SDS-940 assembler with opcode map, lexical and expression parsing, symbol resolution, pseudo-operations, relocatable address handling and assembly listing output. README is boilerplate, but substantive assembler implementation and tests establish its purpose.

decisions.title: simTSS — SDS-940 user-mode time-sharing simulator
decisions.reason: Elixir SDS-940 user-mode simulator with CPU execution, memory mapping, process/machine state and host-side SYSPOP implementation. Phoenix umbrella provides surrounding application infrastructure. Scope is running many user programs rather than reconstructing a complete original TSS kernel.

decisions.title: SIM_LGP30 — Python machine simulator and debugger
decisions.reason: Neil Higgins’s reusable Python LGP-30 simulator models instructions, drum memory, Flexowriter input/output, paper-tape and Intel HEX loading, with interactive debugging controls and recovered program examples. Its stated goal is a hackable simulator suited to future MicroPython use rather than cycle accuracy.

decisions.title: XASM_LGP30 — symbolic Python cross-assembler
decisions.reason: Neil Higgins’s two-pass LGP-30 cross-assembler provides structural validation, symbols and expressions, directives, formatted listings and Intel HEX binary output. Modernized syntax intentionally differs from the historical native assemblers.

decisions.title: HEX2TAPE_LGP30 — Intel HEX to native tape converter
decisions.reason: Companion Python tool converts sparse Intel HEX LGP-30 binaries into v-formatted LGP-30 paper-tape text, preserving start address in Stop and Transfer records. Implementation groups segments into chunks, writes tape headers and encodes the machine’s nonstandard hexadecimal alphabet.

decisions.title: Panchenko LGP-30 — C emulator, assembler and REPL
decisions.reason: Reusable C11 LGP-30 core with drum rotational timing, all instruction implementations, Flexowriter/simplified I/O interfaces, integrated assembler and memory-image format, plus batch CLI and interactive debugger. Independent implementation has tests and detailed manual-linked instruction semantics.

decisions.title: LGP-ASM — Go symbolic LGP-30 assembler
decisions.reason: Compact independent Go assembler for LGP-30 source with labels, opcode/order table, literal packing, multiple number notations, two-pass symbol replacement and native-word emission. Unit tests exercise literals and parsing; implemented tool distinct from the author’s browser-emulator code.

decisions.title: Wolves
decisions.reason: Native turn-based wolf-pack survival strategy game for the Commodore C64, Plus/4 and Commander CX16. C gameplay implements prey spawning and movement, wolf selection, energy costs, catching prey, scoring and ten levels, with separate machine I/O implementations.

decisions.title: Electron Adventure
decisions.reason: Native 6502 graphical adventure engine and playable technology demo for Acorn Electron/BBC Micro Model B, inspired by the style of Sierra AGI. Includes a custom script bytecode VM, synonym-aware text parser, tiled backgrounds, sprites and compressed tape loading; this is an original engine, not a recovered AGI interpreter.

decisions.title: Crawlers
decisions.reason: Large native MSX multiplayer snake game with up to eight players, battle/training game states, forty levels, score codes, sound and joystick-adapter support. Implemented in C using MSXgl, with substantial game code and data rather than an engine-only sample.

decisions.title: Edelweiss
decisions.reason: Substantial native MSX adventure/action game source with a banked overworld, title sequence, scrolling tile renderer, sprites, collision system, inventory/weapons, NPCs and enemy entities. C implementation coordinates segmented modules and interrupt-driven display updates.

decisions.title: Atalanta
decisions.reason: MSX2 graphical/text adventure adapted in C from a Spanish-book BASIC listing called Neutronia. Includes English and French versions, graphics, parser vocabulary, location/action state, sound and MSX-DOS disk distributions.

decisions.title: Big Blast
decisions.reason: Historical original MSX Asteroids-like game by Eric Boon and Manuel Bilderbeek, preserved as C source with CVS-era revision headers. Contains ship/asteroid/UFO objects, bullets, explosions, collision detection, scoring, shield-energy and level/bonus handling.

decisions.title: MZ3D2 / Angrybot
decisions.reason: Native MSX turbo R raycasting demo game by Wouter Vermaelen and Artrag, also released as ANGRYBOT.COM. Implements fixed-point 64-column ray casting, textured/flat drawing, sprite rendering, movement clipping, dungeon loading and NPC behavior in C with performance-critical Z80 assembly.

decisions.title: Speeb
decisions.reason: Native Amstrad CPC 464 runner by The CiAO Project, written in Z80 assembly with CPCTelera. Separate managers/systems implement scrolling grassfield, levels, player/enemy entities, AI control, physics, collisions, sound, menus, death and victory/restart flow.

decisions.title: Super Tongue Dino / Super Tongueboy
decisions.reason: Native CPCRetroDev 2019 Amstrad CPC platform game, titled Super Tongueboy in README and Super Tongue Dino in source/configuration. Assembly entity system includes level/obstacle managers, invisibility, player input, enemy behavior, physics, collisions, rendering, deaths and in-game menus.

decisions.title: TradAms
decisions.reason: Native Amstrad CPC 464 roguelike/dungeon-action shooter in Z80 assembly using CPCTelera. Game loop generates levels and rooms, updates player/enemies/attacks, checks bullet, stairs, doors, object and actor collisions, and handles room changes, HUD and game-over state.

decisions.title: Cannibalator
decisions.reason: Original CPC RetroDev 2016 Amstrad action game source dump with player platform movement, enemy behaviors, collisions, level data, graphics, sound and interrupt routines. Includes a coherent main assembly unit with included subsystems and level/enemy initialization.

decisions.title: The Grenade's Conquest
decisions.reason: Native Amstrad CPC two-player arena-action game from SubXplosion’s 2016 academic project. Large C implementation handles characters Jimmy/Obdulia, controls, movement/collisions, ammunition, shots, keys/doors, arena blocks, rounds, score, menus and music.

decisions.title: Zoo Clean / Zoo Care
decisions.reason: Native Amstrad CPC zoo-themed action/collection game in C. The source menu calls it Zoo Clean (and retains Scape text), while repository is zoo-care. Gameplay includes directional movement, bait/attack controls, guard/enemy state behavior, collectibles, cage-opening objectives, lives and level changes.

decisions.title: Murder — native Amiga adventure
decisions.reason: Original work-in-progress Sierra-style point-and-click adventure for Amiga. Native C includes room loading, text handling, images, custom screen/UI abstraction and a separate vocabulary/room-data compiler. Distinct title from commercial Murder! and from the author's Parrot project.

decisions.title: Astralbound — native Amiga space trader
decisions.reason: Original solid-polygon space-trading/combat prototype inspired by Frontier: Elite II. Contains substantial original universe generation, terrain renderer, physics, ports, contracts, combat, save state and ECS/AGA/RTG Amiga backends, rather than an emulated original game.

decisions.title: Jupiter Lander — Paul Grebenc Amiga source
decisions.reason: Preserved original 1993 Amiga game source by Paul Grebenc, uploaded by its author. Full C game loop includes thrust, collision, landing pads, scoring, BOB graphics, keyboard/audio and memory services. This is an independent Amiga implementation, not the indexed C64 Jupiter Lander disassembly.

decisions.title: iGameLite — native Amiga game launcher
decisions.reason: Compact native custom-screen Amiga game launcher experiment by MrZammler. C source implements manifest/game-list display, gameport joystick navigation and Execute-based launch, with a classic VBCC build. Distinct lightweight interface from full iGame.

decisions.title: Glider — independent Glider 4 C++ rewrite
decisions.reason: From-scratch C++20 recreation of John Calhoun's Macintosh Glider 4 with original house-file compatibility and a separate house editor. Implements its own physics/game state, object behavior, binary house reader/writer, SDL renderer and audio. Independent of Aerofoil, which ports Glider PRO.

decisions.title: TheEscape — RISC OS BBC BASIC game
decisions.reason: Original RISC OS Star Trek-themed spaceship/shooter learning project. Tokenised BASIC application files are accompanied by readable plain-text .bas equivalents with ship movement, shields, phasers, enemies, projectiles, sprites and audio.

decisions.title: amipkg — AmigaOS package manager
decisions.reason: Native AmigaOS package manager with CLI, GadTools and MUI interfaces. Portable C core implements signed catalog verification, dependency resolution, recipes and receipts; Amiga layer implements HTTP/AmiSSL downloads and DOS-library install/remove operations. Independent package-manager component extracted from Amiga Imager.

decisions.title: GameX-Gels — native Amiga graphics library
decisions.reason: ANSI C AmigaOS game-development library implementing screens, Copper synchronization, IFF loading, icons and graphics.library-compatible BOB/VSprites with custom accelerated blitter/mask operations. Substantial reusable graphics subsystem rather than the author's skeletal Blaster game.

decisions.title: Nuclear Reaction — C64 implementation
decisions.reason: Native Commodore 64 implementation based on Amiga Nuclear Reaction. C/6502 assembly provides atom-placement chain reactions, two-player turns, winner detection, AI search, PETSCII rendering, SID sound and hardware input. Substantial independent game implementation.

decisions.title: Teenage Queen — Mega Drive port
decisions.reason: Pascal/Foxy native Mega Drive assembly port of ERE's Atari ST poker game. README explicitly credits Foxy's reverse engineering; source implements card/deal evaluation, betting turns, opponent decisions and Sega display/input/audio routines.

decisions.title: Flappy Bird — native monochrome Atari ST
decisions.reason: Educational native Atari ST C/assembly Flappy Bird recreation with complete staged implementations. Latest stage includes game state/collision, monochrome raster routines, menu, score, PSG effects/music, IKBD input, vectors and VBL timing. Distinct from deferred BBC/Electron binary-only Flappy Bird release.

decisions.title: Wondersnake — WonderSwan Color snake game
decisions.reason: Tomasz Słanina’s 2007 native WonderSwan Color Snake game, published with its complete 80186-compatible assembly, level data and a C COM-to-cartridge converter. This is original homebrew rather than recovered commercial source.

decisions.title: PARAMECIUM — Vectrex orbit-and-jump game
decisions.reason: Original Vectrex homebrew by Brian Jones. A single-cell organism orbits nuclei, jumps between them and tethers the board while avoiding biological hazards; the repository exposes the native game implementation rather than wrapping an old ROM.

decisions.title: Zombie Near — MSX and ColecoVision source release
decisions.reason: Oscar Toledo’s original Zombie Near action game source release, preserving dated development snapshots and native platform versions. The ColecoVision game contains its own Z80 game loop, enemy AI, maps and SN76489 music rather than emulating an existing game.

decisions.title: Stargunner — Neo Geo Pocket Color shooter
decisions.reason: Native NGPC scrolling-shooter demo built on NGPC Template 2026. Unlike a bare starter template, it contains a substantial distinct shooter implementation, scripted stages, multiple enemy patterns, bosses, graphics and audio.

decisions.title: OVER REV racing engine template — native NGPC road renderer
decisions.reason: A standalone source template extracted from the original OVER REV Neo Geo Pocket Color racer. Promote only the reusable engine/sample in the checked-in ZIP: the full game is distributed as binaries and explicitly has not had its complete source published.

decisions.title: Bad Apple!! for WSwan — native audiovisual demo
decisions.reason: WonderSwan Bad Apple demo with a native banked command-stream/tile video player and interrupt-driven PCM/IMA-ADPCM audio, plus a Java video quantizer. It is native media-player homebrew, not a recovered game executable.

decisions.title: AthenaOS — WonderWitch BIOS and OS reimplementation
decisions.reason: Independent native replacement for the FreyaBIOS/FreyaOS WonderWitch abstraction layer. It aims to make existing freely available WonderWitch software run with third-party WonderSwan cartridges and emulators, with BIOS services, interrupt plumbing and OS/filesystem code.

decisions.title: ECS Extended BASIC — Intellivision interpreter
decisions.reason: Oscar Toledo’s CP1610-native replacement BASIC interpreter for the Intellivision Entertainment Computer System. It implements a full-screen editor, tokenized statements, floating-point expressions, graphics, sound and tape I/O.

decisions.title: IntyBASIC — Intellivision BASIC cross-compiler
decisions.reason: BASIC-to-CP1610-assembly cross-compiler with its own parser, intermediate-code representation, register tracking, peephole optimizer and native runtime prologue/epilogue. Provides a substantial original retro language toolchain rather than only editor support.

decisions.title: inty-midi — MIDI to IntyBASIC music converter
decisions.reason: Haskell MIDI importer and converter that maps instruments, quantizes time and allocates available voices, producing IntyBASIC MUSIC statements or a standalone preview program for Intellivision/ECS.

decisions.title: LibVec — Vectrex assembly routine library
decisions.reason: Pre-alpha collection of reusable 6809 routines/macros for Vectrex vector drawing, timers, scoring, text, raw audio and DS2431 EEPROM. It adapts existing routines and some BIOS calls into macros to trade ROM space for cycles.

decisions.title: HuDK — PC Engine native development kit
decisions.reason: PC Engine ASM/C SDK with native hardware libraries for sprites, video, scrolling, input, interrupts, audio, storage and mathematics, plus desktop graphics/tilemap/VGM tools and runnable source examples.

decisions.title: pcmenc — PSG sample encoder and native replayers
decisions.reason: Extended pcmenc audio conversion toolkit based on Arturo Ragozini/Daniel Vik’s MSX encoder, adding SN76489 targets, packing methods, banking and cycle-budgeted Z80 replay routines. Actual encoder and native players are present.

decisions.title: Phantasy Star Retranslation — disassembly and enhancement source
decisions.reason: Unofficial retranslation/re-localisation of the original Japanese Master System Phantasy Star. The source includes annotated Z80 disassembly, text/graphics reimplementation, grammar-aware multilingual scripts and gameplay/bug-fix patches, not merely released IPS/BPS binaries.

decisions.title: libpressf — portable Fairchild F8 emulation library
decisions.reason: Reusable C89 emulation library for Fairchild F8-family systems, including Channel F. Models the CPU instruction/ROMC machinery and memory, display, beeper, controllers and auxiliary devices; shared by multiple distinct platform frontends.

decisions.title: PC98Bridge — PC-98 serial inspection and file-transfer agent
decisions.reason: Native PC-98 DOS agent plus Windows Python CLI and MCP server for bounded hardware/DOS inspection and file/directory transfer over RS-232C. Substantial command parser, DOS memory/device inspection and streaming transfer code; not a shell or game wrapper.

decisions.title: PC98IMEBridge — Windows IME to PC-98 input bridge
decisions.reason: Windows .NET input window and native FreeDOS(98) resident program transmit committed Japanese input into PC-98 BIOS keyboard queues. Contains serial protocol, TSR hooks, IRQ buffering and a device-driver alternative.

decisions.title: PC98Emu — C# NEC PC-98 emulator
decisions.reason: Reusable NEC PC-9801/PC-9821 emulator implementing V30/x86 instruction execution, machine bus, disk controllers, GDC/GRCG, YM2608 and compatible BIOS/DOS interception in C#. Not tied to one game.

decisions.title: 98Bridge — PC-98 disk image mounter
decisions.reason: Host-side wxPython application with actual D88/FDI/HDI/HDM/raw/NHD parsing, FAT12/FAT16 filesystem access, PC-98 IPL/MBR partition detection, hex viewing and controlled writeback. Reusable preservation and inspection tooling.

decisions.title: UnPKd — PKLite executable unpacking GUI
decisions.reason: Rust/wxDragon GUI for detecting and analysing PKLite-packed DOS executables, with a Rust-port bitstream/Huffman/LZ decoder and experimental MZ output reconstruction. Substantial implementation exists, but executable restoration is incomplete.

decisions.title: Tank — native Pascal DOS tank game
decisions.reason: Complete native DOS tank-combat Pascal program with keyboard/mouse movement, projectiles, collision logic, scores and BGI graphics; original source and data/binary packaging remain available.

decisions.title: Damaniel DOS games and CGA sprite tools
decisions.reason: Shaun Brandt/Holy Meatgoat Software collection of native DOS projects including Damanoid, Move-it Man, LOCGAED CGA sprite editor and a historical Allegro Tetris. Retained as one repository-level collection, not inflated into one row per directory.

decisions.title: DOS Game Engine — Turbo Pascal multimedia engine
decisions.reason: Native Turbo Pascal 7 multimedia/game engine with VGA renderer, widget UI, TMX/PCX/BMP loading, resource manager, XMS, AdLib HSC music, Sound Blaster audio and example XiClone game.

decisions.title: XEngine — native Pascal DOS game toolkit
decisions.reason: Native Pascal/x86 assembly VGA toolkit covering buffered blitting, BMP images, fonts, keyboard/mouse/joystick, Sound Blaster WAV playback, PC speaker, timer and package I/O, with sample chess, snake and Tetris games.

decisions.title: Sadist 2 — original DOS source and English restoration
decisions.reason: Author-released Sadist 2 (2000), sequel to Sadist, with original Polish Turbo Pascal code, 2026 English translation, tools and installer scripts. Graphics, XMS storage, mouse and sound units accompany the main game.

decisions.title: Star Fighter — DIV Games Studio 2 DOS game
decisions.reason: Original 2020 game-jam pseudo-3D space shoot-em-up using vanilla DOS DIV Games Studio 2 and mode-7-style presentation. PRG game source and custom Watcom C++ DLL modules are included.

decisions.title: Cripple Smash — DOS BBS source and browser port
decisions.reason: TypeScript browser reimplementation of Ben Freeman’s 1992 DOS BBS door game, retaining original Turbo Pascal source and ANSI art. Implements game-state flow, combat, progression, saving and terminal presentation without emulating a CPU.

decisions.title: Pascal-Monitor — BESM-6 compiler reconstruction and C++ conversion
decisions.reason: Reconstructs the Pascal compiler included in the Dubna monitor from a recovered object module. Includes disassembly, annotated recovery material, Pascal auxiliaries and a direct C++ translation that emits big-endian BESM-6 object modules.

decisions.title: Monitor-80 — BESM-6 OS source reconstruction
decisions.reason: Reconstructs Kurchatov Institute Monitor-80, derived from Dubna, by disassembly and correlation with surviving Dubna sources. Contains substantial assembly and recovered Fortran overlays plus binary comparison and volume construction tooling.

decisions.title: Pascal-Autocode — first BESM-6 Pascal compiler decompilation
decisions.reason: Recovers Pascal-Autocode version 9 (17 May 1988), descended from the first BESM-6 Pascal compiler begun in 1975. The implementation emits Cyrillic-mnemonic autocode for the BESM-6 assembler and includes editor and formatting tools.

decisions.title: TIRAZH — BESM-6 document printing system decompilation
decisions.reason: Reconstructs TIRAZH, a line-printer document formatting system with rudimentary markup, two-column output, justification and hyphenation. Includes recovered Pascal implementation and decompilation/reassembly scripts.

decisions.title: KADRY — BESM-6 HR database decompilation
decisions.reason: Recovers the KADRY personnel database system as multiple Pascal programs, including main database commands, questionnaire input, service/help, field formats and report generation. README identifies original binary zones on disk image 2148.

decisions.title: Cornwell Smalltalk-80 — custom-bytecode clone
decisions.reason: Richard Cornwell's Smalltalk-80 clone based on the Blue Book, with a simplified/custom VM, C bootstrap compiler, native Smalltalk compiler, object memory, image snapshots and a partly finished graphical interface.

decisions.title: IBM 709 diagnostic program source collection
decisions.reason: Preserves IBM 709 diagnostics covering CPU, indexing, floating point, memory, tape, cards, drums, printer, display and special controls. Includes dated assembly listings, scan images, loader/diagnostic assembler sources and card/tape generation tools.

decisions.title: Xpw — original X11 widget library
decisions.reason: Cornwell's 1990s X Toolkit widget set developed alongside XMS mail, addressing Athena widget limitations through cascaded menus, selection controls, cached 3D drawing and an extensible widget library.

decisions.title: BKUNIX — LSX/Mini-Unix restoration and BK port
decisions.reason: Leonid Broukhis and Serge Vakulenko's Unix for BK-0010/BK-0011M, derived from revived LSX and Mini-Unix V6 sources. Modernizes ancient C, fixes cross-compilers and relocates the kernel into the BK memory map.

decisions.title: Demos Commander — Unix text-mode file manager
decisions.reason: Demos Commander (deco) preserves a two-panel Unix shell file manager with file selection, copying, renaming, viewing, hex viewing and editing. Includes full C implementation, help translations and modern CMake build support.

decisions.title: SNO — Unix V4 Snobol III interpreter modernization
decisions.reason: Modernizes Ken Thompson's SNO compiler/interpreter from the Unix 4 tape. Retains legacy C sources alongside a C++17 implementation and tests, documenting deviations from standard Snobol III.

decisions.title: BLISS-M — portable BLISS cross-compiler
decisions.reason: Matthew Madison's BLISS-M compiler source with parser, macro facility and LLVM backend for the DEC-associated systems language. Repository carries an LLVM 11 update and extensive frontend/backend implementation.

decisions.title: OMU — original 6809 and 68000 Unix-like OS sources
decisions.reason: Preserves Steve Hosgood and Terry Barnaby's early-1980s cut-down Unix-like OMU kernel, originally for a homemade 6809 computer and ported to 68000 with multitasking, hard-disk support and UID/GID handling.

decisions.title: Dunfield Micro-C — preserved compiler and bootstrap cleanup
decisions.reason: Hosts a cleaned-up version of Dave Dunfield's historic Micro-C C-subset compiler, optimizer, preprocessor, libraries and target code generators, aimed at bootstrapping on a modern host.

decisions.title: Rain Panic — Oric Atmos arcade game
decisions.reason: Original native arcade game in which Mr Aldo catches ceiling rain; source implements waves, character animation, hazards, score, music and fast display primitives.

decisions.title: Game of Thrones main theme — Oric music demo
decisions.reason: Chloé Avrillon’s native AY-3-8912 theme adaptation and playback demonstration. Despite repository search description mentioning a game, README and implementation establish a music demo.

decisions.title: Tomzox VIC-20 games — restored 1982–84 source
decisions.reason: T. Zoerner’s own three early VIC-20 games recovered by retyping paper hex dumps, disassembling with dxa, reconstructing labels/comments and repairing code. Keep as one coherent author-restoration collection.

decisions.title: QUIKMAN — VIC-20 tape-source reconstruction
decisions.reason: Robert Hurst reconstructed his hand-coded 1984 maze game from recovered cassette data and a VICMON disassembly, aiming for exact reassembly of the original.

decisions.title: Bomb Jack Revisited — VIC-20 native game
decisions.reason: Author ops’s 1985 VIC-20 game revisited in 2018, with BASIC game administration and interrupt-driven assembly movement/music. Distinct VIC-20 implementation of the arcade theme.

decisions.title: Serpentine — VIC-20 annotated cartridge disassembly
decisions.reason: Annotated disassembly of David Snider’s Serpentine, VIC-20 port by Creative Software, documenting its bitmap-style character rendering and snake/egg/frog systems.

decisions.title: VIC-20 cartridge games — da65/ca65 disassembly collection
decisions.reason: Eleven VIC-20 cartridge games reconstructed with da65 and relabelled for ca65, including relocatable absolute references and split-bank treatment of 16KB titles. Keep as one repository-level disassembly collection.

decisions.title: Timebomb — VIC-20 BASIC-to-assembly remake
decisions.reason: Dave Curran’s 2026 6502 rewrite of Doug Smoak’s July 1983 Compute! BASIC type-in game. Original BASIC listing and magazine scans accompany the implementation.

decisions.title: FiZZ — VIC-20 platform puzzle game
decisions.reason: Native VIC-20 FiZZ platform-puzzle implementation in Turbo Rascal, with modular object physics, control, lasers/floater/fontaine components and JSON level data.

decisions.title: Droid Wars — Dragon32 to CoCo source port
decisions.reason: Marky-D-32’s restored/adapted 6809 two-player droid shooter from the Dragon32 Micropaedia listings in Personal Computer News 27–29 (September 1983), adjusted to CoCo ROM and workspace addresses.

decisions.title: Nite Move — Dragon32 to CoCo source port
decisions.reason: CoCo adaptation of Pat McCabe and Colin Turner’s Dragon User May 1986 knight-move board puzzle, restoring its 6809 assembly and remapping ROM services.

decisions.title: Grand Prix — Dragon32 to CoCo source port
decisions.reason: CoCo2 source port of Brian Cadge’s Dragon User June 1984 one/two-player driving game, with documented ROM-call conversion and named recovered game variables.

decisions.title: XOR — SAM Coupé from-scratch remake
decisions.reason: Howard Price/Tobermory’s 2012 SAM Coupé recreation of Astral/Logotron XOR. Author explicitly says it was started from scratch and nothing was reverse-engineered; predecessor behavior/maps do not imply recovered CPU input.

decisions.title: Fickle — VIC-20 one-button puzzle game
decisions.reason: Malcolm Tyrrell’s original 2011–2012 four-kilobyte real-time puzzle game for unexpanded VIC-20. One-button red/green mood switching controls whether the moving player responds to floor symbols, keys and switches.

decisions.title: BassoonTracker
decisions.reason: A substantial browser-native Amiga-style tracker with independent WebAudio playback, MOD/XM parsing/writing and sample/pattern editors, rather than a hosted original binary.

decisions.title: Gateway
decisions.reason: Native Classic Toolbox PowerPC Mac OS 9 and Win32 gateway/proxy application that supplies modern TLS, mail splicing, Wayback forwarding and tunnels to vintage clients.

decisions.title: Gazette
decisions.reason: Native RSS/Atom reader for PowerPC Mac OS 9 and Windows 95-XP, sharing a portable C engine and using separate native Carbon and Win32 interfaces.

decisions.title: talkip
decisions.reason: New small-footprint TCP/IP and MacIP stack linked into native Macintosh applications, plus a MacTCP-compatible driver, for a 512Ke with System 6 over LocalTalk.

decisions.title: iRunes
decisions.reason: A native C11 Macintosh II media player with DAAP streaming, AIFF/PCM pipeline, classic Toolbox UI and Apple Event scripting, inspired by the iTunes interface rather than recovered iTunes source.

decisions.title: mac-control
decisions.reason: Classic Mac remote-control/development tool consisting of a tiny native System 7 MacTCP agent and Rust CLI/client/MCP server, with screen, input, file, Apple Event and resource-fork operations.

decisions.title: MiniVNC native PowerPC port
decisions.reason: Substantial derivative of Marcio Teixeira MiniVNC adding native PowerPC CFM builds, Retro68 integration, background operation and true-color wire-format fixes, while retaining classic 68k builds.

decisions.title: Disc Image Manager
decisions.reason: A Lazarus/Free Pascal desktop and console utility implementing filesystem-level extraction and mutation for Acorn, Commodore, Amiga, DOS and other retro disk images.

decisions.title: AutoVIDC
decisions.reason: Preserved and maintained ARM relocatable module source controlling VIDC-enhancer oscillator clocks on original Acorn Archimedes RISC OS 2/3 hardware.

decisions.title: arcimage
decisions.reason: Restored 1997-2000 Turbo Pascal-era PC utility that reads and writes physical Archimedes floppy sectors into emulator-compatible disk images, including later F-format improvements.

decisions.title: Prospector in the Mazes of XOR remake
decisions.reason: Independent Java/PlayN implementation of the 1989 Amiga Prospector in the Mazes of XOR, compiled to an HTML5 browser game, with maze rules, renderer, editor and replay handling.

decisions.title: Continuum JS
decisions.reason: A substantial TypeScript/browser port of the released Macintosh Continuum source, translating game physics, shots, collision and rendering into modules rather than executing the original game binary.

decisions.title: Lander GBA
decisions.reason: Bare-metal ARM7TDMI port of reconstructed Archimedes Lander, using a Python source transpiler plus custom GBA display/input/RISC OS SWI replacement assembly.

decisions.title: Glider PRO Windows port
decisions.reason: Direct Windows port of John Calhoun released Glider PRO C source, retaining gameplay/house resources while replacing platform UI/audio/rendering and adding resource extraction tools.

decisions.title: Space — Game Boy asteroid-dodging homebrew
decisions.reason: Native SM83 assembly game by Bot Randomness. Actual source initializes LCD/VRAM/OAM, scrolls the star field, moves multiple asteroids, reads controls and implements spaceship movement. This is an authored homebrew prototype, not recovered commercial source.

decisions.title: Galaxy Patrol — NES homebrew source
decisions.reason: Riley Lannon’s NES assembly project, inspired/guided by the NESdev Galaxy Patrol example. Main source implements a scrolling asteroid/fuel game, game states, player movement and collision handling; an included sound engine remains partial. This is a distinct educational authored version, not a commercial disassembly.

decisions.title: Falling — native NES game source
decisions.reason: Jesse Williams / tragicmuffin’s Falling, a complete authored NES game in NESASM assembly. Source contains title/play/pause/game-over states, difficulty progression, player/obstacle/pickup logic, graphics and music/sound routines.

decisions.title: NES Snake — native assembly game source
decisions.reason: Authored NES Snake game with a modular NESASM implementation. Game code covers persistent direction, movement ticks, pause/game-over states, snake growth and rendering, with CHR, palettes and nametables committed alongside it.

decisions.title: GB-EMU — reusable Game Boy emulator for 3DS
decisions.reason: Reusable C++ Game Boy emulator targeting Nintendo 3DS. Pinned implementation contains SM83 operand/opcode execution, PPU scanline rendering, cartridge memory banking, APU, timer, joypad, ROM browsing and a platform/core separation. It loads general Game Boy ROMs rather than wrapping one game.

decisions.title: TypeScript Game Boy Emulator — reusable browser core
decisions.reason: Robert Louie’s reusable TypeScript Game Boy emulator with independent CPU operation families, GPU/APU/timer/memory/cartridge subsystems and browser UI/examples. Gameboy.runFrame coordinates arbitrary cartridge execution and frame rendering rather than embedding one game.

decisions.title: Mega Tetris — native Genesis game source
decisions.reason: Authored SGDK/C Tetris game for Sega Genesis. Source separates scene management, main menu, music, piece creation/movement/rotation/collision and board rendering, providing substantive gameplay rather than a ROM collection.

decisions.title: Deflection — Genesis game prototype source
decisions.reason: Lucas Falcão and Flavio Freitas’s SGDK class-project source for a medieval two-player projectile-parrying game. Actual code contains arena, knight/wizard sprites, directional controls, attack handler and display/physics routines. Distinct from the tracked 1986 Apple II game sharing the title.

decisions.title: Mega Car Wars — incomplete Genesis racing source
decisions.reason: Native SGDK/C work-in-progress isometric racing/adventure source by realbrucest. Main loop initializes scenario, car/camera and scrolling; car.c implements rotation-derived velocity, sprite direction frames and motion, alongside scenario, pickup, weapon, enemy, HUD and screen modules.

decisions.title: Paper.io Genesis — native SGDK demake
decisions.reason: Authored C/SGDK demake of Paper.io 1 for Genesis, with tile-map territory/path data, human/computer players, movement, claim/fill calculations, score and rendering implemented in src/main.c. Source-level demake rather than game-specific CPU emulation.

decisions.title: Town Quest — Genesis jam-game source
decisions.reason: Sixteen Bits’s JamToday Almería 2019 native Genesis game. SGDK C source implements stage/state transitions, players/enemies, lives, attacks, input, sprite updates and sounds; committed resources and pipeline make it a concrete source project.

decisions.title: Snake Megadrive — native SGDK game source
decisions.reason: Native Sega Mega Drive Snake implementation in C/SGDK. game.c implements directional steering, level speed, edge/wrap checks, food/bonus placement and self-collision; linked-list body, menu, game-over and win modules accompany graphics/audio resources.

decisions.title: DOS Graphics & Audio Engine (16 bits)
decisions.reason: Original modular DOS C89 VGA and Sound Blaster engine, with nine scene demonstrations; useful native retro engine source rather than an emulator wrapper.

decisions.title: HelloWorld-PC98 bare-metal boot demo
decisions.reason: Small but complete annotated PC-98 bootable assembly demonstration: prints text and beeps without DOS; includes a reproducible floppy-image recipe.

decisions.title: E3Dos protected-mode 3D engine
decisions.reason: Author-released historical roughly 11K-line DOS C++ software 3D engine with handwritten inline assembly, clipping, generic rasterization, mipmapping, lighting and terrain demos.

decisions.title: VOPL3 Win98/ME FM and MIDI driver
decisions.reason: Reusable Windows 9x VxD traps OPL/AdLib and MPU-401 I/O from DOS sessions and streams captured writes to user-mode software audio rendering. Own driver/glue implementation with several bundled synthesis backends.

decisions.title: JUDAS Apocalyptic Softwaremixing Soundsystem
decisions.reason: Preservation repository for the historical JUDAS 2.10d DOS sound library: module/sample playback, software mixers and direct Sound Blaster, GUS, AC97 and HDA hardware support.

decisions.title: retro-kit headless DOS/Win32 reverse-engineering toolkit
decisions.reason: Substantial reusable headless Ghidra workflow with an original LE/LX loader, Watcom calling convention specifications, library signatures, PE/DirectX typing and analysis/export/MCP tools.

decisions.title: ADVGEN 1991 adventure compiler and interpreter
decisions.reason: Original 1991 QuickBASIC text-adventure compiler/interpreter re-released by its author, including a small HOUND demonstration and original source/project files. Distinct historical author network.

decisions.title: Xenon (1995) Win16 artillery game
decisions.reason: Complete source/assets of Max and Morgan McGuire's original Windows artillery game, housed in the xenon directory of Morgan's multi-project archive; inspired by Scorched Earth, not the unrelated Bitmap Brothers Xenon shooter.

decisions.title: Colonization for Windows asset and map tools
decisions.reason: Original Python extract/rebuild toolkit for Colonization for Windows (1995) NE resources, custom asset containers, palettes and map previews; reimplements data-format and tile composition behavior without running the game CPU.

decisions.title: Recreational Software Design Game-Maker (1994)
decisions.reason: Author-published original DOS Game-Maker commercial product sources, runtime, editors and bundled sample games. Includes substantial native engine/gameplay implementation and original Borland build graph.

decisions.title: DOS development template with serial GDB stub
decisions.reason: Turnkey native DOS game/demo development environment integrating DJGPP, CMake/Ninja, VS Code and DOSBox-X with a substantive custom remote GDB serial debugging stub.

decisions.title: AMIS — Stacken TOPS-10 Emacs-style editor source
decisions.reason: Preserved Stacken/KTH Emacs-style screen editor, with Pascal editing modules, MACRO-10 terminal/disk support and native link scripts. This is the historical AMIS editor, unrelated to DOS AMIS resident-service specifications.

decisions.title: TOPS-10 ARPANET NCP — Harvard network subsystem source
decisions.reason: SAILDART-recovered TOPS-10 ARPANET NCP, IMP driver, FTP and mail subsystem sources. README credits Robert Sundberg for NCP and Edward Taft for FTP/MAIL; actual IMPSER implementation and native FTP link command are preserved.

decisions.title: cfront 3 — historical AT&T C++ translator restoration
decisions.reason: Historical cfront 3.0.3 C++-to-C implementation with compiler, runtime and libraries, re-ported from the Plan 9 fourth-edition source distribution. Includes actual parser/simplifier/code printer and staged bootstrap scripts.

decisions.title: GPM/CLR — Gardens Point Modula-2 compiler for CLR
decisions.reason: Gardens Point Modula-2 compiler frontend with a CIL emitter, preserving the historical compiler lineage while enabling unmanaged Modula-2 applications on .NET. Source includes semantic traversal, parser, CIL writer and C# runtime modules.

decisions.title: CP/M-86 1.1 — reconstructed kernel and command distribution
decisions.reason: Disassembly-recovered CP/M-86 BIOS/BDOS/CCP with frozen, annotated and experimental source variants, plus reconstructed command sources. Includes local patch mapping and native IBM PC XT/V20 MBC output recipes.

decisions.title: Cirsovius CP/M library — ZSID reconstruction and source restoration
decisions.reason: Restored Werner Cirsovius CP/M source library, including BASELIB and reconstructed Digital Research ZSID debugger. Current maintainer adds Z180 disassembly support and build integration to recovered source originally distributed as a readable website.

decisions.title: Rutgers ELISP — extended-addressing Lisp compiler source
decisions.reason: Charles Hedrick and colleagues’ extended-addressing Lisp preserved from Linköping tape images. Extracted source includes actual Lisp compiler, runtime/assembler modules and native TOPS-20 control scripts.

decisions.title: BBN Logo — PDP-10 interpreter and MIT/NRC variants
decisions.reason: Original BBN Logo assembly source plus MIT modifications and NRC turtle/music adaptations. Actual interpreter source includes storage tables, procedure compilation, turtle terminal support and configuration switches.

decisions.title: PDP-10 XPL — original XCOM compiler and host cross-port
decisions.reason: DECUS PDP-10 XPL/XCOM 4 source and a modern nexcom.xpl cross-compiler port using an XPL-to-C translator. Preserves actual parser tables, scanner and PDP-10 code emitter rather than only compiler documentation.

decisions.title: MIMIC — original PDP-10 minicomputer emulator suite
decisions.reason: Applied Data historical reusable emulator suite written by Bob Supnik, Len Fehskens and Mike McCarthy. Preserved MACRO-10 source contains VM break handling, command editor and machine loaders, alongside minicomputer-specific components.

decisions.title: SUDS — Stanford PDP-10 electronic design system source
decisions.reason: Stanford University Drawing/Design System source corpus from SAILDART and ITS, containing circuit drawing, wirelisting, layout and routing programs. Inspected DRAW display implementation and WL assembly inclusion manifest provide concrete implementation evidence.

decisions.title: KLDCP — KL10 PDP-11 diagnostic console source
decisions.reason: DEC KL10 diagnostic-console program running on the PDP-11 frontend, preserved in MIT and SAIL variants with loader/device modules and console instructions. Reviewed kldcp.20 is PALX-format source assembling actual console modules.

decisions.title: The New Zealand Story Swift translation scope
decisions.reason: The README describes build-time static translation of original 68000 routines into generated Swift with original memory/register/timing behaviour and an Amiga hardware runtime. The M68K interpreter is used for reference/lockstep checks, so this is not described as merely running the game through that interpreter. Generated game code is not committed. Deferred pending review of whether the maintained game-specific translator/runtime qualifies under the current policy, or offers independently reusable tooling; no high-level recovered game-source promotion is made.

decisions.title: Magic Maze
decisions.reason: Author-maintained Ruby/SDL continuation of a 1994 Turbo Pascal maze game. Atari ST is an inspiration reference, not the target.

decisions.title: MIDI Maze browser multiplayer remake
decisions.reason: ASP.NET Core/SignalR remake with a client raycaster and server-authoritative multiplayer. No binary equivalence claimed.

decisions.title: The Dungeons C128
decisions.reason: C128 adaptation of the author's deconstructed C64 version, with disk save/load. README discloses Claude and Copilot assistance.

decisions.title: Vleermuis
decisions.reason: Author-retyped 1989 magazine BASIC game with MSX compatibility. MIT re-release; not independently executed.

decisions.title: Tool Blocks
decisions.reason: Original MSX BASIC homebrew with editable ASCII source and packaged ROM version. Source publication, not a commercial-game decompilation.

decisions.title: Joe Blade DOS
decisions.reason: DOS COM disassembly with TASM-style source, includes and an IDA database. Generic labels and resource dependencies remain.

decisions.title: International Karate DOS
decisions.reason: DOS assembly reconstruction with timer routines, many generic labels and explicit unresolved hard-coded-offset constraints. Modified startup means no byte-exact claim.

decisions.title: AMOK reverse-engineering maps
decisions.reason: Named functions/globals, structure specifications and Ghidra scripts for DOS, Win95 and Saturn builds. This is an analysis corpus, not a completed source port.

decisions.title: 3DO Portfolio OS
decisions.reason: Preserved 1995 Portfolio operating-system source snapshot. Repository attributes the public release to EagleSoft; public availability does not establish an open-source licence.

decisions.title: Retro BIOS source and disassembly collection
decisions.reason: Collection of BIOS sources/listings for Soviet computers and DEC Rainbow. Architecture varies by component; buildability is not claimed for the collection.

decisions.title: ShareFS compatible server
decisions.reason: Native ShareFS protocol implementation for modern hosts serving RISC OS clients. README documents x64/arm64 builds; GPL-3.0-only. Scoped Copilot instructions are present.

decisions.title: Atolm: Panzer Dragoon Saga
decisions.reason: Matching-oriented decompilation with original-era compiler investigation. Not a playable port; compiler-version uncertainty remains. Successor to pds-tools, distinct from asset tooling.

decisions.title: Tokyo Bus Guide
decisions.reason: Partial shiftable reconstruction with SH4 function tests and matching build targets; combines recovered functions with original code and requires user game data.

decisions.title: 3D Pinball: Space Cadet Dreamcast
decisions.reason: Dreamcast/KallistiOS port based on k4zmu2a's SpaceCadetPinball decompilation, with documented text-panel rendering issues.

decisions.title: Mario Kart 64 Dreamcast
decisions.reason: Dreamcast adaptation of n64decomp/mk64 with hardware audio and PowerVR backend. Author reports physical-hardware testing; independent execution not performed.

decisions.title: Pokémon Trading Card Game
decisions.reason: RGBDS disassembly with documented US ROM and patch identities, assembly instructions and CI. Matching is author-documented, not independently verified here.

decisions.title: X / Lunar Chase / Eclipse
decisions.reason: RGBDS disassembly with models, graphics compression and a stripped build. Unreferenced content, script pointers and English/prototype differences remain unfinished.

decisions.title: UNO Game Boy Color
decisions.reason: RGBDS reconstruction with named interrupts, banked assembly, build comparison and remaining baserom INCBIN regions.

decisions.title: Money Idol Exchanger
decisions.reason: Banked Game Boy disassembly generated using mgbdis, with target digest and assembly scaffold. Semantic annotation completeness is not established.

decisions.title: Donkey Kong Country 2
decisions.reason: Banked disassembly with RAM/VRAM maps, structure definitions, compression and audio notes; explicit conventions favour meaningful names and why-comments.

decisions.title: SNES Control Deck Tester
decisions.reason: Disassembly of the SELF TEST WCS diagnostic ROM using the author's SNES ROM Framework; requires original ROM for asset extraction.

decisions.title: Star Fox sound driver
decisions.reason: N-SPC/Kankichi-kun sound-driver reconstruction with named VCMD macros and patch tables, drawing on SDK and Yoshi's Island analysis. Audio CPU, not Super FX game logic.

decisions.title: Ganbare Goemon 3
decisions.reason: Work-in-progress Asar reconstruction of v1.0; original ROM required and revisions 1/2 explicitly unsupported. SHA1 comparison target supplied.

decisions.title: EarthBound / Mother 2
decisions.reason: ca65/spcasm source with US retail, localisation prototype and Japanese configurations. C decompilation is future work, not present completion.

decisions.title: Hitman: Codename 47
decisions.reason: Inactive partial reconstruction of the GOG release. Several small modules complete by author report while major engine/game modules remain incomplete; not byte-accurate.

decisions.title: OpenBarnyard
decisions.reason: Barnyard and Toshi 2.0 engine decompilation with Windows build instructions, engine library, SDK and developer tools.

decisions.title: Bounce Tales
decisions.reason: Readable Java reconstruction with extracted-resource tooling and Jademula Windows layer. Explicitly targets behaviour rather than identical bytecode.

decisions.title: Mega Man Zero 3
decisions.reason: Japanese-version reconstruction with C sources, assembly portions, linker scripts and graphics/audio build pipeline. Supplied ROM identity does not establish completion.

decisions.title: Apple IIc ROM 3
decisions.reason: SourceGen banked-ROM analysis focused on SmartPort extraction for Mega IIe, with symbol files and linked HTML listings. Use original author repository, not the fadden copy.

decisions.title: CPC Quest
decisions.reason: Native CPCTelera game source with input, collision, turn/map and music systems. Main code credits Antonio Corpas Cuenca and LGPLv3-or-later.

decisions.title: Kaypro D.COM
decisions.reason: Commented NASM reconstruction of a 3552-byte directory utility with DOS/BIOS simulation fixtures. Kaypro provenance is described as believed, not certain.

decisions.title: 98imgtools

decisions.title: LibreROM

decisions.title: Super Disc BIOS

decisions.title: Arcana SNES disassembly

decisions.title: Ms. Pac-Man SNES disassembly

decisions.title: Star Rider arcade notes
decisions.reason: Substantive laserdisc-game research on sprite pages, palette, phrases and memory layouts, with image-bank reconstruction assembly. Not a complete game-code restoration.

decisions.title: Power Drift arcade and Saturn analysis

decisions.title: Zeal 8-bit OS

decisions.title: Star Raiders source modifications

decisions.title: Plumbers Don't Wear Ties enhanced reconstruction

decisions.title: AmigaOS libraries — mixed C reconstruction and binary-preserving corpus

decisions.title: dubcrt — C64 cartridge analysis and extraction tools

decisions.title: Hyper Sports 2 — MSX disassembly
decisions.reason: Interrupt-driven three-event game, VRAM helpers and inline dispatch tables documented in address-anchored annotations. Upstream reports byte-exact 16 KB reconstruction with a user-supplied ROM; no independent build or completeness verification performed.

decisions.title: Hyper Sports 1 — MSX disassembly
decisions.reason: Address-anchored analysis distinguishes event table order from text order and documents interrupt, state and drawing systems. Upstream reports byte-exact 16 KB reconstruction with a user-supplied ROM; no independent build or completeness verification performed.

decisions.title: Cabbage Patch Kids — MSX disassembly
decisions.reason: Semantic annotations cover the interrupt-driven state machine, controllers, dispatch tables and graphics scripts. Upstream reports byte-exact 16 KB reconstruction with a user-supplied ROM; no independent build or completeness verification performed.

decisions.title: Konami's Tennis — MSX disassembly
decisions.reason: Annotations cover delayed anti-copy ROM writes, menu streams and VDP layout; sampled annotation contains malformed-looking text, so build correctness is not assumed. decisions.title: Konami's Billiards — MSX disassembly
decisions.reason: Semantic annotations identify interrupt scheduling, inline dispatch and two graphics interpreters. Upstream reports byte-exact 16 KB reconstruction with a user-supplied ROM; no independent build or completeness verification performed.

decisions.title: Nibbli — ColecoVision source
decisions.reason: Native homebrew source with game logic, graphics and music resources. README requires its compatible SDCC version and batch build scripts; bundled compiler binaries were not executed.

decisions.title: Star Eater — ColecoVision source
decisions.reason: Z80 main program and separate music/sprite source for ColecoVision. Sparse README is supplemented by source inspection; no runtime or build validation.

decisions.title: Macintosh SE/30 video declaration ROM disassembly
decisions.reason: Assembly for declaration ROM, primary initialization, video driver and Easter egg. Author describes it as a codebase for explaining declaration ROMs, not a complete system ROM reconstruction.

decisions.title: Mac ROM Atlas — 68k ROM research workspace

decisions.title: Saturn 480P mode demo — C decompilation
decisions.reason: Charles MacDonald demo reconstruction with video-register definitions and Jo Engine build. Author reports emulator/hardware behaviour and cable-specific limitations; those claims were not independently tested.

decisions.title: Manatee — Dreamcast AICA sound-driver reconstruction
decisions.reason: Logical C reconstruction and Ghidra annotations for the Katana sound driver, pinned to Soul Calibur's reference build. Source exposes MIDI-ring behaviour and uncertainty notes. Explicitly non-byte-matching; ARM audio CPU must not be misclassified as the console's SH-4 host.

decisions.title: New Yokosuka — Shenmue world reconstruction and asset tools
decisions.reason: Browser recreation using decoded original world/model/animation data and a Go multiplayer server. Story progression and broader original behaviour remain incomplete. Arcade cabinets use EmulatorJS, but core world recreation is separate native application logic, not a game-specific emulator wrapper.

decisions.title: Z80 state-tracking decompiler
decisions.reason: Substantive JavaScript decoder/decompiler with state/context tracking, data walkers and Spectrum tape research. It is an experimental analysis tool; no IDA-equivalence or complete decompilation claim inferred.

decisions.title: SNES CIC research and SuperCIC source archive
decisions.reason: Preservation archive of Segher's CIC analysis and SuperCIC key/lock implementations. Source identifies PIC16F630/676 targets and upstream authors. This is an attributed archive, not newly authored research or a 65C816 program.

decisions.title: Dr. Mario — NES disassembly
decisions.reason: ASM6f source targeting Japan/USA Rev A, with named RAM/constants, game data and PRG modules. Sampled constants describe pill, virus and multiplayer mechanics; build not independently run.

decisions.title: International Superstar Soccer Deluxe — SNES disassembly
decisions.reason: USA-version source using the author's SNES ROM Framework. Includes named game RAM, routines and asset extraction; requires a user-supplied clean ROM. No independent rebuild.

decisions.title: Tototek SUPER-FLASH multi-game menu disassembly
decisions.reason: Traced and rewritten flash-cart menu using bass v14. Source notes incomplete commenting, and README says relocation would be needed for original byte layout; functional-equivalence claims do not establish byte matching.

decisions.title: Sanco 800x CP/M BIOS, loader and utilities
decisions.reason: Reconstructed CP/M loader and BIOS with commented machine-specific utilities. README explicitly limits operating-system disassembly to loader/BIOS, not the entire CCP/BDOS. Build and consistency targets exist but were not executed.

decisions.title: Intellivision generated listings
decisions.reason: README describes bulk dis1600 output with inferred labels and some disabled analysis. Do not equate 178 raw listings with semantically recovered projects; review meaningful annotations before promotion.

decisions.title: Spudster obsolete source
decisions.reason: README explicitly says not to use this source and points to gauze/Spudster-s-Revenge as final version. Current-upstream review remains open.

decisions.title: P-Touch hardware study

decisions.reason: Z180 card firmware disassembly alongside 65C816/C host-side API/library, conversion helpers and protocol documentation. Do not conflate the card CPU with the host IIGS processor; semantic coverage varies across the generated listing.

decisions.title: Nick Andrew's recovered TRS-80 software
decisions.reason: Author's recovered 1981-1990 corpus includes utilities, BBS, games, languages and experimental filesystem/OS code. Kept at repository root rather than arbitrary subprojects. Author distinguishes successful assembly from wider runtime testing still to do.

decisions.title: Color Max Deluxe — Color Computer 3 source
decisions.reason: Original 1987 graphics application source released by its authors for historical study. Assembly is stored in .TXT files. License is CC BY-NC-ND; availability does not imply unrestricted derivative-use permission.

decisions.title: ED-IT — TRS-80 Model 4 editor source
decisions.reason: Mark Reed editor sources covering commands, keyboard, display, disks, menus and printing. Main source identifies version 1.2 while README describes additions in 1.1; do not treat documentation version as current program version.

decisions.title: Alleyway — Game Boy annotated disassembly
decisions.reason: WIP annotated RGBDS source with named ball physics, brick and game-loop routines. README reports roughly 200 named functions and remaining unnamed data; no global completeness or byte-matching inference.

decisions.title: HAM Game Boy Advance library — partial decompilation

decisions.reason: 6502 game and music port with headless Spectrum/jsbeeb comparison harnesses. README supersedes the repository's stale music-only description. Upstream notes slower sliding scroll and provisional colours; requires sideways RAM or Master. Claude credited explicitly.

decisions.title: Chuckie Egg 2 — BBC Micro port
decisions.reason: 6502 port with original-code comparisons, room streaming for stock Model B and sideways-RAM edition. Sampled collision code explains a colour-dependent blind spot. decisions.title: Sega CD US BIOS 2.00w — disassembly

decisions.title: IDA Neo Geo loader

decisions.title: Motorola 68000 round-trip disassembler

decisions.title: CUBIX — 6809 SBC operating-system ports

decisions.title: 6809 Playground OS and monitor

decisions.title: MSC 8004 monitor-debugger — recovered source

decisions.title: Syndicate — Watcom C matching decompilation
decisions.reason: Partial function-by-function matching reconstruction with period Watcom tooling and separate decoded-assembly routines. decisions.title: FAT32 FST private source

decisions.title: Indigo Unreal adaptation

decisions.title: Macintosh Slot Manager ROM tools

decisions.title: Lord of the Sword — Master System disassembly

decisions.reason: C driver implementation with PS1 libspu transfer callbacks, instrument and sequencer structures. Early source research; no independently verified matching or runtime completeness.

decisions.title: boom — BBC Micro portal engine
decisions.reason: Native 6502 portal-rendering code, map/display buffers and support tooling. Sparse README supplemented with source inspection; not a completed game or a desktop Doom engine.

decisions.title: TCH board emulation and disassembly research
decisions.reason: Substantive board-family analysis and MAME driver repairs, but its primary delivered restoration is emulation. Retain in audit backlog rather than promoting as a native source port; separately review the reusable disassembly output.

decisions.title: BBC portal-engine editor skeleton
decisions.reason: Inspected add_vertex command has empty apply and undo bodies. Engine boom is promoted, but the editor needs more implementation evidence before classification as a usable tool.

decisions.title: 4-Ward: Born To Raise The Hell — Amiga rebuild
decisions.reason: Packed/unpacked disassemblies, Imploder unpacker, extracted assets and fixed rebuild. Original-byte source and bug-fixed executable are distinct; upstream reports A500/A600 testing, not independently repeated.

decisions.title: Divina: High Tension Never Born — Amiga rebuild
decisions.reason: Depacker, unpacked listing and relocatable intro rebuild with compatibility fixes. Fixed rebuild must not be conflated with byte-identical original; historical display/audio behaviour documented.

decisions.title: PAWS/Quill to DAAD source converter
decisions.reason: UNPAWS-derived snapshot extractor producing DSF source for DAAD Reborn Compiler. Output needs manual merge with DAAD start template and vocabulary review; not original comments/defines recovery.

decisions.title: Applesoft BASIC decompiler and variable inspector
decisions.reason: Tokenized BASIC detokenizer and variable-table extractor for raw Apple II memory dumps. Produces original-ish text, not lost comments or arbitrary machine-code decompilation.

decisions.title: Apple UniDisk 3.5 / Liron firmware disassembly
decisions.reason: Partial drive/interface firmware reverse engineering with SmartPort/ProDOS status names and assembly source. Do not equate partially annotated firmware with complete understanding.

decisions.title: Infocom Apple II ZIP/EZIP/XZIP interpreter disassembly
decisions.reason: Partially reversed Z-machine interpreters for multiple historical versions using Macro Assembler AS. Version support is explicit and some revisions remain unsupported; this is interpreter source, not all adventure game data.

decisions.title: Apple 3.5 Controller firmware disassembly
decisions.reason: Partial 341-0438A firmware listing with 65C02 declaration and named host-ROM/memory state. Distinct controller from the Liron/UniDisk project.

decisions.title: Apple III Apple II-emulation disk analysis
decisions.reason: Partial historical Apple II emulation-disk disassembly for Apple III, including boot/configuration setup and ROM-image layout. System compatibility software, not a game-specific emulation port.

decisions.title: Snowscape — Archimedes terrain engine
decisions.reason: Midwinter-inspired C89/ARM terrain engine; sampled terrain code references original Amiga calculations. An exploratory Archimedes interpretation, not an official Midwinter port or verified full game.

decisions.title: ACE BASIC — Linux-hosted Amiga compiler
decisions.reason: Linux cross-build adaptation of David Benn ACE source with variable-assignment parser and acecc driver. Requires vasm/vlink; distinct host adaptation, not a new BASIC language claim.

decisions.title: Hunkster — Amiga data-object generator
decisions.reason: Windows utility writing HUNK data/external-symbol records for vbcc/Free Pascal linking. Narrow Amiga-oriented predecessor to the separately reviewed multi-format rtbinobj.

decisions.title: CopperSharp68k — CIL-to-68k compiler
decisions.reason: Closed-world ahead-of-time compiler with 68k backend, HUNK/ROM output and Amiga bindings. Supports a bounded .NET profile; planned MorphOS/PPC target and unrestricted .NET compatibility are not promoted.

decisions.title: Atari ST PRG linker
decisions.reason: Small linker with GEMDOS header/relocation output written in Lisp. README lists relocation/alignment checks and general formats as unfinished; not a mature universal linker.

decisions.title: Swabby — Game Gear source
decisions.reason: Author-recovered homebrew game source with level setup, VRAM initialization, assets and PSG library. No independent build/playability test.

decisions.title: furSPC — Furnace SNES sound driver
decisions.reason: WIP SPC700 driver and module converter. Only specified macros/effects supported; BRR sample conversion and non-linear pitch restrictions remain explicit.

decisions.title: Flicky — Mega Drive annotated disassembly
decisions.reason: Older independent annotated listing identifies RAM-executed main code and assembler/debugger constraints. Distinct repository from the separately tracked Flicky reconstruction; no matching or completeness measurement performed.

decisions.title: Toy Story — Mega Drive disassembly tooling
decisions.reason: ROM-driven tracer/generator and evidence modules; game-derived code is generated locally, not committed. Facts separate USA and EU layouts; progress does not imply full semantics or native port.

decisions.title: Dragon Ball Z: Buyuu Retsuden — disassembly tooling
decisions.reason: French-release tracer, source generator, ROM functional map and evidence-backed facts. Original ROM required; hardware-measured facts distinguished from static guesses, with regional addresses not interchangeable.

decisions.title: Pokémon Yellow — disassembly
decisions.reason: Structured battle/audio/map source with retail/debug build targets. Upstream listed hashes are targets, not an independent build result from this pass.

decisions.title: Zelda Oracle of Ages/Seasons — disassembly
decisions.reason: Documented US-version source and LynnaLab integration. JP/EU unsupported; RAM-address relocation less tested and some hardcoded addresses remain despite ROM-relocation support.

decisions.title: cbmasm — mixed 6502/Z80 assembler
decisions.reason: Allows CPU switching within a source file for C128-oriented code and PRG output. README explicitly warns WIP may not compile out of the box; undocumented 6510 opcodes unsupported.

decisions.title: LS-DOS 6.3.1 Level N — Model II source
